explanation.en:
How it works:
A conditional sentence with "if" sets up a condition and its result. The First Conditional (if + present, will + base verb) covers real or likely situations. The Second Conditional (if + past, would + base verb) handles hypothetical or unlikely ones. In song lyrics, conditionals create emotional stakes — "what if this happens?"

Example from this song:
"If I lose it all" — a real conditional presenting a plausible, terrifying scenario. The singer contemplates the possibility of losing everything and what emotional state would follow.

More examples:
• "If the walls fall, we fall with them" — real condition tied to a consequence
• "If I had wings, I would fly away" — hypothetical (Second Conditional)
• "If you leave, nothing remains" — condition with devastating result

grammar_points.name: Present Continuous for dramatic effect (-ing forms)

explanation.en:
How it works:
The Present Continuous tense (am/is/are + verb-ing) normally describes actions happening right now. In song lyrics, -ing forms are used without the auxiliary verb ("burning" instead of "I am burning") to create immediacy, urgency, and visceral tension. This stripped-down style makes the listener feel they are inside the moment.

Example from this song:
"I'm tearless, I'm fearless, I'm burning" — the -ing form "burning" creates a sense of ongoing, present intensity. "Coming for you" — the progressive creates approaching danger.

More examples:
• "Still wandering in the deep mist" — ongoing, atmospheric image
• "The world is crumbling" — present continuous for dramatic tension
• "Hearts are breaking, walls are shaking" — parallel -ing forms for rhythm and urgency

grammar_points.name: "All I ever wanted" — emphatic past desire

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern "All I ever wanted to do was..." is an emphatic structure that distills someone's deepest, most genuine desire into a single statement. "All" means "the only thing," "ever" spans their entire life, and "wanted" places it in the past. Together, it creates a powerful gap between pure intention and tragic outcome — "I only wanted one simple thing, and yet..."

Example from this song:
"All I ever wanted to do was do right things. I never wanted to be the king." — The singer (from Eren's perspective) emphasizes that their original desire was simple and noble, but fate twisted it into something monstrous.

More examples:
• "All I ever wanted was to be free" — simple desire, complex reality
• "All she ever wanted was to be loved" — poignant gap between wish and outcome
• "All we ever wanted was peace" — collective desire contrasted with war

grammar_points.name: German song - no Japanese grammar

explanation.en:
This song is entirely in German. The vocabulary section provides Japanese equivalents of key German words for educational cross-referencing. Attack on Titan frequently uses German in its soundtrack to evoke the European medieval atmosphere of the walled cities.

While no Japanese grammar structures appear in the lyrics, the vocabulary maps German concepts like Mauer (壁, kabe, "wall"), Schicksal (運命, unmei, "fate"), and Flugel (翼, tsubasa, "wings") to their Japanese counterparts.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: N/A

grammar_points.name: 〜まで (made - until)

explanation.en:
The Japanese equivalent of German "bis" (until) as used in this song. まで (made) marks a temporal or spatial endpoint, meaning "until" or "up to."

How it works:
Place まで (made) after a noun (time/place) or a verb in dictionary form. It sets the boundary or limit.

Example from this song:
"Wir werden kampfen bis dieser heisse Wind unsere Flugel nimmt" → 風が翼を奪うまで戦う (kaze ga tsubasa o ubau made tatakau, "fight until the wind takes our wings")

More examples:
- 5時まで待つ (goji made matsu, "wait until 5 o'clock")
- 東京まで行く (toukyou made iku, "go up to Tokyo")
- 終わるまで頑張る (owaru made ganbaru, "keep trying until it's over")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 戦う (tatakau) + まで (made) → 風が翼を奪うまで戦う (kaze ga tsubasa o ubau made tatakau, "fight until the wind takes our wings")

grammar_points.name: 〜ことができる (koto ga dekiru - can do)

explanation.en:
The Japanese equivalent of German "kann" (can) as used in this song. This pattern expresses ability or possibility.

How it works:
Take the dictionary form of a verb, add こと (koto) + が (ga) + できる (dekiru). Together: "can do [verb]."

Example from this song:
"Sogar ein kleiner Vogel kann frei uber die Mauer fliegen" → 飛ぶことができる (tobu koto ga dekiru, "can fly")

More examples:
- 読むことができる (yomu koto ga dekiru, "can read")
- ピアノを弾くことができます (piano o hiku koto ga dekimasu, "I can play the piano")
- 一人で料理することができた (hitori de ryouri suru koto ga dekita, "I was able to cook by myself")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 飛ぶ (tobu) → 飛ぶことができる (tobu koto ga dekiru, "can fly")

explanation.en:
A conditional meaning "if." Used when the speaker takes a hypothetical situation as a premise, then states what would follow.

How it works:
Attach なら (nara) after the plain form of a verb, adjective, or noun.

Example from this song:
あの頃に戻れるなら (ano koro ni modoreru nara, "If we could return to those days")

More examples:
- 時間があるなら手伝って (jikan ga aru nara tetsudatte, "If you have time, help me")
- 安いなら買う (yasui nara kau, "If it’s cheap, I’ll buy it")
- 行くなら早く行こう (iku nara hayaku ikou, "If we’re going, let’s go quickly")

Creates a comparison: "like" or "as if." It connects a descriptive phrase to a noun, saying one thing resembles another.

How it works:
Place ような (you na) after a noun + の (no), or after a verb in dictionary form.

Example from this song:
ガラス細工のような思い出の破片 (garasu saiku no you na omoide no hahen, "Fragments of memories like glasswork")

More examples:
- 夢のような話 (yume no you na hanashi, "A story like a dream")
- 子供のように笑う (kodomo no you ni warau, "Laugh like a child")
- 嵐のような日々 (arashi no you na hibi, "Days like a storm")

Indicates a sequence: "after doing [X], then [Y]." The first action must be completed before the second begins.

How it works:
Take the て-form (te-form) of a verb and add から (kara).

Example from this song:
失くしてから気づく (nakushite kara kidzuku, "You realize after losing")

More examples:
- ご飯を食べてから出かける (gohan o tabete kara dekakeru, "Go out after eating")
- 日本に来てから日本語を勉強した (nihon ni kite kara nihongo o benkyou shita, "Studied Japanese after coming to Japan")
- 話してから決めよう (hanashite kara kimeyou, "Decide after talking")

An emphatic particle meaning "even." It highlights an extreme or unexpected example, implying "if even [this] is the case, then certainly everything else too."

How it works:
Place さえ (sae) after a noun, or after verb + ことさえ. Often paired with も (mo) for extra emphasis.

Example from this song:
夢見ることさえも叶わず (yumemiru koto sae mo kanawazu, "Unable to even dream")

More examples:
- 名前さえ知らない (namae sae shiranai, "I don’t even know their name")
- 水さえあれば生きられる (mizu sae areba ikirareru, "If we just have water, we can survive")
- 子供でさえ分かる (kodomo de sae wakaru, "Even a child can understand")

Defines or names something. It connects a description or name to a noun, meaning "called," "known as," or "the thing that is."

How it works:
Place という (to iu) between a name/description and the noun it modifies.

Example from this song:
現実という鎖 (genjitsu to iu kusari, "The chains called reality")

More examples:
- 東京という街 (toukyou to iu machi, "The city called Tokyo")
- 愛という名の病 (ai to iu na no yamai, "An illness called love")
- 自由という概念 (jiyuu to iu gainen, "The concept known as freedom")

grammar_points.name: 〜てもいい (temo ii - it’s okay to)

explanation.en:
Expresses permission or willingness: "it’s okay to [do X]" or "I don’t mind if [X]." The speaker accepts the action described.

How it works:
Take the て-form (te-form) of a verb and add もいい (mo ii).

Example from this song:
すべてを犠牲にしてもいい (subete o gisei ni shite mo ii, "It’s fine to sacrifice everything")

More examples:
- ここに座ってもいいですか (koko ni suwatte mo ii desu ka, "May I sit here?")
- 食べてもいいよ (tabete mo ii yo, "You can eat it")
- 遅れてもいいから来て (okurete mo ii kara kite, "It’s okay to be late, just come")

grammar_points.name: 〜のでしょう (no deshou: I suppose; probably)

explanation.en:
How it works: のでしょう (no deshou) combines the explanatory の (no) with でしょう (deshou, 'probably/I suppose'). It expresses a polite guess or supposition with an explanatory tone.

Example from this song: 解いたのでしょう (toita no deshou) = 'I suppose (you) solved it' — from 解く (toku, 'to solve') → 解いた (toita, past) + のでしょう (no deshou)

More examples:
• 疲れたのでしょう (tsukareta no deshou, 'I suppose you're tired') — from 疲れる (tsukareru, 'to get tired')
• 知らなかったのでしょう (shiranakatta no deshou, 'I suppose they didn't know')
• 難しいのでしょう (muzukashii no deshou, 'it's probably difficult')

Note: でしょう alone = 'probably.' のでしょう = 'probably (and here's why I think so).' The の adds explanatory nuance. Casual form: のだろう (no darou) / んだろう (n darou).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 解く (toku, 'to solve') → 解いた (toita, 'solved') + のでしょう (no deshou, 'I suppose') → 解いたのでしょう (toita no deshou, 'I suppose you solved it')

grammar_points.name: 〜なんかじゃない (nanka janai: it's not something like)

explanation.en:
How it works: なんか (nanka) means 'something like' (dismissive), and じゃない (ja nai) means 'is not.' Together, なんかじゃない denies that something is trivial or dismissible.

Example from this song: 勇気なんかじゃない (yuuki nanka ja nai) = 'it's not something trivial like courage' — from 勇気 (yuuki, 'courage'). The speaker insists it's something deeper than mere courage.

More examples:
• 嘘なんかじゃない (uso nanka ja nai, 'it's not a lie or anything') — defending the truth
• 遊びなんかじゃない (asobi nanka ja nai, 'it's not just playing around') — insisting it's serious
• 弱さなんかじゃない (yowasa nanka ja nai, 'it's not weakness') — rejecting a label

Note: なんか is casual and slightly dismissive. Using なんかじゃない is emphatic denial — 'it's NOT just some...' It shows emotional investment in correcting a misunderstanding.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 勇気 (yuuki, 'courage') + なんか (nanka, 'something like') + じゃない (ja nai, 'is not') → 勇気なんかじゃない (yuuki nanka ja nai, 'it's not something trivial like courage')

grammar_points.name: 〜じゃなくたって (janakutatte: even if it's not)

explanation.en:
How it works: じゃなくたって (ja nakutatte) is the casual concessive form of ではなくても (de wa nakutemo), meaning 'even if it's not.' たって is a casual version of ても.

Example from this song: 虹の彼方じゃなくたって (niji no kanata ja nakutatte) = 'even if it's not beyond the rainbow' — the speaker says the destination doesn't have to be somewhere magical

More examples:
• 完璧じゃなくたっていい (kanpeki ja nakutatte ii, 'it doesn't have to be perfect')
• 一番じゃなくたって (ichiban ja nakutatte, 'even if you're not number one')
• 大人じゃなくたってわかる (otona ja nakutatte wakaru, 'even kids can understand / even if you're not an adult')

Note: The casual chain: ではなくても → じゃなくても → じゃなくたって. たって is very casual/spoken. This pattern is encouraging — 'even if things aren't ideal, it's still OK.'

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 虹の彼方 (niji no kanata, 'beyond the rainbow') + じゃなくたって (ja nakutatte, 'even if it's not') → 虹の彼方じゃなくたって (niji no kanata ja nakutatte, 'even if it's not beyond the rainbow')

grammar_points.name: 〜だけだ (dake da: it's just that; only)

explanation.en:
How it works: だけだ (dake da) limits the extent of something — 'it was only...' or 'nothing more than...' It downplays or simplifies what happened.

Example from this song: 強がっていただけだ (tsuyogatte ita dake da) = 'I was only putting on a brave face' — from 強がる (tsuyogaru, 'to act tough') → 強がっていた (tsuyogatte ita, 'was acting tough') + だけだ (dake da)

More examples:
• 聞いただけだ (kiita dake da, 'I only asked') — from 聞く (kiku, 'to ask')
• ちょっと疲れただけだ (chotto tsukareta dake da, 'I'm just a little tired')
• 知りたかっただけだ (shiritakatta dake da, 'I just wanted to know')

Note: だけ = 'only/just.' だけだ at the end of a sentence is explanatory — it's saying 'it was nothing more than X.' Very useful for downplaying or explaining away something.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 強がる (tsuyogaru, 'to bluff') → 強がっていた (tsuyogatte ita, 'was bluffing') + だけだ (dake da, 'it's just') → 強がっていただけだ (tsuyogatte ita dake da, 'was only bluffing')

grammar_points.name: 〜てくれる (te kureru: to do for me)

explanation.en:
How it works: Attach くれる (kureru) to a verb's te-form to express that someone does something beneficial for the speaker. It carries a sense of gratitude.

Example from this song: あなたがくれた (anata ga kureta) = 'what you gave me' — from くれる (kureru, 'to give to me') → くれた (kureta, past). Here it stands alone rather than as a compound verb.

More examples:
• 教えてくれた (oshiete kureta, 'taught me') — from 教える (oshieru, 'to teach')
• 助けてくれてありがとう (tasukete kurete arigatou, 'thank you for helping me')
• 信じてくれた (shinjite kureta, 'believed in me') — from 信じる (shinjiru, 'to believe')

Note: くれる means someone gives/does something beneficial TO the speaker. あげる means the speaker gives/does for someone else. This distinction is uniquely Japanese and reflects awareness of social relationships.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: あなた (anata, 'you') + が (ga) + くれた (kureta, 'gave to me') → あなたがくれた (anata ga kureta, 'what you gave me')

translations.en: and a power without limit is born.
translations.es: y nace una fuerza sin límites.
translations.pt-BR: e nasce uma força sem limites.

literal_meaning.en: 'Limit-without strength is-born.' 限りなき is the literary 〜なき form of 限りない ('endless'). The 〜なき is a classical attributive ending.

meaning.en: if (it is the case) (literary なら)

translations.en: If you seek it, then anywhere —
translations.es: Si lo buscas, hasta cualquier lugar —
translations.pt-BR: Se você buscar, então até qualquer lugar —

literal_meaning.en: 'Seek if-it-is, anywhere.' ならば is the literary form of なら — both mean 'if (X) is the case'. どこまでも = 'no matter where'.

meaning.en: unchanging (literary 〜ぬ negative of 変わる)
let's raise it high (volitional of 振りかざす)

translations.en: let's raise high our unchanging bond.
translations.es: alcemos en alto nuestro lazo inalterable.
translations.pt-BR: vamos erguer bem alto nosso vínculo inabalável.

literal_meaning.en: 'Doesn't-change bond raise-up-let's.' 振りかざす specifically means 'to brandish, hold aloft' — like brandishing a banner. The volitional 〜そう rallies action.

meaning.en: clashed against each other (past of ぶつけ合う)

translations.en: The joy of clashing hearts with you in earnest, too,
translations.es: La alegría de chocar los corazones contigo de verdad,
translations.pt-BR: A alegria de entrar de peito aberto e bater coração com você,

literal_meaning.en: 'You with truly heart clashed-mutually joy also.' 〜合う suffix = 'do mutually'. 本気で is an idiomatic 'seriously / for real'.

meaning.en: laughing till we rolled (te-form of 笑い転げる)

translations.en: and the bittersweetness that dried our tears as we rolled with laughter, too —
translations.es: y la melancolía que secó las lágrimas mientras reíamos a carcajadas, también —
translations.pt-BR: e a melancolia que secou as lágrimas enquanto a gente ria sem parar, também —

literal_meaning.en: 'Laugh-roll-and tears dried bittersweetness also.' 笑い転げる ('to laugh till one rolls / collapses') is a vivid compound.

meaning.en: stringing together (te-form of 繋ぎあわせる)

translations.en: stringing them all together, in the wind,
translations.es: juntando todo eso, en medio del viento,
translations.pt-BR: amarrando tudo junto, ao vento,

literal_meaning.en: 'Tie-together wind of inside.' 繋ぎあわせる = 繋ぐ (tie) + 合わせる (combine) — to splice / join. The te-form chains forward.

meaning.en: is fluttering (continuous of はためく)

translations.en: they're fluttering — high, high above.
translations.es: están ondeando — alto, muy alto.
translations.pt-BR: estão flamulando — bem alto, bem alto.

literal_meaning.en: 'Fluttering is [emph], high high.' はためく specifically describes fabric (a flag, sail) snapping in the wind. The repeated 高く mimics rising motion.

cultural_context.en: The image is a flag — likely the Jolly Roger of the Straw Hat Pirates — flying as a banner of all the joys and sorrows from the previous verses, woven together.

translations.en: Why did you give up looking?
translations.es: Why — ¿por qué dejaste de buscar?
translations.pt-BR: Why — por que você desistiu de procurar?

literal_meaning.en: 'Why search thing [obj] gave-up [Q]?' 〜のは a soft, almost confiding question particle. 探すこと turns the verb into a 'thing'.

meaning.en: to keep fighting (闘う + 続ける)

translations.en: Why do you keep fighting alone?
translations.es: Why — ¿por qué sigues luchando solo?
translations.pt-BR: Why — por que continua lutando sozinho?

literal_meaning.en: 'Why alone keep-fighting [Q]?' 闘 uses the kanji of struggle/contest, slightly more elevated than 戦. 〜続ける = 'keep doing'.

meaning.en: braced yourself for (past of 覚悟する)

translations.en: Hey — what kind of future have you braced yourself for?
translations.es: Oye — ¿para qué clase de futuro te has preparado?
translations.pt-BR: Ei — para que tipo de futuro você se preparou?

literal_meaning.en: 'Hey, what-kind-of future braced-yourself [Q]?' 覚悟する = 'to brace oneself / mentally commit' — the verb of warriors and decisions.

meaning.en: did (past of する); 手にする 'to grasp / obtain'

translations.en: Have you grasped the dream already?
translations.es: ¿Ya tienes el sueño en la mano?
translations.pt-BR: Você já tem o sonho na mão?

literal_meaning.en: 'Dream [topic] already hand into did [Q]?' 手にする (literally 'put into hand') = 'to obtain / get hold of'.

translations.en: If you hesitate, then to this world,
translations.es: Si dudas, entonces a este mundo,
translations.pt-BR: Se você titubear, então para este mundo,

literal_meaning.en: 'Hesitate if-it-is, this world to.' Sets up a parallel to v3-4: same grammatical opening, different consequence.

translations.en: let's softly pray — that the dawn will come.
translations.es: recemos suavemente — que rompa el alba.
translations.pt-BR: vamos rezar baixinho — para que o dia amanheça.

literal_meaning.en: 'Softly let's-pray, night [subj] break so-that.' 〜ように at the end of a clause is the 'may it be that' wish form, often used in prayers.

translations.en: Close your eyes, strain your ears,
translations.es: Cierra los ojos, aguza el oído,
translations.pt-BR: Fecha os olhos, apura os ouvidos,

literal_meaning.en: 'Eyes [obj] close-and ears [obj] strain.' 耳を澄ます is an idiom: 'to listen carefully / strain one's ears'. 澄ます literally 'to make clear'.

meaning.en: let's track it down (volitional of 探し出す)

translations.en: let's track down your answer.
translations.es: encontremos tu respuesta.
translations.pt-BR: vamos descobrir a sua resposta.

literal_meaning.en: 'Search-out-let's, you of answer [obj].' 探し出す = 探す + 出す — 'to search and bring out / track down'.

translations.en: At the far end of the wide blue world,
translations.es: Al fin del ancho mundo azul,
translations.pt-BR: Lá no fim do vasto mundo azul,

literal_meaning.en: 'Blue-and wide world of end at.' 青く links to 広い via the adverbial 〜く form — 'blue and wide'. 世界の果て = 'world's end'.

meaning.en: want to aim for (たい-form of 目指す)

translations.en: there's a place I want to head for, with you.
translations.es: hay un lugar al que quiero llegar, contigo.
translations.pt-BR: tem um lugar que eu quero alcançar, com você.

literal_meaning.en: 'You with want-to-aim place [subj] there-is.' 目指したい場所 = 'a place one wants to aim for' — relative clause.

meaning.en: to keep advancing (literary 進む + ゆく)

translations.en: If it's the course we're sailing on,
translations.es: Si es la ruta que estamos siguiendo,
translations.pt-BR: Se for a rota que estamos seguindo,

literal_meaning.en: 'Advance-go sea-route if-it-is.' 航路 (literally 'sailing road') is a nautical word — fittingly evocative for a One Piece OP.

cultural_context.en: 航路 (kourou) is the navigator's word for a planned ocean course. In One Piece, the Grand Line is the famous 航路 the protagonists must navigate using the Log Pose.

meaning.en: had already decided (continuous past of 決める)

translations.en: we'd already decided it long, long ago.
translations.es: ya lo habíamos decidido hace mucho.
translations.pt-BR: já tínhamos decidido há muito tempo.

literal_meaning.en: 'Far long-ago already had-decided.' 〜ていた expresses a past state continuing up to a reference point. 'It was already decided' lands as fated.

translations.en: The day we met and traded words,
translations.es: El día en que te conocí e intercambiamos palabras,
translations.pt-BR: O dia em que te conheci e trocamos palavras,

literal_meaning.en: 'You with meet-and words exchanged that-day of thing.' Long noun phrase: relative clause + that-day-of-things — modifies the predicate in v23.

translations.en: and the things we decided — that we'd make our dreams come true together someday —
translations.es: y las cosas que decidimos — que algún día cumpliríamos los sueños juntos —
translations.pt-BR: e as coisas que decidimos — que um dia realizaríamos nossos sonhos juntos —

literal_meaning.en: 'Someday together dream [obj] make-come-true [quotative] decided thing.' 〜って is casual quotative; 〜って決めた = 'decided that (X)'.

translations.en: like a masterpiece, inside my chest —
translations.es: como una obra maestra, dentro de mi pecho —
translations.pt-BR: como uma obra-prima, dentro do meu peito —

literal_meaning.en: 'Masterpiece like-of, chest of inside.' 名画 = literally 'famous painting'. のように = 'like / in the manner of'.

translations.en: they shine — bright, bright.
translations.es: brillan — fuerte, fuerte.
translations.pt-BR: estão brilhando — forte, forte.

literal_meaning.en: 'Shining-am [emph], strongly strongly.' Mirror of v8 — instead of fluttering high, here memories shine strong.

meaning.en: for the sake of; in order to

translations.en: Cry — to protect what you believe in.
translations.es: Cry — para proteger aquello en lo que crees.
translations.pt-BR: Cry — para proteger aquilo em que você acredita.

literal_meaning.en: 'Cry, believe things protect for-sake-of.' 信じるもの = 'the things one believes in' (relative clause). ために = purpose.

meaning.en: (in a way) like one's true self (自分 + 〜らしく)

translations.en: Cry — so you can laugh as your true self.
translations.es: Cry — para que puedas reír siendo tú mismo.
translations.pt-BR: Cry — para que você possa rir do seu jeito.

literal_meaning.en: 'Cry, self-like-adv laugh for-sake-of.' 〜らしく = 'in a way that befits / true to'. 自分らしく = 'in one's own way'.

meaning.en: to carry on one's back; bear

translations.en: Hey — before you shoulder it all alone,
translations.es: Oye — antes de que cargues con todo solo,
translations.pt-BR: Ei — antes que você carregue tudo sozinho,

literal_meaning.en: 'Hey, all-alone with bear before.' 〜きり as a suffix = 'only (X) and nothing else'. 独りきり = 'utterly alone'.

translations.en: grab this hand of mine.
translations.es: agarra mi mano.
translations.pt-BR: agarra esta minha mão.

literal_meaning.en: 'This hand [obj] grab [emph].' Te-form 掴んで as a request — 'please grab'. The よ adds gentle insistence.

translations.en: Your voice, which still hasn't reached me,
translations.es: Tu voz, que aún no llega hasta mí,
translations.pt-BR: A sua voz, que ainda não chega até mim,

literal_meaning.en: 'Yet doesn't-reach you of voice [subj].' 届かない君の声 = 'a voice from you that doesn't yet reach'.

translations.en: is crushing my powerless chest.
translations.es: me aplasta el pecho impotente.
translations.pt-BR: está esmagando o meu peito impotente.

literal_meaning.en: 'Powerless chest [obj] crushes.' 押しつぶす = 押す (push) + 潰す (smash) — to flatten / crush. 無力 (na-adj) = 'powerless'.

translations.en: Because I'm searching for you,
translations.es: Porque te estoy buscando,
translations.pt-BR: Porque eu estou te procurando,

literal_meaning.en: 'I [topic] you [obj] am-seeking because.' 〜ているから = 'because (I) am (X-ing)' — reasoning for the next clause.

meaning.en: let's keep believing (信じている volitional)

translations.en: let's keep believing in the morning that streams light through.
translations.es: sigamos creyendo en la mañana en que la luz se cuela.
translations.pt-BR: vamos seguir acreditando na manhã em que a luz penetra.

literal_meaning.en: 'Light shine-into morning [obj] keep-believing.' 信じていよう = volitional of 信じている — 'let's stay in the believing state'. 差し込む = light streaming through a window.

translations.en: The road keeps going, without fail —
translations.es: El camino sigue, sin falta —
translations.pt-BR: O caminho continua, com certeza —

literal_meaning.en: 'Road [topic] surely is-continuing [emph].' 必ず + 続いている = 'is unfailingly continuing'.

meaning.en: never seen before (〜たことのない)

translations.en: toward seas we've never seen before.
translations.es: hacia mares que jamás hemos visto.
translations.pt-BR: rumo a mares que nunca vimos.

literal_meaning.en: 'Yet seen-thing-of-not sea toward.' 〜たことのない (the attributive form of 〜たことがない) modifies 海 — 'a sea (that we) have never seen'.

translations.en: There's a place I should return to with you.
translations.es: Hay un lugar al que debo volver contigo.
translations.pt-BR: Tem um lugar para onde devo voltar com você.

literal_meaning.en: 'You with should-return place [subj] there-is.' 〜べき = 'should / ought to'. 還る uses kanji 還 (return-home, more elevated than 帰る).

translations.en: We — for all eternity,
translations.es: Nosotros — eternamente,
translations.pt-BR: Nós — para sempre,

literal_meaning.en: 'We [topic] eternity [adv].' 永遠に attached as adverbial = 'eternally / forever'. The clause hangs into v37.

meaning.en: had decided (continuous past of 決める)

translations.en: we'd already decided that, long ago.
translations.es: ya lo habíamos decidido así, hace mucho.
translations.pt-BR: já havíamos decidido assim há muito tempo.

literal_meaning.en: 'Far long-ago that-way had-decided.' Mirror of v20 with そう ('that way') replacing もう ('already').

grammar_points.name: Literary negative attributives 〜なき / 〜ぬ

explanation.en:
Classical Japanese had two negative endings — 〜ぬ and 〜ず — that survive in modern usage as literary alternatives to 〜ない. When attached attributively (modifying a noun), 〜ぬ feels stately, and 〜なき (a related classical adjective ending) is used for the negation of i-adjectives or for fixed compound expressions.

This song uses both: 限りなき ('boundless' — 限りない in literary form) in 限りなきチカラ, and 変わらぬ ('unchanging' — 変わらない in literary form) in 変わらぬキズナ. Both modify nouns directly with elevated, almost epic register.

For most verbs the form is verb (negative stem) + ぬ: 知らぬ ('not knowing'), 見ぬ ('not seen'), 行かぬ ('not going'). 〜なき attaches to い-stems: 限りない → 限りなき, さえなき, 数なき. Other typical examples: 限りなき愛 ('boundless love'), 変わらぬ友情 ('unchanging friendship'), 動かぬ証拠 ('immovable evidence'), 知らぬ顔 ('a face that doesn't know — feigned ignorance').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (negative stem) + ぬ; i-adj 〜ない → 〜なき (literary attributive)

grammar_points.name: 〜ならば (literary conditional 'if (it is the case)')

explanation.en:
ならば is the literary form of なら, both meaning 'if (X) is the case'. Like なら, it takes an established premise and asks 'if (that) is so, then...'. The longer ならば feels more elevated, fitting song lyrics, formal speech, and old-fashioned dialogue.

This song uses ならば twice in parallel: 求めるならば ('if you seek') and 躊躇うならば ('if you hesitate'), each setting up the verse's conditional reach. Verse 19 uses the shorter なら (進みゆく航路なら).

Other typical examples: 行くならば早く ('if you're going, go quickly'), 信じるならば疑うな ('if you believe, don't doubt'), あなたならば理解できる ('if it's you, you'll understand'), 雨ならば中止 ('cancelled if it rains').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: plain-form predicate + (の)ならば; na-adj/noun + (なら)ば; literary register

grammar_points.name: 〜ために (for the sake of; in order to)

explanation.en:
ために (literally 'for the sake of') attached to a plain-form verb expresses purpose: 'in order to (do X)'. Attached to a noun + の it means 'for the sake of (X)'. Distinct from causal use 〜ため(に) ('because of').

This song uses ために twice in close parallel: 信じるもの守るために ('to protect what you believe in') and 自分らしく笑うために ('to laugh as your true self'). Each frames the song's emotional 'Cry' as purposeful.

Other typical examples: 健康のために運動する ('I exercise for my health'), 君のために頑張る ('I'll do my best for you'), 試験に合格するために勉強する ('I study (in order) to pass the exam'), 平和のために戦う ('to fight for peace').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (plain form) + ために; noun + のために (purpose; not causal)

grammar_points.name: 〜らしく (in the manner of; befitting)

explanation.en:
〜らしい attached to a noun makes a quality-adjective meaning '(in a way) befitting / typical of (X)'. The adverbial form 〜らしく describes an action done in that manner.

This song uses 自分らしく ('in a way befitting yourself / true to yourself') in 自分らしく笑うために. The phrase carries the moral weight of 'authentically' — laughing as you really are, not as others expect.

Distinguish from 〜らしい meaning 'I hear that...' (hearsay). Other typical examples: 男らしく振る舞う ('to act like a man'), 子供らしく遊ぶ ('to play in a childlike way'), あなたらしくない ('that's not like you'), 春らしい一日 ('a springlike day').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: noun + らしい (quality-adj) → adverbial 〜らしく

grammar_points.name: Volitional 〜よう / 〜う (let's...; intent)

explanation.en:
The volitional form expresses 'let's (do)' or the speaker's intent. For Group 1 verbs the final -u shifts to -ō (祈る → 祈ろう, 振りかざす → 振りかざそう). Group 2: -る → -よう (信じている → 信じていよう, 探し出す happens to be Group 1 → 探し出そう). Irregulars: する → しよう, 来る → 来よう.

This song chains volitionals across the chorus: 振りかざそう, 祈ろう, 探し出そう, 信じていよう. Each rallies the listener to share the speaker's resolve — an unbroken chain of 'let's'.

Other typical examples: 一緒に行こう ('let's go together'), 早く帰ろう ('let's head home soon'), 頑張ろう ('let's give it our best'), 信じよう ('let's believe').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: Group 1: -u → -ō; Group 2: -る → -よう; irregular: する → しよう, 来る → 来よう

grammar_points.name: 〜べき (should; ought to)

explanation.en:
〜べき attached to a plain-form verb expresses 'should (do X)' or 'ought to'. It carries moral or logical obligation — stronger than 〜方がいい. The form is classical-derived and slightly formal. する becomes すべき (or するべき).

This song uses 還るべき場所 ('the place I should return to') in 君と還るべき場所がある. The 〜べき turns 還る into a moral imperative: not just 'a place to go back to', but 'a place I'm meant to return to'.

Other typical examples: やるべきこと ('things one should do'), 知るべき真実 ('a truth one should know'), 守るべき約束 ('a promise one should keep'), 言うべきだ ('one should say it'). Negative: 〜べきではない ('shouldn't').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (plain form) + べき; する → すべき (literary) or するべき

grammar_points.name: 〜ても (temo - even if)

explanation.en:
Expresses "even if" — the result does not change regardless of the condition.

How it works:
Take the て-form (te-form) of a verb and add も (mo).

Example from this song:
追いかけても遅く遠く (oikakete mo osoku tooku, "Even if I chase after you, it's too late, too far")

More examples:
- 走っても間に合わない (hashitte mo ma ni awanai, "Even if I run, I won't make it")
- 頑張っても無理だった (ganbatte mo muri datta, "Even if I tried hard, it was impossible")
- お金があっても幸せじゃない (okane ga atte mo shiawase ja nai, "Even with money, you're not happy")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 追いかける (oikakeru) → 追いかけて (oikakete, te-form) → 追いかけても (oikakete mo, "even if I chase")

grammar_points.name: 〜ことも＋なく (koto mo naku - without even)

explanation.en:
Expresses that something does not happen, with emphasis on "not even." It combines こと (koto, "the act of") + も (mo, "even") + なく (naku, "without").

How it works:
Verb dictionary form + ことも + なく. It means "without even [doing X]."

Example from this song:
時が止まることもなく (toki ga tomaru koto mo naku, "Without time ever stopping")

More examples:
- 振り返ることもなく去った (furikaeru koto mo naku satta, "Left without even looking back")
- 休むこともなく働いた (yasumu koto mo naku hataraita, "Worked without even resting")
- 迷うこともなく答えた (mayou koto mo naku kotaeta, "Answered without even hesitating")

Many anime songs mix English and Japanese in the same song. This is called code-switching. English lines often carry universally accessible emotional statements, while Japanese lines add poetic depth and cultural nuance.

How it works:
The songwriter freely alternates between languages, using English for chorus hooks ("Don't you wanna stay with me?") and Japanese for emotional depth (追いかけても遅く遠く, oikakete mo osoku tooku).

Example from this song:
"I'll be waiting for you" alternates with 問いかけに答えはなく (toikake ni kotae wa naku, "There is no answer to my questioning")

This technique is common in SiM, ONE OK ROCK, and many anime soundtrack artists.

grammar_points.name: 〜ぐらいなら (gurai nara - rather than)

explanation.en:
Expresses a strong preference: "rather than doing X (which is undesirable), I would choose Y instead." The speaker considers X so bad that anything else is better.

How it works:
Attach ぐらいなら (gurai nara) after the dictionary form of a verb. The clause that follows states the preferred alternative.

Example from this song:
傷ついた足を休ませるぐらいなら (kizutsuita ashi o yasumaseru gurai nara, "Rather than resting your wounded legs...")

More examples:
- 嘘をつくぐらいなら黙ったほうがいい (uso o tsuku gurai nara damatta hou ga ii, "Rather than lie, it's better to stay silent")
- 諦めるぐらいなら最後まで戦う (akirameru gurai nara saigo made tatakau, "Rather than give up, I'll fight to the end")
- 待つぐらいなら自分で行く (matsu gurai nara jibun de iku, "Rather than wait, I'll go myself")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 休ませる (yasumaseru) + ぐらいなら (gurai nara) → 休ませるぐらいなら (yasumaseru gurai nara, "rather than resting")

grammar_points.name: 〜続ける (tsuzukeru - continue doing)

explanation.en:
An auxiliary verb meaning "to keep doing" or "to continue doing." Attach it to the stem of another verb to express an ongoing, uninterrupted action.

How it works:
Take the masu-stem of a verb (remove ます), then add 続ける (tsuzukeru).

Example from this song:
信じ続けるだけが答えじゃない (shinji tsuzukeru dake ga kotae ja nai, "Just keeping on believing isn't the answer")

More examples:
- 走り続ける (hashiri tsuzukeru, "to keep running")
- 歌い続けた (utai tsuzuketa, "kept singing")
- 彼は努力し続けている (kare wa doryoku shi tsuzukete iru, "He keeps on making effort")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 信じる (shinjiru) → 信じ (shinji, masu-stem) + 続ける (tsuzukeru) → 信じ続ける (shinji tsuzukeru, "keep believing")

grammar_points.name: 〜なければならない (nakereba naranai - must do)

explanation.en:
Expresses obligation: "must do" or "have to do." In this song, it is used in its negative implication: "if you don't do X, Y won't happen."

How it works:
Take the negative form of a verb (ない), replace ない with なければ (nakereba), then add ならない (naranai). It literally means "if [not doing X], it won't do."

Example from this song:
もがき続けなければ始まらない (mogaki tsuzukenakereba hajimaranai, "If you don't keep struggling, nothing begins")

More examples:
- 勉強しなければならない (benkyou shinakereba naranai, "I must study")
- 早く起きなければならない (hayaku okinakereba naranai, "I have to wake up early")
- 薬を飲まなければならない (kusuri o nomanakereba naranai, "I must take medicine")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: もがく (mogaku) → もがき続ける (mogaki tsuzukeru) → もがき続けなければ (mogaki tsuzukenakereba, "if you don't keep struggling")

grammar_points.name: 〜としても (toshitemo - even if)

explanation.en:
A concessive conditional meaning "even if" or "even assuming that." The speaker acknowledges a difficult hypothetical but declares their intention regardless.

How it works:
Attach としても (toshitemo) after the plain form of a verb or adjective + だ (da). The main clause states what the speaker will do despite the condition.

Example from this song:
翳したプライドが間違いだとしても (kazashita puraido ga machigai da toshitemo, "Even if the pride I held up was a mistake")

More examples:
- 失敗したとしても後悔しない (shippai shita toshitemo koukai shinai, "Even if I fail, I won't regret it")
- 雨が降るとしても行く (ame ga furu toshitemo iku, "Even if it rains, I'll go")
- 高いとしても買いたい (takai toshitemo kaitai, "Even if it's expensive, I want to buy it")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 間違いだ (machigai da) + としても (toshitemo) → 間違いだとしても (machigai da toshitemo, "even if it's a mistake")

grammar_points.name: 命令形 (meireikei - imperative form)

explanation.en:
The direct command form of verbs. It is a forceful way to tell someone to do something, commonly used in rallying cries, sports, and passionate lyrics like this song.

How it works:
For godan (u-) verbs: change the final う (u) sound to え (e).
For ichidan (ru-) verbs: replace る (ru) with ろ (ro).

Example from this song:
進め (susume, "Advance!") and 突き破れ (tsukiyabure, "Break through!")

More examples:
- 行け (ike, "Go!")
- 食べろ (tabero, "Eat!")
- 立て (tate, "Stand up!")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 進む (susumu) → 進め (susume, "advance!"), 突き破る (tsukiyaburu) → 突き破れ (tsukiyabure, "break through!")

grammar_points.name: 〜かける (kakeru - about to; on the verge of)

explanation.en:
Attached to a verb stem, かける (kakeru) indicates an action that has started but is not yet complete, or something on the verge of happening. Think of it as "half-done" or "about to."

How it works:
Take the masu-stem of a verb and add かける (kakeru).

Example from this song:
描いてた理想が崩れかけても (egaiteta risou ga kuzure kakete mo, "Even if the ideal I envisioned is about to crumble")

More examples:
- 死にかけた (shinikaketa, "almost died")
- 言いかけてやめた (iikakete yameta, "started to say something but stopped")
- 食べかけのりんご (tabekake no ringo, "a half-eaten apple")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 崩れる (kuzureru) → 崩れ (kuzure, masu-stem) + かける (kakeru) → 崩れかける (kuzurekakeru, "about to crumble")

explanation.en: Group-1 verbs swap the final -u for -ou: なる → なろう ('let's become'), 行く → 行こう. Group-2 verbs use 〜よう: 食べる → 食べよう. Used for proposals to oneself or a group: 'let's do X'.
explanation.es: Verbos del Grupo 1 cambian el -u final por -ou: なる → なろう ('volvámonos'), 行く → 行こう. Grupo 2 usa 〜よう: 食べる → 食べよう. Para propuestas: 'hagamos X'.
explanation.pt-BR: Verbos do Grupo 1 trocam o -u final por -ou: なる → なろう ('vamos ser'), 行く → 行こう. Grupo 2 usa 〜よう: 食べる → 食べよう. Para propostas: 'vamos fazer X'.

explanation.en: The plain imperative is a blunt command. Group-1: change -u to -e (遊ぶ → 遊べ 'play!'). Group-2: add -ろ (食べる → 食べろ 'eat!'). Used in shouted/sung speech, fight scenes, and song lyrics for force; rude in normal conversation.
explanation.es: Imperativo plano = orden directa. Grupo 1: cambia -u por -e (遊ぶ → 遊べ '¡juega!'). Grupo 2: añade -ろ (食べる → 食べろ '¡come!'). Usado en escenas de lucha, gritos, letras; grosero en conversación normal.
explanation.pt-BR: Imperativo simples = ordem direta. Grupo 1: troca -u por -e (遊ぶ → 遊べ 'brinque!'). Grupo 2: adiciona -ろ (食べる → 食べろ 'coma!'). Usado em cena de luta, gritos, letras; grosseiro no dia a dia.

explanation.en: Group-1: -u → -aseru (笑う → 笑わせる 'make laugh'). Group-2: -る → -saseru (咲く is Group-1: 咲かせる 'make bloom'). The causative + imperative (笑わせろ, さかせろ, させろ) is a forceful 'make it happen!' command.
explanation.es: Grupo 1: -u → -aseru (笑う → 笑わせる 'hacer reír'). Grupo 2: -る → -saseru. Causativo + imperativo (笑わせろ, させろ) es una orden enérgica '¡hazlo pasar!'.
explanation.pt-BR: Grupo 1: -u → -aseru (笑う → 笑わせる 'fazer rir'). Grupo 2: -る → -saseru. Causativo + imperativo (笑わせろ, させろ) é um comando forte 'faça acontecer!'.

explanation.en: 〜ちゃう = 〜てしまう ('end up doing / do completely'). The imperative 〜ちゃえ is a punchy 'just do it already!' 笑わせちゃえ = 'just go ahead and make them laugh!'. Often pairs with causative for energetic shounen-style commands.
explanation.es: 〜ちゃう = 〜てしまう ('terminar haciendo / hacer del todo'). El imperativo 〜ちゃえ es un '¡hazlo de una!'. 笑わせちゃえ = '¡venga, hazlos reír!'. Suele combinarse con causativo en comandos shounen.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜ちゃう = 〜てしまう ('acabar fazendo / fazer por completo'). O imperativo 〜ちゃえ é um 'vai logo, faz!'. 笑わせちゃえ = 'vai, faça eles rirem!'. Costuma pareiar com causativo para comandos shounen.

grammar_points.name: 〜場合じゃない (this is no time for X)

explanation.en: Plain form + 場合じゃない literally 'is not the case for X' = 'this is no time to X'. 泣いてる場合じゃない = 'no time to be crying'. Often used to push past hesitation or grief.
explanation.es: Forma simple + 場合じゃない literalmente 'no es caso de X' = 'no es momento de X'. 泣いてる場合じゃない = 'no es momento de llorar'. Empuja a superar la duda.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma simples + 場合じゃない literalmente 'não é caso de X' = 'não é hora de X'. 泣いてる場合じゃない = 'não é hora de chorar'. Empurra para além da hesitação.

explanation.en: Plain form + さ at the end of a sentence is a casual, often masculine, assertive marker — 'you see / it is, you know'. ライバルになるのさ = 'you'll become a rival, you see'. Lighter than よ, more conversational than んだ.
explanation.es: Forma simple + さ al final es un marcador asertivo casual, típicamente masculino — 'sabes / es así'. ライバルになるのさ = 'te vas a volver un rival, sabes'. Más ligero que よ.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma simples + さ no fim da frase é marcador assertivo casual, geralmente masculino — 'sabe / é assim'. ライバルになるのさ = 'vai virar um rival, sabe'. Mais leve que よ.

explanation.en:
This song is entirely in German. It is one of the most iconic emotional pieces in Attack on Titan, reflecting themes of mortality, beauty, and fighting against fate.

The vocabulary section is empty for this track because the German lyrics do not map directly to beginner Japanese grammar. However, key concepts from this song have Japanese equivalents:
- Leben (life) = 命 (inochi) or 人生 (jinsei)
- Schicksal (fate) = 運命 (unmei)
- Licht (light) = 光 (hikari)
- Kinder (children) = 子供たち (kodomo-tachi)

The Japanese equivalent of German "gegen" (against) as used in this song. It expresses direction of action toward a target.

How it works:
Place に対して (ni taishite) after a noun to indicate "against" or "toward" that thing.

Example from this song:
"Wir werden gegen unser Schicksal ankaempfen" → 運命に対して戦う (unmei ni taishite tatakau, "fight against fate")

More examples:
- 敋に対して戦う (teki ni taishite tatakau, "fight against the enemy")
- 問題に対して行動する (mondai ni taishite koudou suru, "take action against the problem")
- 自分に対して正直である (jibun ni taishite shoujiki de aru, "be honest with yourself")

The Japanese equivalent of German "irgendwann" (someday) from this song. It expresses an indefinite future time.

How it works:
いつか (itsuka) is an adverb placed before the verb. It means "someday" or "one day."

Example from this song:
"Hoffentlich koennen wir es irgendwann verstehen" → いつか理解できるといい (itsuka rikai dekiru to ii, "I hope we can understand someday")

More examples:
- いつか日本に行きたい (itsuka nihon ni ikitai, "I want to go to Japan someday")
- いつか分かるだろう (itsuka wakaru darou, "You’ll understand someday")
- いつか会えると信じている (itsuka aeru to shinjite iru, "I believe we’ll meet someday")

grammar_points.name: 〜のは〜から (no wa ... kara) — the reason is because

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern Verb/Clause + のは (no wa) ... から (kara) is used to explain a reason. のは (no wa) nominalizes the first clause ("the fact that ..."), and から (kara) gives the reason. It is like saying "The reason [X] is because [Y]." This is a polite and clear way to give explanations.

Example from this song:
The song uses this structure to express why the singer feels driven to rewrite their story — the reason lies in past pain.

More examples:
• 遅れたのは電車が止まったからです (okureta no wa densha ga tomatta kara desu) — "the reason I was late is because the train stopped"
• 泣いているのは嬉しいからだ (naite iru no wa ureshii kara da) — "the reason I'm crying is because I'm happy"
• ここに来たのは君に会いたかったからだ (koko ni kita no wa kimi ni aitakatta kara da) — "the reason I came here is because I wanted to see you"

grammar_points.conjugation_path: Clause + のは (no wa) + Reason + から (kara) → "the reason ~ is because ~"

grammar_points.name: 〜はず (hazu) — supposed to / should be

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern Verb plain form + はず (hazu) expresses an expectation — something that should logically be true based on evidence or prior knowledge. はず (hazu) means "it is expected that ~" or "it should be ~." When reality does not match the expectation, it often pairs with なのに (nanoni, "but") to express surprise or frustration.

Example from this song:
The singer references expectations that did not match reality — things that were supposed to be true but were not.

More examples:
• もう届いたはずだ (mou todoita hazu da) — "it should have arrived by now"
• 彼は知っているはずだ (kare wa shitte iru hazu da) — "he should know (about it)"
• 簡単なはずだったのに (kantan na hazu datta noni) — "it was supposed to be easy, but..."

grammar_points.conjugation_path: Verb plain form + はず (hazu) → "should be / is expected to"

grammar_points.name: 〜られぬ (rarenu) — literary negative potential

explanation.en:
How it works:
The ending 〜られぬ (rarenu) is the classical Japanese form of the modern 〜られない (rarenai, "cannot"). The ぬ (nu) is the classical negative ending, equivalent to modern ない (nai). This form sounds old-fashioned and dramatic, making it popular in songs, poetry, and literary writing. It adds emotional weight and gravity.

Example from this song:
忘れられぬ (wasurerarenu) — "cannot forget" (literary)
A more powerful way to express inability to forget, as if the memory is eternally etched.

More examples:
• 信じられぬ (shinjirarenui) — "unbelievable" (literary)
• 許されぬ罪 (yurusarenu tsumi) — "an unforgivable sin"
• 逃れられぬ運命 (nogarerarenu unmei) — "an inescapable fate"

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 忘れる (wasureru, "to forget") → 忘れられる (wasurerareru, potential) → 忘れられぬ (wasurerarenu, literary negative, "cannot forget")

grammar_points.name: 複合動詞 (fukugou doushi) — compound verbs with 〜去る

explanation.en:
How it works:
Compound verbs combine two verbs to create a more specific meaning. The pattern Verb ます-stem (masu-stem) + 去る (saru, "to leave/remove") intensifies the base verb, adding the nuance of doing something completely or thoroughly. 消す (kesu, "to erase") + 去る (saru) = 消し去る (keshi saru, "to completely erase / wipe out").

Example from this song:
消し去る (keshi saru) — "to completely erase"
Not just erasing, but wiping out entirely without a trace.

More examples:
• 走り去る (hashiri saru) — "to run away / run off completely"
• 飛び去る (tobi saru) — "to fly away"
• 立ち去る (tachi saru) — "to leave / walk away"

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 消す (kesu, "to erase") → 消し (keshi, masu-stem) + 去る (saru, "to leave") → 消し去る (keshi saru, "to completely erase")

grammar_points.name: 命令形 〜くれ (kure) — give me! / do it for me!

explanation.en:
How it works:
くれ (kure) is the imperative (command) form of くれる (kureru, "to give/do for me"). It is a blunt, masculine demand — "give me ~!" or "do ~ for me!" Adding よ (yo) as くれよ (kure yo) softens it slightly with emphasis. This is rougher than ください (kudasai) and is common in anime dialogue and song lyrics.

Example from this song:
くれよ (kure yo) — "give it to me!" / "do it for me!"
The singer demands something with raw emotional urgency.

More examples:
• 教えてくれ (oshiete kure) — "tell me!" (blunt)
• 待ってくれ (matte kure) — "wait for me!"
• 黙ってくれ (damatte kure) — "shut up!" / "be quiet!"

grammar_points.conjugation_path: くれる (kureru, "to give/do for me") → くれ (kure, imperative) → くれよ (kure yo, emphatic imperative, "give me!")

grammar_points.name: 四字熟語 (yojijukugo) — four-character idioms

explanation.en:
How it works:
Four-character idioms (四字熟語, yojijukugo) are compact expressions made of four kanji, originally from classical Chinese. Each carries a deep meaning packed into just four characters. They are used in formal writing, speeches, and dramatic contexts like song lyrics. They sound powerful and intellectual.

Example from this song:
起死回生 (kishikaisei) — "snatching life from the jaws of death" / "a miraculous comeback"
全身全霊 (zenshinzenrei) — "with all one's body and soul" / "with everything you've got"

More examples:
• 一期一会 (ichigoichie) — "once in a lifetime encounter" — treasure every meeting
• 七転八起 (nanakorobi yaoki) — "fall seven times, get up eight" — never give up
• 自業自得 (jigou jitoku) — "you reap what you sow"

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 起死回生 (kishikaisei): 起 (ki, "rise") + 死 (shi, "death") + 回 (kai, "turn") + 生 (sei, "life") → "turn death into life"

explanation.en: Particle さえ marks something as 'even / surprisingly': 'even X (let alone the rest)'. こころの行方さえ知らず 'without even knowing where my heart's gone'. Often combined with negative or surprising statements.
explanation.es: La partícula さえ marca 'incluso / hasta': 'incluso X (por no hablar del resto)'. こころの行方さえ知らず 'sin saber siquiera dónde quedó mi corazón'.
explanation.pt-BR: Partícula さえ marca algo como 'até / até mesmo': 'até X (sem falar do resto)'. こころの行方さえ知らず 'sem nem saber para onde foi meu coração'.

explanation.en: Noun + ごと means 'together with X / including X (within the action)'. 恐怖ごと胸を焦がす 'burn the chest along with the fear'. The whole thing — fear and chest, game and everything in it — is treated as one unit.
explanation.es: Sustantivo + ごと significa 'junto con X / incluyendo X (en la acción)'. 恐怖ごと胸を焦がす 'quemar el pecho junto con el miedo'.
explanation.pt-BR: Substantivo + ごと significa 'junto com X / incluindo X (na ação)'. 恐怖ごと胸を焦がす 'queimar o peito junto com o medo'.

grammar_points.name: 〜なくていい (don't have to / it's fine if not)

explanation.en: Negative -te-form + いい means 'it's fine if not / don't have to'. 笑えなくていい 'it's fine if I can't laugh'; 許せなくていい 'fine if I can't forgive'. Permission to remain in the negative state.
explanation.es: Forma negativa -te + いい significa 'no pasa nada si no / no hace falta'. 笑えなくていい 'está bien si no puedo reír'; 許せなくていい 'está bien si no puedo perdonar'.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma negativa -te + いい significa 'tudo bem se não / não precisa'. 笑えなくていい 'tudo bem se não conseguir rir'; 許せなくていい 'tudo bem se não puder perdoar'.

explanation.en: Verb stem + たい means 'want to do X'. 連れていきたい 'want to take with me'; 護りぬきたい 'want to protect to the end'. The 〜たい form itself conjugates like an い-adjective.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + たい significa 'querer hacer X'. 連れていきたい 'quiero llevar conmigo'; 護りぬきたい 'quiero proteger hasta el final'. La forma 〜たい se conjuga como adjetivo い.
explanation.pt-BR: Radical do verbo + たい significa 'querer fazer X'. 連れていきたい 'quero levar comigo'; 護りぬきたい 'quero proteger até o fim'. A forma 〜たい conjuga como adjetivo い.

explanation.en: Verb stem + 抜く means 'do all the way through / to the bitter end'. 護りぬく 'protect to the very end'; やりぬく 'see something through'. Stresses persistence and completion.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + 抜く significa 'hacer hasta el final'. 護りぬく 'proteger hasta el final'; やりぬく 'llevar a término'.
explanation.pt-BR: Radical do verbo + 抜く significa 'fazer até o fim'. 護りぬく 'proteger até o fim'; やりぬく 'ir até o final'.

grammar_points.name: 〜たまま (in the state of, leaving X as is)

explanation.en: Past form + まま describes a sustained state: 'while remaining X / leaving X unchanged'. 失くしたまま 'while still losing'; 開けたまま 'with (the door) still open'. Often pairs with another verb that contrasts with the static state.
explanation.es: Forma pasada + まま describe estado sostenido: 'permaneciendo así / dejando como está'. 失くしたまま 'mientras lo pierdo'; 開けたまま 'con (la puerta) aún abierta'.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma passada + まま descreve estado mantido: 'continuando assim / deixando como está'. 失くしたまま 'enquanto ainda perde'; 開けたまま 'com (a porta) ainda aberta'.

explanation.en: Volitional verb (〜よう/〜おう) + ぜ is a strongly masculine 'let's X / come on, X!'. つかもうぜ 'let's grab 'em!', さがそうぜ 'let's search!'. Common in shounen anime, sports, and rough male speech. ぜ is rough; ぞ is slightly more measured.
explanation.es: Volitivo (〜よう/〜おう) + ぜ es un '¡hagamos X!' marcadamente masculino. つかもうぜ '¡atrapémoslas!', さがそうぜ '¡busquémoslas!'. Frecuente en shounen, deporte, habla masculina ruda. ぜ es brusco; ぞ es algo más comedido.
explanation.pt-BR: Volitivo (〜よう/〜おう) + ぜ é um 'vamos X!' fortemente masculino. つかもうぜ 'vamos agarrar!', さがそうぜ 'vamos procurar!'. Comum em shounen, esporte, fala masculina rude. ぜ é rude; ぞ é um pouco mais comedido.

explanation.en: Group-1 verbs swap final -u for -e (追いかける is Group-2, but compare 急ぐ → 急げ). Group-2 verbs add -ろ (入れる → 入れろ, 追いかける → 追いかけろ). Blunt and forceful — used in song lyrics, fight scenes; rude in everyday talk.
explanation.es: Grupo 1: -u → -e. Grupo 2: -る → -ろ (入れる → 入れろ, 追いかける → 追いかけろ). Orden directa — en letras, peleas; grosera en el día a día.
explanation.pt-BR: Grupo 1: -u → -e. Grupo 2: -る → -ろ (入れる → 入れろ, 追いかける → 追いかけろ). Comando direto — usado em letras, lutas; grosseiro no dia a dia.

grammar_points.name: Sentence-final ぜ / さ / ぞ (masculine emphatic particles)

explanation.en: Three closely related particles add masculine emphasis: ぜ (rough, urgent), さ (casual, conversational), ぞ (warning/declaration). 翔ぶのさ 'we soar, you see'; ハンパじゃないぜ 'no joke!'. Female speakers tend to avoid all three.
explanation.es: Tres partículas afines añaden énfasis masculino: ぜ (brusca, urgente), さ (casual), ぞ (aviso/declaración). 翔ぶのさ 'volamos, sabes'; ハンパじゃないぜ '¡no es ninguna broma!'. Las hablantes mujeres suelen evitarlas.
explanation.pt-BR: Três partículas próximas adicionam ênfase masculina: ぜ (rude, urgente), さ (casual, conversacional), ぞ (aviso/declaração). 翔ぶのさ 'nós voamos, sabe', ハンパじゃないぜ 'não é coisa pouca!'. Mulheres tendem a evitar.

grammar_points.name: Verb-stem + に + 行く/来る (go/come to do X)

explanation.en: Verb stem + に + a movement verb expresses purpose: 'go (or come) in order to X'. 見つけに行く 'go to find'; 食べに行く 'go to eat'; 遊びに来る 'come to hang out'. The motion and the goal are stated in one phrase.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + に + verbo de movimiento expresa propósito: 'ir (o venir) a hacer X'. 見つけに行く 'ir a encontrar'; 食べに行く 'ir a comer'; 遊びに来る 'venir a jugar'.
explanation.pt-BR: Radical do verbo + に + verbo de movimento expressa propósito: 'ir (ou vir) para fazer X'. 見つけに行く 'ir achar'; 食べに行く 'ir comer'; 遊びに来る 'vir brincar'.

explanation.en: Verb stem + は + しない is a strong, often defiant negation: 'won't (do that), no way'. かないはしない 'no enemy can stand a chance'; 捨てはしない 'I won't throw it away'. Stronger than plain 〜ない.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + は + しない es negación enfática, a menudo desafiante. かないはしない 'ningún enemigo está a la altura'; 捨てはしない 'no lo voy a tirar'. Más fuerte que 〜ない.
explanation.pt-BR: Radical do verbo + は + しない é negação enfática, frequentemente desafiadora. かないはしない 'nenhum inimigo é páreo'; 捨てはしない 'não vou jogar fora'. Mais forte que 〜ない.

grammar_points.name: Mimetic adverbs (ぎっしり, どっさり, キラキラ etc.)

explanation.en: Japanese has hundreds of mimetic words (giseigo/gitaigo) describing manner, sound, or feeling. ぎっしり 'packed densely'; どっさり 'in heaps'; キラキラ 'sparkling'; ワクワク 'excited heart-pounding'. Often inserted between phrases for vivid effect — sometimes Romanised in song lyrics for stylish look.
explanation.es: El japonés tiene cientos de palabras miméticas (giseigo/gitaigo). ぎっしり 'apretadamente lleno'; どっさり 'a montones'; キラキラ 'resplandeciente'; ワクワク 'corazón emocionado'. Se insertan para efecto vivo — a veces romanizadas en letras.
explanation.pt-BR: O japonês tem centenas de palavras miméticas (giseigo/gitaigo). ぎっしり 'denso, lotado'; どっさり 'aos montes'; キラキラ 'cintilante'; ワクワク 'coração acelerado'. Inseridas para efeito vivo — às vezes romanizadas em letras.

grammar_points.name: 〜たい (tai: want to do)

explanation.en:
How it works: Take the verb stem (masu-stem) and add たい (tai) to express wanting to do something. This is one of the first and most important grammar patterns for beginners.

Example from this song: 帰りたい (kaeritai) = 'want to return' — from 帰る (kaeru, 'to return') → 帰り (kaeri, stem) + たい (tai, 'want to'). Also: 育てたい (sodatetai) = 'want to raise' and 語りたい (kataritai) = 'want to talk about'

More examples:
• 食べる (taberu, 'to eat') → 食べたい (tabetai, 'want to eat')
• 行く (iku, 'to go') → 行きたい (ikitai, 'want to go')
• 見る (miru, 'to see') → 見たい (mitai, 'want to see')

Note: For -ru verbs (ichidan), drop る and add たい. For -u verbs (godan), change the last syllable to its い-row equivalent and add たい: く→きたい, む→みたい, す→したい. たい conjugates like an い-adjective: たくない (don't want), たかった (wanted).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 帰る (kaeru, 'to return') → 帰り (kaeri, stem) + たい (tai, 'want to') → 帰りたい (kaeritai, 'want to return') / 育てる (sodateru, 'to raise') → 育てたい (sodatetai, 'want to raise')

grammar_points.name: 〜のなら (no nara: if it is that)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add のなら (no nara) after a verb to express a conditional that assumes the situation — 'if it is the case that X' or 'given that X'.

Example from this song: くるのなら (kuru no nara) = 'if (that time) comes' — from くる (kuru, 'to come') + のなら (no nara, 'if it is that')

More examples:
• 行く (iku, 'to go') → 行くのなら (iku no nara, 'if you're going')
• 諦める (akirameru, 'to give up') → 諦めるのなら (akirameru no nara, 'if you're going to give up')
• 会える (aeru, 'can meet') → 会えるのなら (aeru no nara, 'if we can meet')

Note: のなら assumes the condition has been stated or is likely. It often implies 'since you've decided...' or 'well, if that's the case...' It's more emphatic than plain なら.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: くる (kuru, 'to come') + のなら (no nara, 'if it is that') → くるのなら (kuru no nara, 'if it comes')

grammar_points.name: 〜だらけ (darake: full of)

explanation.en:
How it works: Attach だらけ (darake) after a noun to mean 'full of' or 'riddled with', usually with a negative or overwhelming connotation.

Example from this song: 強がりだらけ (tsuyogari darake) = 'full of bravado / nothing but false bravery' — from 強がり (tsuyogari, 'bravado/putting on a brave front') + だらけ (darake, 'full of')

More examples:
• 嘘 (uso, 'lies') → 嘘だらけ (uso darake, 'full of lies')
• 傷 (kizu, 'wounds') → 傷だらけ (kizu darake, 'covered in wounds')
• 失敗 (shippai, 'failure') → 失敗だらけ (shippai darake, 'full of failures')

Note: だらけ almost always carries a negative nuance — being overwhelmed by something undesirable. To modify a noun: だらけの + noun: 傷だらけの体 (kizu darake no karada, 'a body covered in wounds').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 強がり (tsuyogari, 'bravado') + だらけ (darake, 'full of') → 強がりだらけ (tsuyogari darake, 'full of bravado')

grammar_points.name: 〜でいい (de ii: it's fine with)

explanation.en:
How it works: Use noun + でいい (de ii) to express that something is acceptable or sufficient — 'X is fine' or 'X will do'. It can also imply settling for something.

Example from this song: 夢物語でいいから (monogatari de ii kara) = 'even if it's just a fairy tale, that's fine' — from 夢物語 (yumemonogatari, 'fairy tale') + でいい (de ii, 'is fine') + から (kara, 'because/so')

More examples:
• 水 (mizu, 'water') → 水でいい (mizu de ii, 'water is fine')
• 明日 (ashita, 'tomorrow') → 明日でいい (ashita de ii, 'tomorrow is fine')
• これ (kore, 'this') → これでいい (kore de ii, 'this is fine')

Note: でいい can sometimes sound like 'settling' — 水でいい means 'water is fine (I don't need anything special)'. For 'water is good/what I want', use がいい: 水がいい. The difference is subtle but important.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 夢物語 (yumemonogatari, 'fairy tale') + でいい (de ii, 'is fine') + から (kara, 'so') → 夢物語でいいから (yumemonogatari de ii kara, 'a fairy tale is fine')

grammar_points.name: 意志形 + よ (volitional + yo: let's)

explanation.en:
How it works: Use the volitional form (〜よう/〜おう) and add よ (yo) for a casual, warm invitation — 'let's do X!' The よ adds encouragement.

Example from this song: 帰ろうよ (kaerouyo) = 'let's go home!' — from 帰る (kaeru, 'to return') → 帰ろう (kaerou, volitional) + よ (yo, encouragement)

More examples:
• 食べる (taberu, 'to eat') → 食べようよ (tabeyou yo, 'let's eat!')
• 行く (iku, 'to go') → 行こうよ (ikou yo, 'let's go!')
• 遊ぶ (asobu, 'to play') → 遊ぼうよ (asobou yo, 'let's play!')

Note: The volitional alone (行こう) is a suggestion; adding よ makes it more encouraging and friendly. For godan verbs: change final syllable to お-row + う. For ichidan verbs: drop る, add よう. する→しよう, 来る→来よう (koyou).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 帰る (kaeru, 'to return') → 帰ろう (kaerou, volitional) + よ (yo, encouragement) → 帰ろうよ (kaerouyo, 'let's go home!')

grammar_points.name: 〜てた (teta: had been doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: Use てた (teta), the casual contraction of ていた (te ita), to express past progressive — 'was doing X' or 'had been doing X'.

Example from this song: 探してた (sagashiteta) = 'had been searching' — from 探す (sagasu, 'to search') → 探していた (sagashite ita, 'was searching') → 探してた (sagashiteta, casual). Also: 気付いてた (kizuiteta) = 'had noticed'

More examples:
• 待つ (matsu, 'to wait') → 待ってた (matteta, 'had been waiting')
• 考える (kangaeru, 'to think') → 考えてた (kangaeteta, 'had been thinking')
• 知る (shiru, 'to know') → 知ってた (shitteta, 'had known')

Note: The contraction pattern: ている → てる (present), ていた → てた (past), ていない → てない (negative). Understanding these casual contractions is essential for comprehending songs and everyday Japanese.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 探す (sagasu, 'to search') → 探していた (sagashite ita, 'was searching') → 探してた (sagashiteta, 'had been searching' — casual)

translations.en: Like I could change myself — even the whole world

literal_meaning.en: Self (object) world even-also, change-completely-can-seemingly

cultural_context.en: Stacking 〜さえ + も is emphatic: '(not just X but) even Y too'. 自分を…世界さえも = 'myself, and even the world'. The grand scale matches Code Geass's themes of remaking reality.

literal_meaning.en: Cannot-hide frustration and stand-frozen self (object) gazing

cultural_context.en: 〜ぬ is the classical/literary negative ending (= 〜ない): 隠せぬ = 隠せない. Common in lyrics, idioms, and proverbs. Sounds heavier and more poetic than the modern form.

translations.en: While wavering, while agonizing

literal_meaning.en: Regretting-while, if-decide good (assertion)

cultural_context.en: 〜ばいい ('it's fine if you do X') is gentle permission/encouragement: 'just go ahead and decide'. Adding さ softens it further into a reassuring 'you'll be alright if you do'.

translations.en: A single word you gave me — and the confusion vanished
translations.es: Una sola palabra que me diste — y la confusión se esfumó
translations.pt-BR: Uma palavra que você me deu — e a confusão se foi

literal_meaning.en: You (subject) gave word one, hesitation (topic) vanish-away

cultural_context.en: くれる is the giving verb that marks the giver as benefitting the speaker — 'you gave (to me)'. Different from あげる (you give to someone else) or もらう (I receive).

translations.en: Light streamed into my once-empty room
translations.es: La luz entró en mi cuarto, antes vacío
translations.pt-BR: A luz invadiu meu quarto antes vazio

literal_meaning.en: Empty was, my room into, light (subject) shone

cultural_context.en: 光が射す ('light shines/streams in') is a stock phrase for sunlight reaching a previously dark place. Often metaphorical for hope arriving.

translations.en: The wide sky I looked up at clears more and more, deeply blue
translations.es: El gran cielo que miré se va aclarando, completamente azul
translations.pt-BR: O céu amplo que eu olhei vai ficando azul, totalmente limpo

literal_meaning.en: Looked-up sky (subject) bluely, become-completely-clear-and go

cultural_context.en: 澄む = 'to be clear/limpid'; + 切る ('all the way') = 澄み切る ('become totally clear'); + 〜ていく ('go on doing') = 'progressively becoming clearer'. Three layers stacking the same image.

translations.en: I decided to open the window I'd shut tight
translations.es: Decidí abrir la ventana que había cerrado
translations.pt-BR: Decidi abrir a janela que eu havia trancado

literal_meaning.en: Sealed window (object) open thing (object) decided

cultural_context.en: 閉ざす ('to seal, shut tight') is a heavier, more permanent shutting than 閉める. Pairs with 心を閉ざす ('to close one's heart'). Opening it is metaphorical for committing to change.

translations.en: Searching for an answer that should exist in this unfulfilled daily life

translations.pt-BR: Procurando uma resposta que deveria existir neste cotidiano incompleto

literal_meaning.en: Cannot-be-filled daily-life in, exist-should answer (object) searching

translations.en: Alone in the morning sun — when I turn toward a gentle voice
translations.es: Solo bajo el sol de la mañana — cuando me giro hacia una voz suave
translations.pt-BR: Sozinho no sol da manhã — quando me viro para uma voz suave

literal_meaning.en: Morning-sun in alone, soft voice toward, if-turn

translations.en: Inside that dazzling sunlight — you smile, just like that
translations.es: En medio de esa luz cegadora — tú sonríes, sin más
translations.pt-BR: No meio daquela luz ofuscante — você sorri, sem mais

literal_meaning.en: Dazzling sunlight's midst, casually you (subject) smile

cultural_context.en: ふと is a beautifully untranslatable adverb — 'unexpectedly / casually / out of nowhere'. ふと君が微笑む = 'you smiled, unbidden, the way someone does without thinking'.

translations.en: The sealed window is about to open
translations.es: La ventana cerrada está a punto de abrirse
translations.pt-BR: A janela trancada está prestes a se abrir

literal_meaning.en: Sealed window (subject) likely-to-open become

cultural_context.en: Verb stem + そう ('looks like / seems about to') + になる = 'comes to look like it will'. Common pattern: 泣きそうになる ('feel like I might cry'), 倒れそうになる ('feel like I might collapse').

translations.en: That presence is right before my eyes...
translations.es: Esa presencia está justo delante de mí...
translations.pt-BR: Essa presença está bem na minha frente...

literal_meaning.en: Existence (topic) my eye's-front at

translations.en: I feel that moment — right here, right now...
translations.es: Siento ese instante — aquí y ahora...
translations.pt-BR: Sinto esse instante — agora, aqui mesmo...

literal_meaning.en: Moment (object) feel, now here at

translations.es: Tendiendo las dos manos hacia la luz...
translations.pt-BR: Estendendo as duas mãos rumo à luz...

literal_meaning.en: Light toward, both-hands (object) stretching

cultural_context.en: へと is the directional particle へ ('toward') + と (an emphatic/quoting marker) — slightly heavier than へ alone, common in lyrics for added gravity.

translations.en: The colors of the sky and a fragrant wind, blowing right through my heart
translations.es: Los colores del cielo y un viento perfumado que cruza mi corazón
translations.pt-BR: As cores do céu e um vento perfumado que atravessam meu coração

literal_meaning.en: Heart (path) blow-through, sky's color, fragrant wind

cultural_context.en: 心を吹き抜ける ('to blow right through one's heart') is a stock J-rock image: a sensation so strong it passes through you like wind. Pairing it with the song's title (色/colors) closes the lyric on an open, sensory note.

explanation.en: 〜さえ marks something extreme as 'even X'. Adding も intensifies it: 世界さえも = 'even the world (no less)'. Often paired with conditional or volitional clauses to set up a 'if even X, then surely Y' frame.
explanation.es: 〜さえ marca algo extremo como 'hasta X / incluso X'. Añadir も lo intensifica: 世界さえも = 'incluso el propio mundo'. Suele acompañar a condicionales: 'si hasta X, seguro que Y'.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜さえ marca algo extremo como 'até X'. Adicionar も intensifica: 世界さえも = 'até o próprio mundo'. Costuma combinar com condicionais para 'se até X, então com certeza Y'.

grammar_points.name: Verb-て + しまえそう ('looks like one might be able to fully do')

explanation.en: Three layers: 〜てしまう ('do completely / end up doing') + 〜える (potential 'be able to') + 〜そう ('looks like'). 変えてしまえそう = 'looks like (I) could fully change (it)'. Used to express a sudden sense of possibility for a big, irreversible act.
explanation.es: Tres capas: 〜てしまう ('hacer del todo') + 〜える (potencial 'poder') + 〜そう ('parece'). 変えてしまえそう = 'parece que podría cambiarlo del todo'. Sensación repentina de poder con algo grande.
explanation.pt-BR: Três camadas: 〜てしまう ('fazer por completo') + 〜える (potencial 'poder') + 〜そう ('parece'). 変えてしまえそう = 'parece que eu conseguiria mudar por completo'. Sensação repentina de poder fazer algo grande.

explanation.en: 〜ぬ is the classical negative ending equivalent to 〜ない: 隠せぬ = 隠せない ('cannot hide'), 満たせぬ = 満たせない ('cannot be filled'). Common in lyrics, set phrases (時の流れに身をまかせぬ), and proverbs. Reads as more solemn or old-fashioned.
explanation.es: 〜ぬ es la terminación negativa clásica equivalente a 〜ない: 隠せぬ = 隠せない, 満たせぬ = 満たせない. Frecuente en letras, frases hechas y proverbios. Suena más solemne/antiguo.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜ぬ é a terminação negativa clássica equivalente a 〜ない: 隠せぬ = 隠せない, 満たせぬ = 満たせない. Comum em letras, expressões fixas e provérbios. Soa mais solene/antigo.

explanation.en: Verb stem + ながら expresses two simultaneous actions by the same subject: 迷いながら 悩みながら 悔やみながら ('while wavering, while worrying, while regretting'). Stacking ながら-clauses is a common rhythmic device in lyrics — accumulates a list of overlapping internal states.
explanation.es: Raíz verbal + ながら expresa dos acciones simultáneas del mismo sujeto: 迷いながら 悩みながら 悔やみながら. Apilar varios ながら es un recurso rítmico en letras — acumula estados internos solapados.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz verbal + ながら exprime duas ações simultâneas do mesmo sujeito: 迷いながら 悩みながら 悔やみながら. Empilhar ながら é um recurso rítmico em letras — junta estados emocionais sobrepostos.

grammar_points.name: 〜ばいい (it's fine if you / just do X)

explanation.en: Conditional 〜ば + いい literally 'if X then it's good' = 'just do X / it'll be fine to do X'. Gentle permission or encouragement: 決めればいい ('it's fine to just decide'). Adding さ at the end softens it further into reassurance.
explanation.es: Condicional 〜ば + いい significa 'si X, entonces bien' = 'basta con hacer X / hazlo y ya'. Permiso/aliento suave: 決めればいい. Con さ al final suena aún más reconfortante.
explanation.pt-BR: Condicional 〜ば + いい significa 'se X, então tudo bem' = 'é só fazer X / pode fazer X'. Permissão ou incentivo suave: 決めればいい. Com さ no fim, vira tom mais reconfortante.

explanation.en: Verb stem + 切る ('to do completely'): 澄み切る ('become totally clear'). Verb stem + 抜ける ('to pass through completely'): 駆け抜ける ('race through'), 吹き抜ける ('blow through'). Verb stem + 去る ('to depart'): 消え去る ('vanish completely'). Each suffix adds a flavor of completeness or directional motion.
explanation.es: Raíz verbal + 切る ('hacer del todo'): 澄み切る. Raíz + 抜ける ('atravesar'): 駆け抜ける, 吹き抜ける. Raíz + 去る ('marcharse'): 消え去る. Cada sufijo aporta un matiz de totalidad o movimiento direccional.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz verbal + 切る ('fazer por completo'): 澄み切る. Raiz + 抜ける ('atravessar'): 駆け抜ける, 吹き抜ける. Raiz + 去る ('partir'): 消え去る. Cada sufixo dá um sabor de totalidade ou movimento direcional.

grammar_points.name: Verb stem + そう (looks like / seems about to)

explanation.en: Verb stem + そう = 'looks like X is about to happen / seems likely to'. 開きそう ('looks like it'll open'); 泣きそう ('about to cry'); 倒れそう ('about to fall'). Adding になる ('come to be that') makes it 'come to be on the verge of': 開きそうになる.
explanation.es: Raíz verbal + そう = 'parece a punto de / parece que va a'. 開きそう, 泣きそう, 倒れそう. Añadir になる = 'estar a punto de': 開きそうになる.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz verbal + そう = 'parece prestes a / parece que vai'. 開きそう, 泣きそう, 倒れそう. Adicionar になる = 'estar prestes a': 開きそうになる.
