translations.en: I pressed my ear tight against your back and held you — this body of mine, like a borderline, just gets in the way; it feels like it could drift off somewhere.
translations.es: Apreté el oído contra tu espalda y te abracé — este cuerpo mío, como una línea divisoria, sólo estorba; siento que podría irse a algún lado.
translations.pt-BR: Encostei meu ouvido bem junto às suas costas e te abracei — esse meu corpo, que parece uma linha de fronteira, só atrapalha; tenho a impressão de que pode escapar para algum canto.

literal_meaning.en: 'To-back ear snugly-pressing, embraced. Boundary-line-like body is hindrance, right? Somewhere-going-seems-like, (emphasis).' The narrator imagines her skin as a border that keeps her and the beloved apart.

cultural_context.en: ぴっと is a mimetic (giongo) adverb evoking a tight snap-fit — Japanese pop lyrics use mimetics like this to convey physical sensation without medical vocabulary.

translations.en: Because if I stay quiet, this feeling feels like it'll tear apart — in a world only three meters across, I want to cling to you more, closer still.
translations.es: Porque si me quedo callada, este sentimiento parece a punto de desgarrarse — en un mundo de apenas tres metros a la redonda, quiero pegarme más a ti.
translations.pt-BR: Porque se eu ficar calada, esse sentimento parece que vai se rasgar — num mundo de apenas três metros de raio, quero grudar em você cada vez mais.

literal_meaning.en: 'Staying-silent if, about-to-tear-apart because, this-kind-of feeling. Radius 3-meter within-of world in, more more, want-to-cling (emphasis).'

translations.en: Taking turns pedaling, we pass the drooping sunflowers on the street, swallowing up the wind as we go — feels like we could just lift off. The first time I felt your body heat, I wanted to be stronger than anyone — a warm rhythm, our two hearts drawing together.
translations.es: Turnándonos en los pedales, dejamos atrás la calle de los girasoles caídos, tragándonos el viento — parece que hasta podríamos volar. La primera vez que sentí tu calor corporal, quise ser más fuerte que nadie — un ritmo cálido, nuestros dos corazones uniéndose.
translations.pt-BR: Pedalando alternado, passamos pela rua dos girassóis caídos, engolindo o vento — parece que a gente até voaria. Na primeira vez que senti seu calor, quis ser mais forte que qualquer um — um ritmo quente, nossos dois corações se grudando.

literal_meaning.en: 'Taking-turns with pedal pedaling, bow-of-sunflower passing, rapidly wind swallowing — like-that could-fly, right? For-the-first-time felt your body-heat. Than-anyone stronger want-to-become. Warm rhythm. Two-hearts are drawing-together.'

cultural_context.en: おじぎのひまわり ('bowing sunflower') is a poetic image — a sunflower whose heavy head has drooped into a bow, like the Japanese おじぎ greeting. 2コ is a colloquial written form of 二個 mixing digits and katakana.

meaning.en: drawing together (colloquial くっついていく)

translations.en: Lip to lip, eye to eye, hand to hand — God hasn't forbidden a thing. I love you. I love you. I love you. I'm not chastened yet; grown-ups just don't get it. It hurts, it aches, I want to show you — I'll burst. I'm waiting while I look the other way, so with my hesitating hand still in my pocket, touch my cheek — cast a spell on this power called love.
translations.es: Labio con labio, ojo con ojo, mano con mano — Dios no ha prohibido nada. Te amo. Te amo. Te amo. Todavía no aprendo la lección; los adultos no lo entienden. Duele, aprieta, quiero mostrártelo — voy a estallar. Espero mirando hacia otro lado, así que con mi mano indecisa en el bolsillo, toca mi mejilla — lánzale un hechizo a esta fuerza que se llama amor.
translations.pt-BR: Lábio no lábio, olho no olho, mão na mão — Deus não proibiu coisa nenhuma. Eu te amo. Eu te amo. Eu te amo. Ainda não aprendi a lição; adulto não entende. Dói, aperta, quero mostrar — vou explodir. Estou esperando olhando pro outro lado, então com minha mão hesitante no bolso, toca minha bochecha — lança um feitiço nessa força chamada amor.

literal_meaning.en: 'Lip and lip, pupil and pupil and hand and hand. God anything at-all prohibition such-as isn't-doing. Loving. Loving. Loving. I still not-chastened, adult-as don't-understand. Painful, heartrending, wanting-to-show, I'll-burst. Other-way looking waiting because, pocket's hesitating hand with, cheek touching — in-love power on magic cast.'

cultural_context.en: そっぽを見る ('look the other way') is the classic Japanese shoujo gesture of shy affection — pretending not to watch while actually waiting. パンクしちゃう uses パンク (originally 'puncture/flat tire') as slang for emotional overload.

meaning.en: not chastened; not learned the lesson
don't get it (casual わからない)
pocket (cute form of ポケット)

translations.en: The way home — always taking the long route together. Under a sky that looks like spilled orange, I feel somehow HAPPY & SAD.
translations.es: El camino a casa — siempre dábamos el rodeo más largo juntos. Bajo un cielo como naranja derramado, de algún modo me siento HAPPY & SAD.
translations.pt-BR: O caminho pra casa — sempre dávamos a volta mais longa juntos. Sob um céu parecendo laranja derramado, de alguma forma me sinto HAPPY & SAD.

literal_meaning.en: 'Always together-(adv) long-way were-doing homeward-road. Orange spill-like sky in, somehow HAPPY & SAD.'

translations.en: Why were we born at all? We're each half, right? I try puzzling it out alone, but I just end up bad at it.
translations.es: ¿Por qué nacimos? Cada una es una mitad, ¿no? Lo pienso sola, pero al final se me da fatal.
translations.pt-BR: Por que a gente nasceu, afinal? Cada um é metade, né? Tento pensar sozinha, mas no fim das contas sou ruim nisso mesmo.

literal_meaning.en: 'We-(topic) why were-born? Half are right? Alone-by thinking-try but, after-all not-good-at-it (emphasis).' The song's title 1/2 surfaces here: each person is a half, completed by the other.

cultural_context.en: 半分だよね ('we're each a half, right?') is the thematic pivot — the song's title '1/2' comes from this idea of each person being half of a pair. へたっぴ is cute/childish slang from 下手 with the -っぴ diminutive suffix.

meaning.en: no good at it (cute form of 下手)

translations.en: A shoulder strong enough to hurl a ball so far it vanishes — I envied that, I wanted to be a boy. Soft as clear water, stronger than anyone — the way I was when I was little. Weird, isn't it — my tears are spilling over.
translations.es: Un hombro fuerte capaz de lanzar la pelota hasta que desaparece — lo envidiaba, quería ser niño. Suave como agua clara, más fuerte que nadie — como cuando era pequeña. Qué raro, ¿no? — las lágrimas se me caen.
translations.pt-BR: Um ombro forte o bastante pra jogar a bola tão longe que some — eu invejava isso, queria ser menino. Macia como água clara, mais forte que qualquer um — como eu era quando criança. Estranho, né — minhas lágrimas estão transbordando.

literal_meaning.en: 'Becoming-invisible to-extent far to ball can-throw strong shoulder — enviable, boy want-to-become. Clear water like softly, than-anyone want-to-be-stronger. Tiny-time like. Strange right, tear spilling-goes.'

cultural_context.en: おとこの子になりたかった ('I wanted to be a boy') is a nostalgic childhood memory — Japanese female pop lyrics of the era often revisited tomboy-phase regret as shorthand for losing a simpler strength.

meaning.en: spilling over (colloquial こぼれていく)
even if I'm told (passive + ても)

translations.en: We feel the same things the same way. Even if they tell me I can't reach, I want to jump, just like this. I'll give you a goodbye kiss — so hold that last-step distance tight, so the sun will never set.
translations.es: Sentimos lo mismo de la misma forma. Aunque me digan que no llegaré, quiero saltar tal cual. Te daré un beso de despedida — así que aprieta fuerte esa distancia del último paso, para que el sol nunca se ponga.
translations.pt-BR: A gente sente as mesmas coisas do mesmo jeito. Mesmo que me digam que não vou alcançar, quero pular assim mesmo. Vou te dar um beijo de despedida — então me abrace forte, nessa distância do último passo, pra que o sol nunca se ponha.

literal_meaning.en: 'Same thing same way-of-feeling doing. Won't-reach even-if-told, just-like-this want-to-jump. Bye-bye-of-kiss do because, last-step-of distance tightly hold. Sun forever doesn't-set so-that.'

translations.en: We watched one lonely sunset together, just the two of us. It's beautiful but... somehow I can't put it into words — somehow something's missing. Ba-bang-bang!
translations.es: Vimos juntos una puesta de sol solitaria, sólo nosotros dos. Es hermoso, pero... de algún modo no puedo decirlo — falta algo. ¡Ba-bang-bang!
translations.pt-BR: A gente ficou olhando um pôr do sol solitário, só nós dois. É bonito, mas... de alguma forma não consigo dizer — tem alguma coisa faltando. Ba-bang-bang!

literal_meaning.en: 'One-(piece)-of setting-sun solitarily, two-people with, were-watching. Beautiful but-(emphasis). Somehow can't-say right? Somehow isn't-enough (emphasis). Ba-bang-bang!'

cultural_context.en: ぽつんと is a mimetic adverb conveying a single, lonely dot in wide space — here it paints the sunset as an isolated spot of light. ババンバン! is a playful sound-effect closer, mimicking a drum or firework burst.

translations.en: Just as Nostradamus foretold, on the day this planet explodes — I want to be one with you. A warm rhythm, our two hearts drawing closer still.
translations.es: Tal como Nostradamus profetizó, el día que este planeta explote — quiero ser uno contigo. Un ritmo cálido, nuestros dos corazones uniéndose.
translations.pt-BR: Assim como Nostradamus previu, no dia em que esse planeta explodir — quero ser um só com você. Um ritmo quente, nossos dois corações se unindo.

literal_meaning.en: 'Nostradamus prophesied just-as, this planet explode day (topic), one-into want-to-become.' A 1997-era reference to the Nostradamus 1999 apocalypse prophecy — popular Japanese pop-culture touchstone at the time.

cultural_context.en: ノストラダムスの大予言 (Nostradamus's Great Prophecy) was a massive Japanese pop-culture phenomenon from the 1970s through the late 1990s, predicting Earth's destruction in July 1999. For a 1997 song, referencing it is a shorthand for 'right before the end of the world'.

grammar_points.name: 〜みたい (mitai — 'like/similar to')

explanation.en: Attached to nouns or plain-form verbs, 〜みたい expresses similarity or resemblance ('like X'). More casual than the bookish 〜のよう. In 境界線みたいな身体, みたい acts as a na-adjective modifying 身体.
explanation.es: Unido a sustantivos o verbos en forma simple, 〜みたい expresa semejanza ('como X'). Más coloquial que 〜のよう. En 境界線みたいな身体, funciona como adjetivo-na modificando 身体.
explanation.pt-BR: Ligado a substantivos ou verbos na forma simples, 〜みたい expressa semelhança ('como X'). Mais coloquial que 〜のよう. Em 境界線みたいな身体, funciona como adjetivo-na modificando 身体.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: noun / plain verb → + みたい → + な (before noun) / + に (before verb)

grammar_points.name: 〜そう (sou — 'looks like / seems about to')

explanation.en: Attached to a verb stem, 〜そう means the action looks about to happen: 飛べそう ('looks like [we] could fly'), ちぎれそう ('about to be torn'), いっちゃいそう ('looks about to go off'). The song uses this pattern five+ times to convey imminence.
explanation.es: Unido a la raíz del verbo, 〜そう expresa 'parece a punto de': 飛べそう ('parece que volaríamos'), ちぎれそう ('a punto de romperse'). La canción usa este patrón varias veces para sugerir inminencia.
explanation.pt-BR: Ligado ao radical verbal, 〜そう indica que algo 'parece prestes a acontecer': 飛べそう ('parece que vai voar'), ちぎれそう ('quase rasgando'). A música usa esse padrão várias vezes para evocar iminência.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb stem → + そう (e.g. 飛ぶ → 飛び → 飛べそう with potential stem)

grammar_points.name: 〜たい (tai — 'want to')

explanation.en: Attached to verb stem to express the speaker's desire: なりたい ('want to become'), ひっついてたい ('want to keep clinging'), ジャンプしたい ('want to jump'). Conjugates like an i-adjective (なりたかった = past).
explanation.es: Unido a la raíz verbal para expresar deseo propio: なりたい ('quiero llegar a ser'), ひっついてたい ('quiero seguir pegada'). Se conjuga como adjetivo-i (なりたかった = pasado).
explanation.pt-BR: Ligado ao radical verbal para expressar desejo próprio: なりたい ('quero me tornar'), ひっついてたい ('quero continuar grudada'). Conjuga-se como adjetivo-i (なりたかった = passado).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: dictionary form → ます-stem → + たい (e.g. なる → なり → なりたい)

grammar_points.name: 〜てない / 〜てる (colloquial shortening of 〜ていない / 〜ている)

explanation.en: In casual speech the い of 〜ている / 〜ていない is dropped: 待ってる (= 待っている), 懲りてない (= 懲りていない), してない (= していない), 黙ってる (= 黙っている). Used throughout the song to keep the tone conversational.
explanation.es: En el habla coloquial el い de 〜ている/〜ていない se elide: 待ってる, 懲りてない, 黙ってる. La canción lo usa en toda la letra para mantener un tono conversacional.
explanation.pt-BR: Na fala coloquial, o い de 〜ている/〜ていない cai: 待ってる (= 待っている), 懲りてない (= 懲りていない). A música usa esse encurtamento o tempo todo para manter o tom de conversa.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 待っている → 待ってる (drops い); 待っていない → 待ってない

grammar_points.name: 〜ように (you ni — 'so that / in order that')

explanation.en: After a negative verb, 〜ように expresses a wish or hope for something NOT to happen: 太陽がずっとしずまないように ('so that the sun will never set'). Also appears as 水のように ('like water') to mean 'in the manner of'.
explanation.es: Tras verbo negativo, 〜ように expresa deseo para que algo NO suceda: 太陽がずっとしずまないように ('para que el sol nunca se ponga'). También aparece como 水のように ('como agua').
explanation.pt-BR: Após verbo negativo, 〜ように expressa desejo para que algo NÃO aconteça: 太陽がずっとしずまないように ('para que o sol nunca se ponha'). Também aparece como 水のように ('como água').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb plain negative + ように (e.g. しずむ → しずまない → しずまないように)

grammar_points.name: 〜ても / 〜たって (te mo / tatte — 'even if')

explanation.en: The verb te-form + も grants a concessive meaning ('even if X'): 考えてもみる ('even if I try thinking'). The colloquial equivalent is 〜たって: 届かないって言われたって ('even if I'm told [it] won't reach'). Common in casual speech and lyrics.
explanation.es: Forma-te del verbo + も da sentido concesivo ('aunque X'): 考えてもみる. El equivalente coloquial es 〜たって: 届かないって言われたって ('aunque me digan que no llega').
explanation.pt-BR: Forma-te do verbo + も cria sentido concessivo ('mesmo que X'): 考えてもみる. O equivalente coloquial é 〜たって: 届かないって言われたって ('mesmo que me digam que não chega'). Comum na fala coloquial e em letras.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb → te-form → + も (formal) / plain past → + たって (casual)

grammar_points.name: Casual contractions (わかんない, やっぱ, どっか, ポッケ)

explanation.en: The song is saturated with casual spoken contractions: わかんない (= わからない), やっぱ (= やっぱり), どっか (= どこか), ポッケ (= ポケット), メトル (= メートル). These give the speaker a young, conversational voice. Learners should recognize them in speech and anime but avoid them in formal writing.
explanation.es: La canción está llena de contracciones habladas: わかんない (= わからない), やっぱ (= やっぱり), どっか (= どこか), ポッケ (= ポケット). Dan un tono joven y coloquial. Reconocerlas en habla/anime, pero evitarlas en escritura formal.
explanation.pt-BR: A música é cheia de contrações da fala cotidiana: わかんない (= わからない), やっぱ (= やっぱり), どっか (= どこか), ポッケ (= ポケット). Dão voz jovem e coloquial. Reconhecer em fala/anime, mas evitar em escrita formal.

grammar_points.name: English lyrics in anime OST

explanation.en:
How it works: This song is entirely in English. Hiroyuki Sawano's Attack on Titan soundtrack frequently uses English vocal tracks to create emotional, cinematic moments. The choice of English adds a universal quality to the music.

Example from this song: 'Call Your Name' (GV version) is performed entirely in English by Gemie, one of Sawano's regular vocalists.

Note: While this doesn't teach Japanese grammar, recognizing the emotional vocabulary (loss, determination, hope) in English anime songs helps build context for similar themes expressed in Japanese lyrics across other AOT tracks.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: N/A — English lyrics, not Japanese conjugation

grammar_points.name: Past tense narration

explanation.en:
How it works: English past tense is formed by adding -ed to regular verbs or using irregular forms. In Japanese, the past tense (た-form / ta-form) is used similarly for narration.

Example from this song: 'lost', 'gave', 'dreamt' — irregular English past tenses narrating loss and sacrifice.

Japanese equivalents:
• 'lost' → 失った (ushinatta, from 失う/ushinau, 'to lose')
• 'gave' → 与えた (ataeta, from 与える/ataeru, 'to give')
• 'dreamt' → 夢見た (yumemita, from 夢見る/yumemiru, 'to dream')

Note: Both languages use past tense for emotional narration in songs. Japanese た-form can also express discovery or sudden realization, not just past events.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: lose → lost, give → gave, dream → dreamt / Japanese: 失う (ushinau) → 失った (ushinatta), 与える (ataeru) → 与えた (ataeta)

grammar_points.name: Present continuous for emotion

explanation.en:
How it works: English present continuous ('am/is/are + -ing') expresses ongoing emotional states. The Japanese equivalent is 〜ている (te-iru), which shows both ongoing actions and resulting states.

Example from this song: 'I'm crying', 'I'm standing' — present continuous expressing raw, ongoing emotion.

Japanese equivalents:
• 'I'm crying' → 泣いている (naiteiru, from 泣く/naku, 'to cry')
• 'I'm standing' → 立っている (tatteiru, from 立つ/tatsu, 'to stand')
• 'I'm waiting' → 待っている (matteiru, from 待つ/matsu, 'to wait')

Note: In casual Japanese, ている contracts to てる: 泣いてる (naiteru), 立ってる (tatteru). This contraction is very common in anime dialogue and song lyrics.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: cry → I'm crying / Japanese: 泣く (naku, 'to cry') → 泣いている (naiteiru, 'am crying') → 泣いてる (naiteru, casual)

meaning.en: want to keep (-ている + たい)
aesthetics; a personal code of beauty

translations.en: Too dazzling — but I want to keep looking. I sense something of an aesthetic in it.

translations.pt-BR: Ofuscante demais — mas quero continuar olhando. Sinto uma espécie de estética aí.

translations.en: I chase, and keep chasing, the back of a dream that looks like no one else's.
translations.es: Persigo, y sigo persiguiendo, la espalda de un sueño que no se parece al de nadie.
translations.pt-BR: Corro atrás, e continuo correndo, da silhueta de um sonho que não se parece com o de ninguém.

literal_meaning.en: 'to-no-one not-resembling dream of back [obj] chasing, keep-chasing.' 〜背中を追う = idiomatic 'chase after [someone/something]'.

cultural_context.en: 夢の背中を追いかける (chasing the back of a dream) is a classic J-pop image — the dream is personified as someone walking ahead; you follow.

translations.en: A burning feeling that seems to call the dawn awake.
translations.es: Un sentimiento ardiente que parece despertar el amanecer.
translations.pt-BR: Um sentimento ardente que parece acordar o amanhecer.

literal_meaning.en: 'dawn [obj] call-awaken like-that burning feeling.' キモチ in katakana is a stylized version of 気持ち — common in pop lyrics.

translations.en: I don't care about consequences right now — anything beats boring time,
translations.es: Ahora no me importan las consecuencias — cualquier cosa es mejor que tiempo aburrido,
translations.pt-BR: Agora eu não ligo pras consequências — qualquer coisa é melhor que tempo entediante,

literal_meaning.en: 'consequences or-anything now [topic] don't-know, boring time than.' アトサキ literally 'after-before' = 'implications'.

cultural_context.en: アトサキ (後先) written in katakana for emphasis — literally 'after-before', meaning 'consequences, what comes from and after an action'. Dismissing it = 'live now, think later'.

translations.en: — until I have the dramatic firmly in hand. Believe in wonderland!

literal_meaning.en: 'dramatic hand in put until.' 手に入れる = set idiom 'get hold of / obtain'.

translations.en: You brush off mountains of problems with a light kind of vibe.

literal_meaning.en: 'piled-high of problems [obj] light-ish of mood with brush-off-[regret-tinged].' 〜ちゃう is colloquial 〜てしまう = 'do completely / end up doing'.

translations.en: There's no going back on this road — that's your pride, isn't it?
translations.es: Este camino no tiene vuelta — es tu orgullo, ¿no?

literal_meaning.en: 'this road [topic] can't-go-back, you of pride is [confirm].' 戻れない is the negative potential of 戻る.

translations.en: On nights when trouble keeps coming and you feel weak, I'll hold you tight.
translations.es: En las noches llenas de problemas, cuando te sientes frágil, te abrazo fuerte.
translations.pt-BR: Nas noites em que tudo dá errado e você fica fraco, eu te abraço apertado.

literal_meaning.en: 'trouble streak faint-hearted night [topic] tightly hug-give-for-you [emph].' 〜てあげる = 'do X for someone's benefit'.

translations.en: I catch, and keep catching, the shape of a dream no one else can see.
translations.es: Atrapo, y sigo atrapando, la forma de un sueño que nadie más puede ver.
translations.pt-BR: Eu capturo, e continuo capturando, a forma de um sonho que ninguém mais vê.

literal_meaning.en: 'to-anyone not-seen dream of shape [obj] catching keep-catching.'

translations.en: I'll follow you — because of this burning feeling.
translations.es: Yo te sigo — por este sentimiento ardiente.
translations.pt-BR: Vou te seguir — por esse sentimento ardente.

literal_meaning.en: 'I [topic] follow-go because, hot feeling.' ついて行く = 'go along with / follow'.

translations.en: I don't particularly need things to add up neatly — anything beats everyday routine,
translations.es: No necesito especialmente que todo cuadre — cualquier cosa es mejor que el día a día de siempre,
translations.pt-BR: Não preciso que tudo faça sentido — qualquer coisa é melhor que a rotina comum,

literal_meaning.en: 'coherence-fitting particularly don't-need, commonplace everyday than.' 辻褄を合わせる = 'make things add up'; here 合わせ stands alone as a noun.

cultural_context.en: 辻褄 (tsujitsuma) is written in katakana to feel breezy/rebellious. The set phrase 辻褄が合う / 辻褄を合わせる = 'logically consistent / make consistent' — rejecting 'ツジツマ合わせ' is refusing to rationalize.

translations.en: — aim for paradise, run! Believe in wonderland!
translations.es: — apunta al paraíso, ¡corre! Believe in wonderland!
translations.pt-BR: — mire no paraíso, corra! Believe in wonderland!

literal_meaning.en: 'paradise aiming-for run!' 走れ is the imperative of 走る.

grammar_points.name: 〜ても / 〜てもかまわない (te mo / te mo kamawanai: even if / don't mind even if)

explanation.en:
〜ても after a verb te-form = 'even if (X)'. Add かまわない / いい for 'it doesn't matter even if / it's fine even if'.

From this song: 嘲ってもかまわない = 'I don't mind even if (someone) mocks'.

More examples:
• 失敗してもかまわない (it's okay to fail)
• 行ってもいい？(Can I go?)
• 雨が降っても行く (I'll go even if it rains)

grammar_points.name: 〜せる / 〜させる (causative: make someone do)

explanation.en:
Causative suffix attaches to the negative stem of a verb. Godan → 〜せる; ichidan → 〜させる. Means 'make/let X do'.

From this song: キラめかせる = '(something) makes X sparkle' — causative of キラめく.

More examples:
• 子供を寝させる (put the child to bed)
• 彼を待たせる (make him wait)
• 花を咲かせる (make flowers bloom)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: キラめく → キラめか (neg. stem) + せる → キラめかせる

grammar_points.name: 〜過ぎる (sugiru: too much)

explanation.en:
Attaches to the stem of a verb or adjective to mean 'too (X)'. い-adjective: drop い + 過ぎる; な-adjective: drop な + 過ぎる.

From this song: 眩し過ぎ = 'too dazzling' (truncated 眩し過ぎる).

More examples:
• 食べ過ぎる (eat too much)
• 高すぎる (too expensive)
• 静かすぎる (too quiet)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 眩しい → 眩し + 過ぎる → 眩し過ぎる

grammar_points.name: 〜ような / 〜ように (you na / you ni: like / as if)

explanation.en:
Draws a comparison — 'like / resembling / in the manner of'. ような modifies a noun; ように modifies a verb or clause.

From this song: 夜明けを呼び覚ますような燃えるキモチ = 'a burning feeling like one that calls the dawn'.

More examples:
• 夢のような日 (a dream-like day)
• 泣いているように見える (looks as if crying)
• 鳥が飛ぶように (like a bird flies)

grammar_points.name: 〜ていく / 〜てくる (te iku / te kuru: progressive aspect)

explanation.en:
〜ていく after a verb's te-form = 'go on Xing / progress away from now'. 〜てくる = 'come toward / start happening'.

From this song:
• 追いかけてく (contracted 追いかけていく) = 'keep chasing (into the future)'
• つかまえてく = 'keep catching'

More examples:
• 変わっていく (gradually change)
• 雨が降ってくる (rain starts coming down)
• 年を取っていく (age gradually)

grammar_points.name: 〜ちゃう / 〜てしまう (chau / te shimau: do completely / end up doing)

explanation.en:
Attach to the te-form of a verb to express completion or an unintended result. 〜てしまう is the formal version; 〜ちゃう is its colloquial contraction.

From this song: かわしちゃう = 'brush (it) off (completely / casually)'.

More examples:
• 食べちゃう (eat up)
• 忘れちゃった (ended up forgetting)
• 行っちゃえ (just go already)

grammar_points.name: 〜てあげる (te ageru: do X for someone)

explanation.en:
Attach to the te-form of a verb to express doing the action for someone else's benefit. The speaker is the giver of the action.

From this song: 抱いてあげるよ = 'I'll hold you (for your sake)'.

More examples:
• 教えてあげる (I'll teach you)
• 手伝ってあげる (I'll help)
• 買ってあげる (I'll buy it for you)

Note: can sound condescending if used to superiors — use 〜てくれる / 〜てさしあげる depending on direction.

grammar_points.name: Imperative (〜え / 〜ろ: blunt command)

explanation.en:
The blunt imperative form: godan verbs end in 〜e (走る → 走れ); ichidan verbs end in 〜ろ (食べる → 食べろ). Used in songs for punch; in real life it's quite rough.

From this song: 走れ = 'Run!'.

More examples:
• 急げ (hurry up)
• 信じろ (believe)
• 食べろ (eat!)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 走る → 走れ

translations.en: No matter what time it is —
translations.es: No importa el momento —
translations.pt-BR: Não importa o momento —

literal_meaning.en: 'What-kind-of time even.' どんな〜だって is a fixed pattern: 'no matter what (X)'. The line opens the song as an unconditional promise.

cultural_context.en: Hikari (光, 'Light') is the Japanese theme song of Kingdom Hearts (2002). The English version 'Simple and Clean' became a global gaming anthem; the original Japanese is softer, more intimate — about partnership, not just adventure.

translations.en: all by myself,
translations.es: completamente sola,
translations.pt-BR: completamente sozinha,

literal_meaning.en: 'Only one-person with.' たった一人 = 'just one and only' — emphatic 'all alone'.

translations.en: I'd been forgetting fate,
translations.es: olvidé el destino,
translations.pt-BR: esqueci o destino,

literal_meaning.en: 'Fate forgetting.' Te-form chains into the next verse. 運命忘れて (with the を particle dropped colloquially) = 'forgetting fate / putting destiny aside'.

meaning.en: have been living (生きる + 〜てくる perfective)

translations.en: and I'd been living that way — yet,
translations.es: y había vivido así — y sin embargo,
translations.pt-BR: e vinha vivendo desse jeito — e mesmo assim,

literal_meaning.en: 'Living-came although.' 〜てくる as a perfect: 'have come to (do X) up to now'. のに sets up the contrast — 'I'd been managing alone, BUT...'.

translations.en: in a sudden burst of light, I open my eyes —
translations.es: en medio de una luz repentina, abro los ojos —
translations.pt-BR: no meio de uma luz repentina, eu acordo —

literal_meaning.en: 'Sudden of light of inside, eyes [subj] wake.' 目が覚める ('eyes wake') is the standard idiom for waking up. 突然の光 = 'a sudden light' (with の linking adverb to noun).

translations.en: in the middle of the night.
translations.es: en plena medianoche.
translations.pt-BR: no meio da noite.

literal_meaning.en: 'Midnight at.' 真夜中 = 真 (deep) + 夜中 (middle of night) — the very deepest hour.

translations.en: Standing quietly at the exit,
translations.es: De pie, en silencio, junto a la salida,
translations.pt-BR: Em pé, em silêncio, na saída,

literal_meaning.en: 'Quietly exit at standing.' Te-form chains forward. 静かに sets the cinematic mood — the singer poised on a threshold.

translations.en: fire light into the darkness!
translations.es: ¡dispara luz a la oscuridad!
translations.pt-BR: dispare luz na escuridão!

literal_meaning.en: 'Darkness into light [obj] fire!' 撃つ specifically means 'to shoot (a gun, an arrow)'. The bare imperative 撃て gives the line a battle-cry edge — uncharacteristic for an Utada ballad.

translations.en: These days, things like 'promises' —
translations.es: Hoy en día, cosas como las "promesas" —
translations.pt-BR: Hoje em dia, coisas como "promessas" —

literal_meaning.en: 'These-days promise things-like.' なんて dismissively introduces 約束 — 'promises and so on'. Sets up the next verse's hesitation.

meaning.en: to make (someone do); cause (causative of する)

translations.en: do they just make us anxious, I wonder?
translations.es: ¿no será que solo nos ponen ansiosos?
translations.pt-BR: será que só servem pra deixar a gente ansiosa?

literal_meaning.en: 'Anxious make-do only I-wonder.' 不安にさせる = causative 'make (someone) anxious'. 〜だけ + かな = 'I wonder if it's just (X)'.

meaning.en: into (here in idiom 口にする)
want to do (たい-form of する)

translations.en: I just want to put the wish into words, that's all.
translations.es: Solo quiero ponerle palabras al deseo, nada más.
translations.pt-BR: Eu só quero pôr o desejo em palavras, é só isso.

literal_meaning.en: 'Wish [obj] mouth into want-to-do only [emph].' 口にする = 'to mention; to put into words'. だけ + さ = 'it's just only X' — defensive softening.

translations.en: I'll introduce you to my family, you know.
translations.es: Te voy a presentar a mi familia, ¿sabes?
translations.pt-BR: Vou te apresentar para a minha família, viu.

literal_meaning.en: 'Family to-also introduce [emph].' にも = 'to (the family) too / even'. 紹介する is the suru-verb 'to introduce'.

translations.en: It'll all work out, for sure.
translations.es: Saldrá todo bien, seguro.
translations.pt-BR: Vai dar tudo certo, com certeza.

literal_meaning.en: 'Surely well-go [emph].' うまくいく is one of Japanese's most useful idioms — '(things) go smoothly / work out'.

meaning.en: two people; the two of us

translations.en: the two of us, all along.
translations.es: los dos, siempre juntos.
translations.pt-BR: nós dois, sempre juntos.

literal_meaning.en: 'All-along two-people with.' Closes the first chorus — completes the v1 'no matter what time it is' with 'we'll be together'.

meaning.en: side; near (also read がわ for 'side of')

translations.en: I'll be by your side, so —
translations.es: Voy a estar a tu lado, así que —
translations.pt-BR: Vou estar do seu lado, então —

literal_meaning.en: 'Near at to-be because.' 側にいる = 'to be near (someone)'. The clause-final から carries the implied promise — 'so don't worry'.

meaning.en: called; named (X-という-Y = 'a Y called X')

translations.en: the light called 'you' will find me
translations.es: la luz llamada "tú" me va a encontrar
translations.pt-BR: a luz chamada "você" vai me encontrar

literal_meaning.en: 'You called light [subj] me [obj] find.' 君という光 — the noun phrase 'the light that is you'. 〜という is how Japanese names or defines: 'a Y called X'.

cultural_context.en: 君という光 is the song's emotional centre — and the title's grammatical reverse. The light isn't somewhere out there; it's the other person.

translations.en: Heading into the noisy street,
translations.es: Entrando a una calle ruidosa,
translations.pt-BR: Entrando numa rua barulhenta,

literal_meaning.en: 'Noisy street into entering.' Te-form chains into v18. The image: a quiet inner moment opening onto the loud public world.

meaning.en: take it off! (imperative of 取る)

translations.en: take off the mask of fate!
translations.es: ¡quítate la máscara del destino!
translations.pt-BR: tira a máscara do destino!

literal_meaning.en: 'Fate of mask [obj] take-off!' Bare imperative とれ. 仮面をとる is a direct translation of 'remove the mask' — drop the pretense.

meaning.en: doing too much (する + 過ぎ)

translations.en: Things like over-anticipating —
translations.es: Eso de andar adelantando todo —
translations.pt-BR: Esse negócio de ficar antecipando demais —

literal_meaning.en: 'Reading-ahead of doing-too-much things-like.' 先読み = literally 'reading what comes ahead' — predicting outcomes. The dismissive なんて scoffs at it.

translations.en: let's stop with the things that are pointless.
translations.es: dejemos de hacer cosas sin sentido.
translations.pt-BR: vamos parar com as coisas que não fazem sentido.

literal_meaning.en: 'Meaning of nothing thing [topic] stop.' 意味のない = 'meaningless / pointless'. Te-form 止めて without ください — soft request.

translations.en: Today, let's just eat something delicious.
translations.es: Hoy, vamos a comer algo rico.
translations.pt-BR: Hoje, vamos comer uma coisa gostosa.

literal_meaning.en: 'Today [topic] delicious things [obj] let's-eat [emph].' Volitional + よ adds gentle insistence. The line lands as the song's quiet philosophy: skip the existential dread, share a meal.

cultural_context.en: This verse is famous — it captures Utada's signature trick of placing a deeply ordinary line ('let's eat something good') against a cosmic backdrop. The mundane act becomes the act of love.

translations.en: The future's still way ahead.
translations.es: El futuro aún está muy adelante.
translations.pt-BR: O futuro ainda está bem mais à frente.

literal_meaning.en: 'Future [topic] way-ahead is [emph].' ずっと先 = 'far far ahead'. Implied: don't try to plan it all now.

meaning.en: I don't know (negative of 分かる)

translations.en: Even I don't know what comes.
translations.es: Ni yo sé lo que viene.
translations.pt-BR: Nem eu sei o que vem.

literal_meaning.en: 'I to-also don't-know.' 〜にも = 'even to (X)'. The speaker admits to not knowing — paired with 'so let's not worry about planning the future right now'.

translations.en: Don't try to finish it all,
translations.es: No intentes terminarlo todo,
translations.pt-BR: Não tente concluir tudo,

literal_meaning.en: 'Completion don't-make-do.' 完成させる is causative 'to make (X) be completed' — to wrap up. 〜ないで is 'please don't'.

meaning.en: (let's) make it better (te-form of 良くする)

translations.en: let's keep making it better.
translations.es: vamos haciéndolo mejor.
translations.pt-BR: vamos continuar deixando melhor.

literal_meaning.en: 'More make-good.' 良くする is i-adj 良い + する → 'to make (X) good'. Te-form 良くして acts as a soft request.

translations.en: Filming one scene at a time —
translations.es: Filmando una escena a la vez —
translations.pt-BR: Filmando uma cena de cada vez —

literal_meaning.en: 'One-scene each filming.' ずつ = 'X at a time / X each'. 撮る is the verb specifically for taking photos or filming.

translations.en: all we have to do is go on like that.
translations.es: basta con que sigamos así.
translations.pt-BR: basta a gente seguir assim.

literal_meaning.en: 'Go-if good because.' 〜ばいい = 'it's enough to / all (one) needs to do is'. Closes the sentence: '(filming one scene at a time), going like that is fine'.

meaning.en: to project; cast onto (映す + 出す)

translations.en: the light called 'you' projects my screenplay.
translations.es: la luz llamada "tú" proyecta mi guion.
translations.pt-BR: a luz chamada "você" projeta o meu roteiro.

literal_meaning.en: 'You called light [subj] my of script project-out.' 映し出す = 映す ('to project') + 出す ('to put out') — to cast onto a screen, vividly.

translations.en: Let's talk more —
translations.es: Hablemos más —
translations.pt-BR: Vamos conversar mais —

literal_meaning.en: 'More let's-talk [emph].' Volitional 話そう (from 話す) + よ — gentle persuasion.

translations.en: about tomorrow, right around the corner,
translations.es: sobre el mañana que está a la vuelta,
translations.pt-BR: sobre o amanhã, ali na esquina,

literal_meaning.en: 'Right-in-front of tomorrow of things-also.' 目前 (literally 'before the eyes') = 'imminent / about to happen'. ことも links to v29 — '(let's talk) about tomorrow's things, too'.

translations.en: switch off the TV,
translations.es: apaga la tele,
translations.pt-BR: desliga a TV,

literal_meaning.en: 'TV turn-off.' Te-form as soft imperative — '(please) turn off the TV'. The most domestic, intimate image of the song.

meaning.en: stay watching (request: te-form of 見ている + よ)

translations.en: and look at only me.
translations.es: y mírame solo a mí.
translations.pt-BR: e olha só pra mim.

literal_meaning.en: 'Me of things only [obj] keep-watching [emph].' 〜のこと is the standard way to refer to a person in casual speech ('matters concerning X'). 見ていて = 'keep watching' (te-form of continuous 見ている).

translations.en: No matter how good (anything) is,
translations.es: Por más buena que sea cualquier cosa,
translations.pt-BR: Por mais boa que seja qualquer coisa,

literal_meaning.en: 'How-much good-even-if.' 〜たって is the colloquial collapse of 〜ても. 良くたって = 良くても = 'even if it's good'. どんなに stacks 'no matter how'.

meaning.en: can't fully believe (信じる + 〜きれない)

translations.en: I can't quite bring myself to believe it.
translations.es: no termino de creérmelo.
translations.pt-BR: não consigo acreditar de verdade.

literal_meaning.en: 'Believe-cannot-completely [agree].' 〜きれない negates 〜きる ('do completely') → 'cannot do (X) all the way'. The line lands as half-confession, half-shared knowledge.

translations.en: Even at moments like those —
translations.es: Incluso en esos momentos —
translations.pt-BR: Mesmo em momentos assim —

literal_meaning.en: 'Such time even.' Variation on v1's どんな時だって — 'even (in moments) like THAT'. The chorus comes back with promise.

grammar_points.name: 〜だって (even; no matter)

explanation.en:
〜だって is the colloquial collapse of だ + って, used to mean 'even (X)' or 'no matter (X)'. After question words like どんな or いつ, it forms unconditional concessions: 'no matter what time / no matter what kind'.

This song opens with どんな時だって ('no matter what time it is') and echoes it later as そんな時だって ('even at moments like that'). Both function as openers to a promise: I'll be there.

Distinguish from だって as 'because' (sentence-initial, casual reason) and だって as 'X also (does)' (after a noun). Other typical examples: 誰だって知ってる ('everyone knows'), 雨の日だって出かける ('I go out even on rainy days'), 冬だって泳ぐ ('I swim even in winter'), どこだって行く ('I'll go anywhere').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: noun / question word + だって; for verbs/adjectives use 〜たって (verb-past + たって)

grammar_points.name: 〜なんて (dismissive 'things like')

explanation.en:
なんて attaches to a noun or verb to introduce something dismissively — 'things like (X)' or 'such a (X)'. It carries a tone of 'pfft, that's not worth much'. With negative predicates it intensifies the dismissal.

This song uses it in 約束なんて ('promises and the like') and 先読みのし過ぎなんて ('over-anticipating things and that'). Both phrases scoff at the named thing before the song moves toward what matters more.

Distinguish from なんて as 'how (X)!' (exclamation) and なんて as 'what?'. Other typical examples: お金なんていらない ('I don't need money or anything'), 嘘なんて言わない ('I'd never lie'), 結婚なんて考えていない ('I'm not even thinking about marriage'), 怖いなんて思わない ('I don't think it's scary at all').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: noun / verb (plain form) + なんて

grammar_points.name: Bare imperative — 撃て, とれ

explanation.en:
Japanese has a stark imperative form for direct commands. Group 1 verbs shift -u to -e (撃つ → 撃て, 取る → とれ). Group 2 verbs shift -る to -ろ. Irregulars: する → しろ, 来る → 来い.

This song fires off two bare imperatives in surprising places — 暗闇に光を撃て ('fire light into the darkness!') and 運命の仮面をとれ ('take off the mask of fate!'). The form is uncharacteristically rough for Utada's intimate style; it cuts through the song's quietness with sudden urgency.

Other typical examples: 待て ('wait!'), 見ろ ('look!'), 頑張れ ('do your best!'), 行け ('go!'), 来い ('come here!').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: Group 1: -u → -e (撃つ → 撃て); Group 2: -る → -ろ; する → しろ, 来る → 来い

grammar_points.name: 〜きれない (can't fully / can't completely)

explanation.en:
〜きれない is the negative of 〜きる. The suffix 切る (kiru) attached to a verb's i-stem means 'do (X) completely / through to the end'; negating it (〜きれない) means 'cannot do (X) fully'.

This song uses 信じきれない ('can't quite bring myself to believe'). The form is gentler than 信じられない ('can't believe at all') — the speaker isn't denying belief, just admitting they can't go all the way.

Other typical examples: 食べきれない ('I can't finish eating'), 数えきれない ('countless'), 言いきれない ('I can't say definitively'), 待ちきれない ('I can't wait any longer').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (i-stem) + きれない (negative of 〜きる)

grammar_points.name: 〜という (X called Y; the X that is Y)

explanation.en:
X + という + Y is the standard pattern for 'a Y called X' or 'the Y that is X'. The という comes from と (quotative) + 言う ('to say') — literally 'a Y said-to-be-X'. Used to define, name, or appose.

This song features it twice in the chorus's emotional core: 君という光 ('the light called you / the light that is you'). The construction equates 'you' with 'light' through という — a bold poetic merger.

Other typical examples: 田中という人 ('a person named Tanaka'), 愛という言葉 ('the word called love'), 時間という宝 ('the treasure that is time'), 桜という花 ('the flower called sakura').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: noun X + という + noun Y

grammar_points.name: 〜ばいい (it's enough to / all you have to do is)

explanation.en:
〜ばいい combines the conditional 〜ば with いい ('good') to express 'it's enough / sufficient to (do X)' or 'all (one) needs to do is (X)'. Often used to suggest a course of action without forcing it.

This song uses it in ワンシーンずつ撮っていけばいいから ('all we have to do is keep filming one scene at a time'). The 〜ばいいから adds 'so don't worry' to the suggestion.

Other typical examples: わからなければ聞けばいい ('if you don't understand, just ask'), 嫌ならやめればいい ('if you don't like it, just quit'), 早く寝ればいい ('all you have to do is go to bed early'), 自分のやりたいようにやればいい ('just do it however you want').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (conditional 〜ば) + いい

explanation.en: Verb te-form + も means 'even if X' / 'even though X'. 揺さぶっても聴こえない 'even if I shake it, I can't hear'. The negative version is 〜なくても 'even if not'.
explanation.es: Forma -te del verbo + も significa 'aunque X'. 揺さぶっても聴こえない 'aunque lo sacuda, no se oye'. La forma negativa es 〜なくても.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma -te do verbo + も significa 'mesmo se X' / 'mesmo que X'. 揺さぶっても聴こえない 'mesmo se eu sacudir, não consigo ouvir'. A negativa é 〜なくても.

explanation.en: Verb -a-stem + ずに is the literary equivalent of 〜ないで ('without doing'). ため息も出ずに = 'without even a sigh coming out'. する → せずに (irregular). Common in songs and formal writing.
explanation.es: Raíz -a del verbo + ずに es el equivalente literario de 〜ないで ('sin hacer'). ため息も出ずに = 'sin que salga ni un suspiro'. する → せずに (irregular).
explanation.pt-BR: Radical -a do verbo + ずに é equivalente literário de 〜ないで ('sem fazer'). ため息も出ずに = 'sem nem um suspiro sair'. する → せずに (irregular).

explanation.en: Group-1: -u → -areru (洗い流す → 洗い流される). Group-2: -る → -rareru (止める → 止められる). Past: 〜された / 〜られた. Lyrics often use the passive to describe things done to the speaker — 洗い流された衝動 'the impulse that was washed away'.
explanation.es: Grupo 1: -u → -areru (洗い流す → 洗い流される). Grupo 2: -る → -rareru. Pasado: 〜された / 〜られた. Las letras suelen usar la pasiva para cosas hechas al narrador.
explanation.pt-BR: Grupo 1: -u → -areru (洗い流す → 洗い流される). Grupo 2: -る → -rareru. Passado: 〜された / 〜られた. Letras costumam usar a passiva para coisas feitas ao narrador.

explanation.en: Group-1: -u → -e (走り出す → 走り出せ 'start running!'). Group-2: -る → -ろ (覚ます → 覚ませ for Group-1; 食べる → 食べろ). A blunt command — used in lyrics for force; rude in everyday conversation.
explanation.es: Grupo 1: -u → -e (走り出す → 走り出せ '¡echa a correr!'). Grupo 2: -る → -ろ. Orden directa — usada en letras; grosera en conversación normal.
explanation.pt-BR: Grupo 1: -u → -e (走り出す → 走り出せ 'comece a correr!'). Grupo 2: -る → -ろ. Comando direto — usado em letras; grosseiro no dia a dia.

grammar_points.name: 〜ままに (just as, in the manner of)

explanation.en: Verb (plain) + ままに means 'just as / in the manner of'. 思うままに 'just as I feel'; 気の向くままに 'as the mood takes me'. Conveys spontaneity — doing X without filtering or planning.
explanation.es: Verbo (forma simple) + ままに significa 'tal como / al gusto de'. 思うままに 'como siento'; 気の向くままに 'según el ánimo'. Sugiere espontaneidad.
explanation.pt-BR: Verbo (forma simples) + ままに significa 'tal como / da maneira que'. 思うままに 'como sinto'; 気の向くままに 'como o humor me leva'. Ideia de espontaneidade.

explanation.en: 〜ていた contracts to 〜てた in casual speech and lyrics — describing an ongoing past state or action. 重なってた 'was overlapping', 強がってた 'was acting tough', 見守ってた 'was watching over'. Drop the い for the casual form.
explanation.es: 〜ていた se contrae a 〜てた en el habla casual y en letras — describe estado o acción continuos en pasado. 重なってた 'se estaba superponiendo', 強がってた 'me hacía el fuerte'. Cae la い en la forma casual.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜ていた contrai para 〜てた no falar casual e em letras — descreve estado ou ação contínuos no passado. 重なってた 'estava se sobrepondo', 強がってた 'estava bancando o forte'. Cai o い na forma casual.

grammar_points.name: 〜ながら (while doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: ながら (nagara) attaches to a verb's masu-stem to express doing two actions simultaneously: 'while doing X, also doing Y.'

Example from this song: 揺らめきながら (yurameki nagara) = 'while flickering' — from 揺らめく (yurameku, 'to flicker') → 揺らめき (yurameki, stem) + ながら (nagara)

More examples:
• 音楽を聴きながら勉強する (ongaku o kiki nagara benkyou suru, 'study while listening to music')
• 歩きながら話す (aruki nagara hanasu, 'talk while walking')
• 泣きながら笑う (naki nagara warau, 'laugh while crying')

Note: The main action is the second verb (after ながら). The ながら verb is the background/simultaneous action. Both actions are done by the same person.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 揺らめく (yurameku, 'to flicker') → 揺らめき (yurameki, stem) + ながら (nagara, 'while') → 揺らめきながら (yurameki nagara, 'while flickering')

grammar_points.name: 〜ていく (continuing/progressing)

explanation.en:
How it works: ていく (te iku) expresses an action or change that continues from now into the future, or progresses away from the current point.

Example from this song: 変えていった (kaete itta) = 'kept changing (over time)' — from 変える (kaeru, 'to change') → 変えて (kaete) + いった (itta, past of iku)

More examples:
• 成長していく (seichou shite iku, 'keeps growing') — from 成長する (seichou suru, 'to grow')
• 忘れていく (wasurete iku, 'gradually forgetting') — from 忘れる (wasureru, 'to forget')
• 強くなっていく (tsuyoku natte iku, 'getting stronger and stronger')

Note: ていく = future/away direction. てくる = past-to-present/toward direction. Past tense ていった means this progression happened over time in the past.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 変える (kaeru, 'to change') → 変えて (kaete) → 変えていった (kaete itta, 'kept changing over time')

grammar_points.name: 〜としても (even if)

explanation.en:
How it works: としても (to shite mo) means 'even if' or 'even assuming that.' It presents a hypothetical condition and says the result holds regardless.

Example from this song: The song uses としても to express that even in a hypothetical worst case, something still holds true.

More examples:
• 雨だとしても行く (ame da to shite mo iku, 'I'll go even if it rains')
• 失敗したとしても後悔しない (shippai shita to shite mo koukai shinai, 'even if I fail, I won't regret it')
• 嘘だとしても嬉しい (uso da to shite mo ureshii, 'even if it's a lie, I'm happy')

Note: としても is more formal/hypothetical than ても. ても is 'even if (it happens),' while としても is 'even assuming/supposing that.'

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb/noun + としても (to shite mo, 'even assuming that')

grammar_points.name: 〜かな (I wonder)

explanation.en:
How it works: かな (kana) is a sentence-ending particle expressing wondering or uncertainty. It's like thinking out loud: 'I wonder if...'

Example from this song: The song uses かな to express the singer's inner wondering and uncertainty about a situation.

More examples:
• 大丈夫かな (daijoubu kana, 'I wonder if it's OK')
• 明日は晴れるかな (ashita wa hareru kana, 'I wonder if it'll be sunny tomorrow')
• 好きなのかな (suki na no kana, 'I wonder if I like them')

Note: かな is softer and more introspective than か (ka, question marker). It's used for self-directed wondering, not direct questions to others. Very common in songs for expressing inner thoughts.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: plain form + かな (kana, 'I wonder')

grammar_points.name: 〜次第 (depends on; up to)

explanation.en:
How it works: 次第 (shidai) after a noun means 'depends on' or 'up to.' It indicates that the outcome is determined by the stated factor.

Example from this song: 自分次第 (jibun shidai) = 'up to myself / depends on me' — from 自分 (jibun, 'oneself') + 次第 (shidai)

More examples:
• 天気次第 (tenki shidai, 'depends on the weather') — from 天気 (tenki, 'weather')
• やり方次第 (yarikata shidai, 'depends on how you do it') — from やり方 (yarikata, 'method')
• 気持ち次第 (kimochi shidai, 'depends on your feelings') — from 気持ち (kimochi, 'feelings')

Note: Noun + 次第 is a very empowering expression. 自分次第 means 'it's all up to me' — a common motivational phrase. 次第 can also mean 'as soon as' with verb stems: 届き次第 (todoki shidai, 'as soon as it arrives').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 自分 (jibun, 'oneself') + 次第 (shidai, 'depends on') → 自分次第 (jibun shidai, 'up to myself')

grammar_points.name: 〜たら (if/when conditional)

explanation.en:
How it works: たら (tara) is a conditional meaning 'if' or 'when.' Form it by adding ら to the past tense (ta-form) of a verb or adjective.

Example from this song: 埋められたら (umeraretara) = 'if I could fill (the gap)' — from 埋める (umeru, 'to fill') → potential: 埋められる (umerareru) → past: 埋められた (umerareta) + ら (ra)

More examples:
• 食べたら (tabetara, 'if/when you eat') — from 食べる (taberu, 'to eat')
• 安かったら買う (yasukattara kau, 'if it's cheap, I'll buy it') — from 安い (yasui, 'cheap')
• 暇だったら来て (hima dattara kite, 'if you're free, come over') — from 暇 (hima, 'free')

Note: たら is the most versatile conditional — it works for hypothetical ('if'), temporal ('when'), and counterfactual ('if only'). It's often the safest conditional to use when unsure.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 埋める (umeru, 'to fill') → 埋められる (umerareru, potential) → 埋められた (umerareta, past) + ら (ra) → 埋められたら (umeraretara, 'if I could fill')

translations.en: Before you go far away —
translations.es: Antes de que te vayas lejos —
translations.pt-BR: Antes que você vá para longe —

literal_meaning.en: 'Far to go-away before.' 〜てしまう adds 'regretfully / completely' to a verb. 〜前に attaches to plain-form verb to mean 'before (X-ing)'.

cultural_context.en: Harukaze (春風, 'spring wind') is the Bleach OP 15 by SCANDAL (2012). The song is a soft farewell-and-rebirth — petals scattering on the wind as a long arc closes.

meaning.en: I have to tell (you) (colloquial 〜なきゃ contraction)

translations.en: Even as I tell myself I have to tell you,
translations.es: Aunque pienso "tengo que decírtelo",
translations.pt-BR: Mesmo pensando "preciso te contar",

literal_meaning.en: 'Must-tell [quotative] thinking-while.' 〜なきゃ is the colloquial collapse of 〜なければ(ならない) — 'have to / must'. The と marks the inner thought.

translations.en: today's time slips by once again.
translations.es: el tiempo de hoy pasa una vez más.
translations.pt-BR: o tempo de hoje passa mais uma vez.

literal_meaning.en: 'Today also passes-going time.' 〜てゆく (literary 〜ていく) projects passage into the future. 過ぎてゆく時間 = 'time that flows on past me'.

meaning.en: laughing together (te-form of 笑い合う)

translations.en: Laughing together, my heart aches just a little.
translations.es: Riendo juntos, me duele el pecho un poquito.
translations.pt-BR: Rindo juntos, meu peito dói só um pouquinho.

literal_meaning.en: 'Laughing-together, a-little chest hurting.' 〜合う suffix on a verb stem = 'doing together / mutually'. 胸を痛める = 'to be heartsick'.

translations.en: On a night when the spring wind blew,
translations.es: Una noche en que soplaba el viento de primavera,
translations.pt-BR: Numa noite em que o vento da primavera soprava,

literal_meaning.en: 'Spring-wind [subj] blow night.' 春風が吹く is a relative clause modifying 夜 — 'a night (in which) the spring wind blows'.

meaning.en: 'I don't want us to part' (inner thought)

translations.en: "I don't want to part with you," I thought —
translations.es: "No quiero separarme", pensé —
translations.pt-BR: "Não quero me afastar", pensei —

literal_meaning.en: 'Want-to-part-not [emph] [quotative].' 〜たくない is the negative of the desiderative 〜たい. なあ adds wistful self-talk. って is colloquial と (quotative).

translations.en: Thinking things like that,
translations.es: Pensando cosas así,
translations.pt-BR: Pensando coisas assim,

literal_meaning.en: 'Such things [obj] thinking.' そんな事 = 'such matters / things like that'. The te-form leaves the sentence open into the next verse.

meaning.en: couldn't manage to say (potential negative + なる + te-form)

translations.en: I somehow ended up even less able to say it.
translations.es: Y, no sé, me costó aún más poder decirlo.
translations.pt-BR: Aí, sei lá, fiquei menos capaz ainda de dizer.

literal_meaning.en: 'Somehow all-the-more couldn't-say became.' 言える is the potential 'can say'; 言えない negates it; + なる = 'come to not be able to say'.

translations.en: Saying "See you tomorrow" — and saying goodbye,
translations.es: Diciendo "hasta mañana" — y despidiéndome,
translations.pt-BR: Dizendo "até amanhã" — e me despedindo,

literal_meaning.en: 'Tomorrow [emph] [quotative] goodbye doing.' さよならする = 'to say goodbye'. The mismatch between casual 「明日ね」 and the weight of さよなら makes the line ache.

translations.en: Walking alone beneath the row of trees,
translations.es: Caminando sola bajo la hilera de árboles,
translations.pt-BR: Caminhando sozinha debaixo das árvores enfileiradas,

literal_meaning.en: 'Alone walk tree-row of under at.' 並木 is a specific word for the lined-up trees of an avenue — typical of Tokyo's cherry-blossom streets in spring.

translations.en: I suddenly think — the traces of a dream.
translations.es: De pronto pienso — las huellas de un sueño.
translations.pt-BR: De repente penso — os vestígios de um sonho.

literal_meaning.en: 'Suddenly think dream of trace.' 夢の跡 ('the trace of a dream') is a literary phrase from Bashō's haiku about ruined battlefields ('夏草や兵どもが夢の跡').

cultural_context.en: 夢の跡 is a famous phrase from Matsuo Bashō: 夏草や 兵どもが 夢の跡 ('Summer grass — all that's left of the warriors' dream'). Borrowing it gives this pop song a quiet literary weight.

meaning.en: to flutter down (舞う + 落ちる)
flutter-flutter (gitaigo for thin things in air)

translations.en: Petals fluttering down, flutter-flutter —
translations.es: Pétalos cayendo flotando, ondulando —
translations.pt-BR: Pétalas caindo dançantes, flutuando —

literal_meaning.en: 'Flutter-fall petals flutter-flutter.' ヒラヒラ mimics light, thin objects (paper, cloth, petals) drifting in the air.

meaning.en: heart (心 written in katakana for tone)
slips through (contracted すり抜けていく)

translations.en: slipping through the cracks of my heart.
translations.es: colándose por las grietas de mi corazón.
translations.pt-BR: passando pelas frestas do meu coração.

literal_meaning.en: 'Heart of gap slip-through-go.' すり抜ける = すり (sliding) + 抜ける (pass through). The 〜てく contraction makes the slipping ongoing/forward.

meaning.en: have to become (colloquial of ならなければ)

translations.en: I have to be honest about it.
translations.es: Tengo que ser sincera.
translations.pt-BR: Eu preciso ser sincera.

literal_meaning.en: 'Honest become-must.' 素直になる = 'to become honest / open'. なんなきゃ is the colloquial collapse of ならなければ — a strong 'must'.

meaning.en: even if it strikes (te-form of 襲う + も)

translations.en: No matter what kind of pain hits my heart again,
translations.es: Pase lo que pase, no importa qué dolor vuelva a azotar mi corazón,
translations.pt-BR: Não importa que dor venha de novo atacar meu coração,

literal_meaning.en: 'What-kind-of pain [subj] again, my heart strike-even-if.' 〜ても is the concessive 'even if'. どんな〜が〜ても = 'whatever (X) does to me'.

meaning.en: shut tight (passive past of 閉ざす)

translations.en: I'll go see what's beyond
translations.es: Voy a ver lo que hay más allá
translations.pt-BR: Vou ver o que há além

literal_meaning.en: 'Shut-tight door of.' 閉ざす is a literary intransitive 'to shut firmly' — stronger than 閉める. The verse continues into v17.

translations.en: of that tightly-shut door — I'm going.
translations.es: de esa puerta cerrada — voy a ir.
translations.pt-BR: daquela porta fechada — eu vou.

literal_meaning.en: 'Other-side [obj] go-to-see [emph].' 〜にいく chain = 'go (in order) to (do X)'. The clause-final から here doesn't mark 'because' but adds firm assertive — 'so I will, mark my words'.

translations.en: Two people who were complete opposites,
translations.es: Dos personas que eran totalmente opuestas,
translations.pt-BR: Duas pessoas que eram totalmente opostas,

literal_meaning.en: 'Completely opposite of two-people.' まるで is an intensifier — here it strengthens 正反対 ('exact opposite'). The line stands alone as a noun phrase.

translations.en: but somehow — when we're together, before I knew it —
translations.es: pero quién sabe por qué — cuando estamos juntos, sin que me dé cuenta —
translations.pt-BR: mas, sei lá por quê — quando estamos juntos, sem eu perceber —

literal_meaning.en: 'But why-it-is, together be when, before-I-knew.' 〜と as a conditional means 'when / whenever (X)'. いつの間にか = 'in some span of time I didn't notice'.

translations.en: the bits where we're alike kept growing, didn't they?
translations.es: fueron creciendo las cosas en que nos parecemos, ¿verdad?
translations.pt-BR: foram aumentando as coisas em que somos parecidos, né?

literal_meaning.en: 'Resemble bits also increased [agree].' 似ているところ → 似てるとこ — colloquial drops both い and the formal ろ. ね seeks agreement.

meaning.en: had been imitating each other (真似 + 〜合う + ていた)

translations.en: ...or so (we said) — but really, we were copying each other a little.
translations.es: ...pero, en realidad, nos estábamos imitando un poco.
translations.pt-BR: ...mas, na real, a gente estava se imitando um pouco.

literal_meaning.en: 'Such-things really [topic] a-little imitate-mutually-was.' 真似する = 'to imitate'; 〜合う = 'to do together / mutually'; 〜ていた = past continuous.

translations.en: On the night you were crying,
translations.es: La noche en que llorabas,
translations.pt-BR: Na noite em que você chorava,

literal_meaning.en: 'You [subj] was-crying night.' 泣いてた = 泣いていた contracted. The whole clause modifies 夜 as a relative clause.

translations.en: I wiped your tears.
translations.es: Te sequé las lágrimas.
translations.pt-BR: Eu enxuguei suas lágrimas.

literal_meaning.en: 'I [topic] tears [obj] wiped.' Plain past sentence — direct, intimate.

meaning.en: nodding to each other (te-form of うなずき合う)

translations.en: Nodding lightly to each other —
translations.es: Asintiendo levemente uno al otro —
translations.pt-BR: Concordando levemente um com o outro —

literal_meaning.en: 'Easily nod-mutually-and.' 〜合う suffix once again — both people doing the same gesture together.

translations.en: I noticed the future I'd been running from —
translations.es: Me di cuenta del futuro del que estaba huyendo —
translations.pt-BR: Percebi o futuro do qual eu estava fugindo —

literal_meaning.en: 'Run-away future to notice.' 逃げる未来 = 'a future (one is) running from' — relative clause. 〜に気が付く = 'to notice / become aware of (X)'.

translations.en: Gazing at the unchanging you,
translations.es: Mirando fijamente al tú que no cambia,
translations.pt-BR: Encarando você, que segue igual,

literal_meaning.en: 'Doesn't-change you [obj] gaze-and.' 変わらないキミ = 'the you who doesn't change' — present-tense relative clause.

meaning.en: let's leave (it) behind (置く + ていく volitional)

translations.en: I decided to leave the memories behind.
translations.es: Decidí dejar atrás los recuerdos.
translations.pt-BR: Decidi deixar as lembranças para trás.

literal_meaning.en: 'Memories [topic] leave-go [quotative] decided.' Volitional + と + 決める = 'decide that (one) will (do X)'. The volitional acts as the inner thought.

translations.en: Sorry — I'm going on ahead now.
translations.es: Perdón — me adelanto.
translations.pt-BR: Desculpa — vou na frente agora.

literal_meaning.en: 'Sorry, now ahead to go [emph].' 先に行く is the formula said when leaving before someone — at work, on a date, on a journey. Loaded with farewell weight here.

translations.en: Petals fluttering down, swaying-swaying —
translations.es: Pétalos cayendo, meciéndose —
translations.pt-BR: Pétalas caindo dançantes, balançando —

literal_meaning.en: 'Flutter-fall petals sway-sway.' Variant of v12 — same sentence, ヒラヒラ replaced by ユラユラ. The shift suggests a slower, more deliberate motion.

meaning.en: stay holding (te-form of 繋いでいる, contracted; soft request)

translations.en: Keep holding my swaying heart —
translations.es: Sigue sosteniendo este corazón que tiembla —
translations.pt-BR: Continue segurando esse coração que treme —

literal_meaning.en: 'Sway heart, holding-be (please).' 繋いでて is 繋いでいて contracted — 'stay holding'. Used as a soft imperative 'please keep doing X'.

translations.en: so that I don't forget,
translations.es: para no olvidar,
translations.pt-BR: para não esquecer,

literal_meaning.en: 'Forget-not so-that.' 〜ないように = 'so that (X) doesn't happen' — purpose clause attached to a negative.

meaning.en: to start walking (歩く + 出す inceptive)

translations.en: I set my dreams and wishes on the spring wind, and I start walking.
translations.es: Pongo mis sueños y deseos en el viento de primavera, y empiezo a caminar.
translations.pt-BR: Coloco meus sonhos e desejos no vento da primavera, e começo a andar.

literal_meaning.en: 'Spring-wind on dream and wish [obj] load, start-walking.' 〜出す attached to a verb stem = 'start (doing X)' suddenly. The closing image: setting hopes adrift on the wind to journey on.

translations.en: Hey — lift up your face,
translations.es: Oye — levanta la cara,
translations.pt-BR: Ei — levanta o rosto,

literal_meaning.en: 'Hey, face [obj] lift.' 顔をあげる is the literal 'raise one's face' — lift one's eyes from the ground. Common idiom for 'cheer up / look ahead'.

translations.en: so that we can laugh side by side again.
translations.es: para que podamos volver a reír uno al lado del otro.
translations.pt-BR: para que possamos rir lado a lado de novo.

literal_meaning.en: 'Again next-to at can-laugh so-that.' 笑える is the potential of 笑う ('to laugh'); 〜ように with potential = purpose 'so that one can'.

translations.en: No one is really strong, you know.
translations.es: Nadie es realmente fuerte, ¿sabes?
translations.pt-BR: Ninguém é forte de verdade, sabe.

literal_meaning.en: 'Anyone strong things-like is-not (it's that).' なんて attached to an i-adj stem dismissively + ない = 'isn't anything like (X)'. Confessional tone.

translations.en: Being alone is scary — me too.
translations.es: Estar solo da miedo — a mí también.
translations.pt-BR: Estar sozinho dá medo — comigo também.

literal_meaning.en: 'Alone if uneasy is [emph], I-even so.' 〜だって = 'even (X) is the same way' — admitting shared vulnerability. The whole verse is the emotional core.

translations.en: (So that) the future I believed in
translations.es: (Para que) el futuro en el que creí
translations.pt-BR: (Para que) o futuro em que acreditei

literal_meaning.en: 'Believed future [subj].' 信じた未来 — relative clause: 'the future (one) believed in'. Sentence trails into v38.

translations.en: may begin here, again.
translations.es: vuelva a comenzar, desde aquí.
translations.pt-BR: comece outra vez, daqui.

literal_meaning.en: 'Here-from again begin so-that.' Final 〜ように at the end of a sentence functions as a wish — 'may (X)'. Closes the song on a quiet prayer.

cultural_context.en: Sentence-final 〜ように without a main clause is a Japanese way of phrasing a wish or prayer (神様、〜ますように 'God, may it be that...'). Closes the song with the resigned hope of a Shinto prayer.

grammar_points.name: 〜なきゃ (colloquial 'have to / must')

explanation.en:
〜なきゃ is the colloquial collapse of 〜なければ(ならない/いけない) — 'must / have to'. It attaches to a verb's negative stem (drop い from 〜ない) plus 〜きゃ. The 'ならない' tail is dropped in casual speech, leaving the obligation implied.

This song uses it twice in close succession: 伝えなきゃ ('I have to tell you') and 素直になんなきゃ ('I have to be honest'). Both are inner thoughts — the speaker is talking to herself.

Note that ならない collapses to なんない (a dialectal/casual form), giving 素直になんなきゃ instead of 素直にならなきゃ. Other typical examples: 行かなきゃ ('I have to go'), 早く起きなきゃ ('I have to get up early'), 食べなきゃダメだよ ('you have to eat').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (negative stem 〜ない, drop い) + きゃ; full form: 〜なければ(ならない)

grammar_points.name: 〜ながら (while doing)

explanation.en:
〜ながら attaches to a verb's i-stem (連用形) to express two simultaneous actions or states by the same subject: 'doing X while doing Y'. The main action is in the second clause; ながら marks the secondary, ongoing action.

This song uses it in 伝えなきゃと思いながら ('while thinking I have to tell you'), pairing the inner monologue with the outer action of letting time slip by.

Other typical examples: 音楽を聴きながら勉強する ('to study while listening to music'), 笑いながら泣く ('to laugh and cry at once'), 歩きながら話す ('to talk while walking'), 涙を流しながら謝った ('she apologised in tears').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (i-stem / 連用形) + ながら

grammar_points.name: Volitional + と思う / と決める (decide that I will...)

explanation.en:
Verb in volitional form (〜よう/〜う) + と + 思う ('think') or 決める ('decide') expresses an inner resolve: 'I think I'll (do X)' or 'I decided to (do X)'. The volitional acts as quoted direct thought.

This song uses it in 思い出は置いていこうと決めた ('I decided I'll leave the memories behind'). The volitional 置いていこう encodes the speaker's willed plan; と marks it as quoted thought; 決めた seals the decision.

Other typical examples: 日本に行こうと思う ('I'm thinking of going to Japan'), 早く寝ようと決めた ('I decided to go to bed early'), 諦めようと思った ('I thought about giving up'), 結婚しようと決めた ('we decided we'd get married').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (volitional 〜よう/〜う) + と + 思う / 決める / する (try to)

grammar_points.name: 〜ても / 〜でも (even if; even when)

explanation.en:
Adding も to a verb's te-form creates the concessive 'even if (X)'. Often pairs with question words (どんな, 何, 誰) to express 'no matter what / whoever / however'.

This song uses どんな痛みがまた 僕のココロ襲っても ('no matter what kind of pain hits my heart again'). The どんな〜が〜ても construction creates an unconditional concession — the speaker promises to act regardless of what comes.

Other typical examples: 雨が降っても行く ('I'll go even if it rains'), 高くても買う ('I'll buy it even if it's expensive'), 誰が反対しても決めた ('I've decided no matter who objects').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (te-form) + も; i-adj (-くて) + も = -くても; na-adj/noun + でも

grammar_points.name: 〜ように (so that / may it be that)

explanation.en:
〜ように has two main uses: (1) attached mid-sentence, it marks purpose — 'so that (X) happens'; (2) at the end of a sentence, it expresses a wish or prayer — 'may it be that (X)'.

This song uses both forms. Mid-sentence purposes: 忘れないように ('so that I don't forget'), 笑えるように ('so that we can laugh'), 始まるように ('so that it begins'). The closing line of the song — ここからまた 始まるように — uses the wish form: 'may it begin here, again' as a quiet final prayer.

Other typical examples: 遅れないように出発する ('to leave so as not to be late'), 風邪をひかないように ('so as not to catch a cold'), 元気でありますように ('may you be well'), 雨が降りませんように ('please don't let it rain').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (plain form, often potential or negative) + ように

grammar_points.name: 〜って (casual quotative)

explanation.en:
って is the colloquial spoken form of the quotative particle と. It can mark direct quotes, reported speech, or even topics (like a casual は). In song lyrics it's especially common because it lets singers slip in spoken words mid-line without breaking flow.

This song uses it twice in the verse-2 stanza: 「離れたくないなあ」って ('thinking 'I don't want to part''), 「明日ね」って さよならして ('saying 'see you tomorrow' as goodbye'). Both are inner-thought / spoken-word quotes; って lets the singer attribute them.

って can also mean 'they say that' (rumor) or replace は in casual definitions: 田中さんって優しい人だ ('Tanaka is a kind person'). Other typical examples: 行くって言ったよ ('she said she'd go'), 何って言うの? ('what are you saying?'), 月曜日って忙しい ('Mondays are busy, you know').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: any quoted phrase + って (replaces formal と)

grammar_points.name: 〜のように見える (no you ni mieru: looks like)

explanation.en:
How it works: のように見える (no you ni mieru) means 'looks like' or 'appears to be.' It combines the comparison pattern のように (no you ni, 'like') with 見える (mieru, 'to be visible/appear').

Example from this song: 山のように見える (yama no you ni mieru) = 'looks like a mountain' — comparing something's appearance to a mountain

More examples:
• 子供のように見える (kodomo no you ni mieru, 'looks like a child') — from 子供 (kodomo, 'child')
• 簡単なように見える (kantan na you ni mieru, 'looks easy') — from 簡単 (kantan, 'simple')
• 怒っているように見える (okotte iru you ni mieru, 'looks angry') — from 怒る (okoru, 'to get angry')

Note: のように is for nouns, なように is for na-adjectives, and plain form + ように is for verbs. 見える means something appears that way to the observer — it's not necessarily the truth.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 山 (yama, 'mountain') + の (no) + ように (you ni, 'like') + 見える (mieru, 'appears') → 山のように見える (yama no you ni mieru, 'looks like a mountain')

grammar_points.name: 〜のために (no tame ni: for the sake of)

explanation.en:
How it works: のために (no tame ni) means 'for the sake of' or 'for the benefit of.' After a noun, it expresses who or what something is done for.

Example from this song: 世のために人のために (yo no tame ni hito no tame ni) = 'for the world, for the people' — from 世 (yo, 'world') and 人 (hito, 'people')

More examples:
• 家族のために働く (kazoku no tame ni hataraku, 'work for the sake of family') — from 家族 (kazoku, 'family')
• 健康のために運動する (kenkou no tame ni undou suru, 'exercise for health') — from 健康 (kenkou, 'health')
• 将来のために勉強する (shourai no tame ni benkyou suru, 'study for the future')

Note: Noun + のために = 'for the sake of (noun).' Verb dictionary form + ために = 'in order to (do).' The first is about beneficiary, the second is about purpose.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 世 (yo, 'world') + の (no) + ために (tame ni, 'for the sake of') → 世のために (yo no tame ni, 'for the world')

grammar_points.name: 〜に敗れる (ni yabureru: to be defeated by)

explanation.en:
How it works: に敗れる (ni yabureru) means 'to be defeated by' or 'to lose to.' The particle に marks what defeated you, and 敗れる (yabureru) means 'to be defeated.'

Example from this song: 夢に敗れる (yume ni yabureru) = 'to be defeated by a dream / to have a dream crushed' — from 夢 (yume, 'dream')

More examples:
• 試合に敗れる (shiai ni yabureru, 'to lose the match') — from 試合 (shiai, 'match')
• 相手に敗れた (aite ni yabureta, 'was defeated by the opponent') — from 相手 (aite, 'opponent')
• 現実に敗れる (genjitsu ni yabureru, 'defeated by reality') — from 現実 (genjitsu, 'reality')

Note: 敗れる (yabureru) is more literary/formal than 負ける (makeru, 'to lose'). In songs and poetry, 夢に敗れる conveys having your dreams crushed or failing to achieve them.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 夢 (yume, 'dream') + に (ni, 'by') + 敗れる (yabureru, 'to be defeated') → 夢に敗れる (yume ni yabureru, 'defeated by a dream')

grammar_points.name: 〜たまに (tama ni: occasionally)

explanation.en:
How it works: たまに (tama ni) is an adverb meaning 'occasionally,' 'once in a while,' or 'from time to time.' It describes actions that happen infrequently.

Example from this song: 僕たまに (boku tama ni) = 'I sometimes...' — the speaker admits they occasionally do something

More examples:
• たまに映画を見る (tama ni eiga o miru, 'occasionally watch movies') — from 映画 (eiga, 'movie')
• たまには休もう (tama ni wa yasumou, 'let's rest once in a while') — with は for emphasis
• たまに会う友達 (tama ni au tomodachi, 'a friend I meet occasionally') — from 会う (au, 'to meet')

Note: Frequency scale: いつも (itsumo, 'always') > よく (yoku, 'often') > 時々 (tokidoki, 'sometimes') > たまに (tama ni, 'occasionally') > めったに〜ない (metta ni ~nai, 'rarely'). たまには (tama ni wa) with は is used for suggestions: 'for once, let's...'

grammar_points.conjugation_path: たまに (tama ni, 'occasionally') — adverb, placed before the verb
