translations.en: Here I come! Certain victory! Strongest in history!
translations.es: ¡He llegado! ¡Victoria asegurada! ¡El más fuerte de la historia!
translations.pt-BR: Cheguei! Vitória certa! O mais forte da história!

literal_meaning.en: Have-arrived! Certain-win! History-strongest!

cultural_context.en: 参上 ('san-jou') is the humble verb 'to arrive (before someone of higher rank).' Used here ironically as a battle cry — Saitama announcing himself as an underling-style entry. 史上最強 packs four kanji into 'strongest in all of history.'

translations.en: What's your problem?! Frustration! I don't stop!
translations.es: ¿Cuál es el problema?! ¡Frustración! ¡Yo no paro!
translations.pt-BR: Qual é a desse?! Frustração! Eu não paro!

literal_meaning.en: What is-it-saying! Frustration! I as-for, won't-stop!

cultural_context.en: 何だってんだ contracts 何だと言っているんだ ('what are you saying?'). Sounds growled. 俺 (ore) is rough masculine 'I' — a register choice that picks a fight before any verb arrives.

translations.en: ONE PUNCH! Done! Win after win!
translations.es: ONE PUNCH! ¡Completado! ¡Victorias en cadena!
translations.pt-BR: ONE PUNCH! Concluído! Vitórias em cadeia!

literal_meaning.en: One-punch, completed, consecutive-battles consecutive-wins

cultural_context.en: 連戦連勝 ('battle-after-battle, win-after-win') doubles the same construction (連〜連〜) for the militaristic feel of unbroken streaks. Common pattern: 連〜連〜 = 'X after X.'

translations.en: I am a war cry! I always win! Crushing victory!
translations.es: ¡Yo soy el grito de guerra! ¡Siempre gano! ¡Victoria aplastante!
translations.pt-BR: Eu sou o grito de guerra! Sempre venço! Vitória esmagadora!

literal_meaning.en: I as-for, KATSU! always win, crushing-victory

cultural_context.en: 喝 (katsu!) is the Zen master's shout used to break a student's mental block — yelling-as-teaching. Punning trick: 喝 (katsu shout) and 勝つ (katsu, to win) are homophones, so '俺は喝!' reads simultaneously as 'I am the shout' and 'I win.'

translations.en: Right up to the very limit
translations.es: Justo hasta el mismo límite
translations.pt-BR: Bem no limite, no limite

literal_meaning.en: Right-at-edge limit until

cultural_context.en: ギリギリ — onomatopoeia for 'just barely / right at the edge.' Stacked with 限界 ('limit'), it doubles the 'on the brink' feeling.

translations.en: Voices that praise me, applause and the like — I don't want any of it
translations.es: Voces que me elogian, ovaciones y demás — no las quiero, ¿eh?
translations.pt-BR: Vozes que me elogiam, ovação e essas coisas — não quero, viu

literal_meaning.en: Me (obj) praising voice or-such, applause-something-like, want-as-for-not-ze

cultural_context.en: 讃える ('to praise / extol' — written 称える or 賛える as well) is a more elevated word than 褒める ('praise'). The casual 〜なんて dismisses the listed items as unworthy. ぜ at sentence end is rough masculine emphasis — 'I'm telling you.'

translations.en: That's why I strike down evil where no one sees
translations.es: Por eso golpeo al mal sin que nadie me vea
translations.pt-BR: Por isso bato no mal sem ninguém ver

literal_meaning.en: So, person-not-knowing evil (obj) strike

cultural_context.en: 人知れず ('without people knowing' — bungo-style negative) is literary cousin of modern 人に知られないで. The kanji 人 acts as 'people' generally. This is Saitama's whole drama: he saves the world but stays invisible.

translations.en: Enemies pressing in, blanketing the sky — I will not turn my back
translations.es: Enemigos avanzando, tapando el cielo — no voy a darles la espalda
translations.pt-BR: Inimigos avançando, cobrindo o céu — não vou virar as costas

literal_meaning.en: Sky covering surge enemies, I as-for back (obj) turn-as-for-not-do

cultural_context.en: 天 normally read てん, here read そら ('sky') as a furigana stylization — kanji says 'heaven,' voice says 'sky.' 押し寄せる ('press-in-and-approach') is the verb for waves crashing or armies surging. The split-verb negation 向けはしない is emphatic refusal: 'turn? — that I will NOT do.'

translations.en: If I am a hero, I have forged an unshakable resolve — unleash the iron fist!
translations.es: Si soy un héroe, he forjado una resolución inquebrantable — ¡desata el puño de hierro!
translations.pt-BR: Se sou um herói, fixei uma resolução inabalável — desencadeia o punho de ferro!

literal_meaning.en: Hero if-be, unshakable-no resolve forged, unleash-imp. iron-fist

cultural_context.en: 揺ぎなき = 揺るぎ ('shaking, stem of 揺るぐ') + なき (literary 'no / without') = 'no-shaking,' modifying 覚悟. The 〜き / 〜なき endings are bungo (classical) attributive forms — modern equivalents are 〜い / 〜ない.

translations.en: Here I come! Go on! Fair and square!
translations.es: ¡Aquí estoy! ¡Go on! ¡Limpio y honesto!
translations.pt-BR: Cheguei! Go on! Limpo e honesto!

literal_meaning.en: Have-arrived! Go on! Right-right-noble-noble

cultural_context.en: 正々堂々 ('right-right-noble-noble') = 'with full integrity, no underhanded tricks.' Sports-anime staple yojijukugo. The doubling for emphasis (X-X-Y-Y) is a common four-character structure.

translations.en: What's the deal? I don't feel a thing. Ain't no enemies left
translations.es: ¿Qué pasa? No siento nada. Ya no quedan enemigos
translations.pt-BR: Mas que história é essa? Não sinto nada. Não tem mais inimigo

literal_meaning.en: How is-becoming-it-is? Nothing feel-not, no-longer enemy is-not

cultural_context.en: 感じねぇ = 感じない slurred to ねぇ. 居ねぇ = 居ない slurred. Rough masculine register replaces -ai endings with -ee — heard in shounen anime, yakuza films, and tough-guy speech. Captures Saitama's bored disappointment perfectly.

translations.en: JUSTICE! Execute! No discussion!
translations.es: ¡JUSTICE! ¡Ejecutar! ¡Sin discusión!
translations.pt-BR: JUSTICE! Em execução! Sem conversa!

literal_meaning.en: Justice, execute, question-answer-no-need

cultural_context.en: 問答無用 ('Q&A useless') = 'no point arguing, action time.' Used by samurai-era authority figures and modern action heroes alike to shut down debate before a fight.

translations.en: I win! Sever evil! Hands together — a prayer for the dead
translations.es: ¡Yo gano! ¡Corto el mal! ¡Manos juntas — descansen en paz!
translations.pt-BR: Eu venço! Corto o mal! Mãos juntas — paz aos defuntos

literal_meaning.en: I (subj) win, evil (obj) sever, hands-together

cultural_context.en: 合掌 ('hands together') is the Buddhist gesture of prayer or thanks — placed at the end of a ritual, often in funerals. Saying 合掌 over a defeated enemy = 'rest in peace, bro.'

translations.en: Adrenaline overflowing — let it rip! Land the technique you trained!
translations.es: Adrenalina desbordándose — ¡suéltala! ¡Aplica la técnica entrenada!
translations.pt-BR: Adrenalina transbordando — solta tudo! Manda a técnica treinada!

literal_meaning.en: Adrenaline start-overflow-ze, trained technique (obj) ram-imp.

cultural_context.en: ブチかます is slang from boxing/sumo — 'land a hit so hard it overwhelms.' Imperative 〜かませ adds the urgency. 鍛える ('to forge / train,' as a blade is forged) frames the body as a weapon.

translations.en: No matter how strong a guy is — they were once just a tiny kid
translations.es: Por más fuerte que sea un tipo — alguna vez fue un mocoso pequeño
translations.pt-BR: Não importa quão forte seja o cara — todos foram pirralhos

literal_meaning.en: However-much strong guy-also, tiny brat was-it-is

cultural_context.en: ちっぽけ (chippoke) ='tiny / insignificant,' a casual expressive word. ガキ (gaki) is rough slang for 'kid/brat' — registers don't get more masculine-rough. やつ ('guy / dude') matches the energy.

translations.en: Hero — overcoming the weak self, becoming strong
translations.es: Héroe — superando al yo débil, haciéndose fuerte
translations.pt-BR: Herói — superando o eu fraco, tornando-se forte

literal_meaning.en: Weak-classical self, overcome, strong-become

cultural_context.en: 弱き is the bungo attributive form of 弱い ('weak') — modern: 弱い. 己 (onore) is the formal/literary 'self' (more elevated than 自分). Both choices push the line toward 'samurai-philosophy' register.

translations.en: Holding up a fist where a god dwells, I just charge forward
translations.es: Alzando un puño donde habita un dios, yo solo sigo adelante
translations.pt-BR: Erguendo o punho onde mora um deus, eu só sigo em frente

literal_meaning.en: God-dwell fist hoisting, I as-for, charge-only-sa

cultural_context.en: 神宿る ('god-dwells-in') is a literary attributive — verb directly modifying noun. 拳 (kobushi) is the more dignified word for 'fist' (vs. 拳骨 'genkotsu'). 掲げる ('to hoist a flag/banner') gives the fist banner-energy.

translations.en: A hero — fighting until the day he tastes the mud of defeat
translations.es: Un héroe — luchando hasta el día en que pruebe el barro de la derrota
translations.pt-BR: Um herói — lutando até o dia em que provar a lama da derrota

literal_meaning.en: Someday defeat-by mud lick until, fight

cultural_context.en: 汚泥を舐める ('to lick the filthy mud') = the idiom 'to taste defeat / to be humiliatingly beaten.' Saitama's whole arc is the search for this experience — he's bored with always winning. The verb-clause + まで construction means 'until the action happens.'

translations.en: I won't give up — drawing tomorrow on this chest
translations.es: No me rindo — dibujando el mañana en este pecho
translations.pt-BR: Eu não desisto — desenhando o amanhã neste peito

literal_meaning.en: I as-for, give-up-not, that chest-on future (obj) draw

cultural_context.en: 未来 normally read みらい, here read あす ('tomorrow') — a furigana stylization (kanji says 'future,' voice says 'tomorrow'). Singer Endoh Masaaki of JAM Project is famous for this kind of layered meaning.

translations.en: Toward an awakening world, now — soar! Strong and high!
translations.es: Hacia un mundo que despierta, ahora — ¡vuela! ¡Fuerte y alto!
translations.pt-BR: Rumo a um mundo que desperta, agora — voa! Forte e alto!

literal_meaning.en: Awakening-go world toward, now, soar-imp. strong high

cultural_context.en: 舞い上がる ('dance-rise' = soar / take wing) — combines 舞う ('dance') and 上がる ('rise'). The imperative 舞い上がれ commands the verb. 目覚めゆく uses the literary 〜ゆく for 〜いく.

translations.en: At any time — no matter what happens
translations.es: En cualquier momento — pase lo que pase
translations.pt-BR: Em qualquer hora — aconteça o que acontecer

literal_meaning.en: Any-kind-of time even, anything (subj) even-if-being

cultural_context.en: Stock duo of concessive clauses, parallel-built: どんな時でも (any-time-even) + 何があっても (anything-be-even-if). Together they cover 'every conceivable situation.'

tokens.romaji: I wanna be the SAIKYOU Hero
tokens.reading: アイワナビーザサイキョーヒーロー
tokens.surface: I wanna be the SAIKYOU Hero

translations.en: A lonely hero — I wanna be the SAIKYOU (strongest) Hero!
translations.es: Un héroe solitario — I wanna be the SAIKYOU (el más fuerte) Hero!
translations.pt-BR: Um herói solitário — I wanna be the SAIKYOU (mais forte) Hero!

literal_meaning.en: Lonely hero, I wanna be the strongest hero

cultural_context.en: 孤独 (kodoku) is the song's quietest beat — the cost of strength is loneliness. The closing line code-switches into English with 最強 SAIKYOU dropped in untranslated, leaving the strongest word in Japanese exactly where it lands hardest.

meaning.es: el más fuerte de la historia

explanation.en: Compounds inherited from classical Chinese — fixed four-kanji units where each character contributes meaning. JAM Project leans hard on battle yojijukugo: 史上最強 ('history-on strongest' = strongest ever), 連戦連勝 ('consecutive-battle consecutive-win' = winning streak), 正々堂々 ('right-right noble-noble' = fair and square), 問答無用 ('Q&A useless' = no discussion), 圧勝 ('press-win' = crushing victory — two characters, but same construction). Common doubled patterns: X-X-Y-Y (正々堂々), X-A-X-B (連戦連勝), and antonym pairs (問答無用 sets question and answer as a unit, then dismisses it). Memorize as units, not character by character.
explanation.es: Compuestos heredados del chino clásico — unidades fijas de cuatro kanji donde cada carácter aporta significado. JAM Project se apoya en yojijukugo de batalla: 史上最強 ('en la historia, el más fuerte'), 連戦連勝 ('batallas en cadena, victorias en cadena'), 正々堂々 ('limpio y honesto'), 問答無用 ('sin preguntas, sin discusión'), 圧勝 ('victoria aplastante' — solo dos kanji, misma lógica). Patrones comunes: X-X-Y-Y (正々堂々), X-A-X-B (連戦連勝), y pares antónimos (問答無用). Memoriza como unidades, no kanji por kanji.
explanation.pt-BR: Compostos herdados do chinês clássico — unidades fixas de quatro kanji onde cada caractere contribui significado. JAM Project se apoia em yojijukugo de batalha: 史上最強 ('na história, o mais forte'), 連戦連勝 ('batalhas seguidas, vitórias seguidas'), 正々堂々 ('limpo e honesto'), 問答無用 ('sem perguntas, sem discussão'), 圧勝 ('vitória esmagadora' — só dois kanji, mesma lógica). Padrões comuns: X-X-Y-Y (正々堂々), X-A-X-B (連戦連勝), e pares antônimos (問答無用). Memorize como unidades, não kanji por kanji.

explanation.en: Bare imperative for godlike orders. u-verbs replace final -u with -e: 繰り出す → 繰り出せ ('unleash!'), 舞い上がる → 舞い上がれ ('soar!'), ブチかます → ブチかませ ('land it!'). ru-verbs replace -ru with -ろ: 食べる → 食べろ. The form is blunt — too rough for everyday requests but standard for shounen battle dialogue, dog commands, and shouted instructions. Softer alternatives: 〜なさい (mom-voice), 〜てください (polite ask).
explanation.es: Imperativo puro para órdenes de dios. Verbos-u cambian -u final por -e: 繰り出す → 繰り出せ ('¡desencadena!'), 舞い上がる → 舞い上がれ ('¡vuela!'), ブチかます → ブチかませ ('¡suéltalo!'). Verbos-ru cambian -ru por -ろ: 食べる → 食べろ. La forma es áspera — demasiado ruda para el día a día, pero estándar para batalla shounen, órdenes a perros e instrucciones a gritos. Alternativas suaves: 〜なさい (voz de madre), 〜てください (petición cortés).
explanation.pt-BR: Imperativo puro para ordens de deus. Verbos-u trocam -u final por -e: 繰り出す → 繰り出せ ('desencadeia!'), 舞い上がる → 舞い上がれ ('voa!'), ブチかます → ブチかませ ('manda!'). Verbos-ru trocam -ru por -ろ: 食べる → 食べろ. A forma é seca — rude demais pro dia a dia, mas padrão pra batalha shounen, comando a cachorro e instrução berrada. Alternativas suaves: 〜なさい (voz de mãe), 〜てください (pedido educado).

grammar_points.name: Masculine register: 俺, ぜ, ねぇ contractions

explanation.en: Japanese encodes social register tightly into pronouns and sentence-final particles. 俺 (ore) is rough masculine 'I' — distinct from polite 私 (watashi) and softer 僕 (boku). Sentence-final ぜ adds masculine emphatic confidence ('I'm telling you'). The vowel shift -ai → -ee turns standard endings into rough/blue-collar speech: ない → ねぇ (感じない → 感じねぇ), 居ない → 居ねぇ. Heard everywhere in shounen anime, yakuza films, and Tokyo working-class speech.
explanation.es: El japonés codifica el registro social en los pronombres y partículas finales. 俺 (ore) es 'yo' masculino áspero — distinto del polite 私 (watashi) y el suave 僕 (boku). La partícula final ぜ añade énfasis masculino confiado. El cambio vocálico -ai → -ee convierte terminaciones estándar en habla áspera: ない → ねぇ (感じない → 感じねぇ), 居ない → 居ねぇ. Omnipresente en shounen, películas de yakuza y habla obrera de Tokio.
explanation.pt-BR: O japonês codifica registro social nos pronomes e partículas finais. 俺 (ore) é 'eu' masculino bruto — distinto do polido 私 (watashi) e do suave 僕 (boku). A partícula final ぜ adiciona ênfase masculina confiante. A mudança vocálica -ai → -ee transforma terminações padrão em fala bruta: ない → ねぇ (感じない → 感じねぇ), 居ない → 居ねぇ. Onipresente em shounen, filmes de yakuza e fala operária de Tóquio.

explanation.en: Particle attached to nouns or verb-dictionary forms to mean 'something like ~ / ~ and the like.' Distinctive feature: tone of dismissal or surprise. Listing X with なんて downgrades it: 喝采なんて欲しくはない ('applause and the like? — don't want it'). Compare neutral 喝采は欲しくない ('I don't want applause') vs scornful 喝采なんて欲しくない. Often pairs with surprised reaction: 'できるなんてすごい!' ('the fact that you can do it is amazing!').
explanation.es: Partícula unida a sustantivos o verbos en forma de diccionario con sentido 'algo como ~ / ~ y demás'. Marca: tono de desprecio o sorpresa. Listar X con なんて lo rebaja: 喝采なんて欲しくはない ('ovación y esas cosas — no la quiero'). Compara neutro 喝采は欲しくない vs. despectivo 喝采なんて欲しくない. Frecuente en reacción de sorpresa: 'できるなんてすごい!' ('¡que puedas hacerlo es increíble!').
explanation.pt-BR: Partícula ligada a substantivos ou verbos na forma de dicionário com sentido 'algo como ~ / ~ e tal'. Marca: tom de desdém ou surpresa. Listar X com なんて desvaloriza: 喝采なんて欲しくはない ('ovação e essas coisas? — não quero'). Compare neutro 喝采は欲しくない vs. desdenhoso 喝采なんて欲しくない. Frequente em reação surpresa: 'できるなんてすごい!' ('o fato de você conseguir é incrível!').

explanation.en: まで attaches not just to nouns ('until tomorrow') but also to whole verb-dictionary clauses to mean 'until V happens.' 敗北に汚泥舐めるまで = 'until I taste the mud of defeat.' The verb stays in the plain dictionary form before まで. Sets up an enduring action that won't stop until the V-clause becomes true.
explanation.es: まで se une no solo a sustantivos ('hasta mañana') sino a cláusulas enteras con verbo en forma de diccionario para 'hasta que V ocurra'. 敗北に汚泥舐めるまで = 'hasta que pruebe el barro de la derrota'. El verbo permanece en forma de diccionario antes de まで. Establece una acción prolongada que no se detiene hasta que la cláusula V se cumpla.
explanation.pt-BR: まで se liga não só a substantivos ('até amanhã') como a cláusulas inteiras de verbo na forma de dicionário com sentido 'até V acontecer'. 敗北に汚泥舐めるまで = 'até provar a lama da derrota'. O verbo fica na forma de dicionário antes de まで. Estabelece uma ação prolongada que não para até a cláusula V se tornar verdadeira.

explanation.en: Bungo (classical) attributive endings preserved in literary style. 〜き is the classical adjective attributive (modern 〜い): 弱き己 = 弱い己 ('weak self'). 〜なき is the literary 'without ~' or 'no ~' (modern 〜のない / 〜のない): 揺ぎなき覚悟 = 揺るぎのない覚悟 ('unshakable resolve'). Sprinkled into modern lyrics for samurai-style gravitas — using them everywhere would sound stilted, but a single 〜き or 〜なき per verse signals 'this is heroic register.'
explanation.es: Terminaciones atributivas del bungo (clásico) preservadas en estilo literario. 〜き es el atributivo clásico del adjetivo (moderno 〜い): 弱き己 = 弱い己. 〜なき es el 'sin ~' o 'no-~' literario (moderno 〜のない): 揺ぎなき覚悟 = 揺るぎのない覚悟 ('resolución inquebrantable'). Salpicados en letras modernas para gravitas samurái — usarlos siempre sonaría forzado, pero un 〜き o 〜なき por verso señala 'esto es registro heroico'.
explanation.pt-BR: Terminações atributivas do bungo (clássico) preservadas no estilo literário. 〜き é o atributivo clássico do adjetivo (moderno 〜い): 弱き己 = 弱い己. 〜なき é o 'sem ~' ou 'não-~' literário (moderno 〜のない): 揺ぎなき覚悟 = 揺るぎのない覚悟 ('resolução inabalável'). Salpicados na letra moderna pra peso de samurai — usar sempre soaria forçado, mas um 〜き ou 〜なき por verso sinaliza 'isto é registro heróico'.

synced_lrc.text: 運命なんて知らないけど
この際 存在を認めざるを得ない
本当にこんな私でもいいの ねぇいいの
あんまり期待させないでほしいよ
今日という日は嘘偽りのない
永遠の誓い日和だよ
綺麗な花も証人もいらない

translations.en: I don't know about destiny or anything,
translations.es: No sé nada de destinos ni cosas así,
translations.pt-BR: Não sei de destino nem nada dessas coisas,

literal_meaning.en: 'fate or-anything don't-know though.' なんて dismisses 'fate' as a grand concept the speaker doesn't buy into.

meaning.en: in this case; given the situation

translations.en: — but now I really have to admit it exists.
translations.es: — pero ahora no me queda más que admitir que existe.
translations.pt-BR: — mas agora não tem jeito: preciso reconhecer que existe.

literal_meaning.en: 'in-this-case existence [obj] admit-cannot-but.' 〜ざるを得ない = 'have no choice but to (X)' — a formal reluctant-acceptance pattern.

cultural_context.en: 〜ざるを得ない is a formal/literary construction. Hearing it in a love song signals resigned acceptance — 'I didn't want to believe, but here we are'.

translations.en: Are you really sure I'm the one? I mean, really?
translations.es: ¿De verdad te sirvo una como yo? ¿En serio?
translations.pt-BR: Tem certeza de que sou eu mesmo? Sério?

literal_meaning.en: 'truly this-kind-of me even fine [question] hey fine [question].' こんな私でもいい = 'I'm okay even being (who I am)?' — a vulnerable tag.

translations.en: Don't make me hope too much, okay?
translations.es: No me hagas esperar demasiado, ¿vale?
translations.pt-BR: Não me faz esperar demais, tá?

literal_meaning.en: 'too-much expectation don't-make-do want [emph].' 〜させないでほしい = 'I want you not to cause X'.

translations.en: This day called today has no lies, no falsehood —
translations.es: Este día llamado hoy no tiene mentira ni falsedad —
translations.pt-BR: Este dia de hoje não tem mentira nem falsidade —

literal_meaning.en: 'today [called] day [topic] lies falsehood of without.' 嘘偽りのない = a set phrase = 'genuine, without lies or deception'.

translations.en: — a perfect day for an eternal vow.
translations.es: — un día perfecto para un juramento eterno.
translations.pt-BR: — um dia perfeito para um juramento eterno.

literal_meaning.en: 'eternity of vow weather-fit-for is [emph].' 〜日和 (biyori) = 'good weather/day for (X)' — e.g. お出かけ日和 = 'a lovely day for going out'. The song title 誓い (Chikai) hides in this line.

cultural_context.en: 誓い (chikai) is the song's title. 日和 turns it into 誓い日和 = 'a day perfect for vows' — a phrase made up for this song, playing on common patterns like 結婚日和 (wedding weather).

translations.en: No pretty flowers, no witnesses needed.
translations.es: No hacen falta flores lindas ni testigos.
translations.pt-BR: Não preciso de flores bonitas nem de testemunhas.

literal_meaning.en: 'beautiful flowers also, witnesses also, don't-need.' 〜も〜も〜ない = 'neither X nor Y'.

translations.en: Let's just wear matching rings.
translations.es: Pongámonos anillos del mismo color.
translations.pt-BR: Vamos só usar alianças da mesma cor.

literal_meaning.en: 'same color of ring [obj] let's-do.' 指輪をする = 'wear a ring'.

translations.en: It's so frustrating I can't stand it.
translations.es: Es tan frustrante que no lo soporto.
translations.pt-BR: É uma frustração que não dá pra suportar.

literal_meaning.en: 'frustrating, can't-be-helped.' 〜くて仕方がない = 'so X (that) I can't stand it'.

translations.en: Every day, I want to sleep clinging to you in a way that's almost embarrassing.
translations.es: Cada día quiero dormir aferrada a ti de un modo casi ridículo.
translations.pt-BR: Todo dia eu quero dormir agarrada a você de um jeito quase ridículo.

literal_meaning.en: 'uncool to-the-extent-of clung while-remaining want-to-sleep every-day.' 〜たまま = 'in the state of having X-ed'.

translations.en: I'm not making promises anymore.
translations.es: Ya no quiero hacer promesas.
translations.pt-BR: Não quero mais fazer promessas.

literal_meaning.en: 'promise [topic] no-longer don't-do.' 約束する vs 誓う — the song's thesis: promises are out, oaths are in.

translations.en: Those are just something we do to make someone happy.
translations.es: Esas son cosas que hacemos para complacer a alguien.
translations.pt-BR: Isso é só coisa pra agradar alguém.

literal_meaning.en: 'that-kind-of-thing, someone [obj] please for-sake of thing.' 喜ばす is the causative of 喜ぶ — 'make X happy'.

translations.en: What I'm saying now isn't something I picked up from somebody else.
translations.es: Lo que digo ahora no es nada que haya copiado de otra persona.
translations.pt-BR: O que eu digo agora não é repetição de ninguém.

literal_meaning.en: 'now say thing [topic] borrowed-opinion or-anything isn't.' 受け売り (ukeuri) = 'reselling' — reusing someone else's thoughts as one's own.

translations.en: It's not even a promise — it's an oath.
translations.es: No es ni siquiera una promesa — es un juramento.
translations.pt-BR: Não é nem promessa — é um juramento.

literal_meaning.en: 'promise even-isn't, vow is [emph].' 約束 ≠ 誓い — the song distinguishes: one can be broken, the other is absolute.

cultural_context.en: In Japanese, 約束 (yakusoku, 'promise') is an everyday commitment; 誓い (chikai, 'oath/vow') is weightier — reserved for wedding vows, sacred pledges. The song asserts its claim is the latter.

translations.en: I can't go back to the me who was a liar.
translations.es: No puedo volver a ser el mentiroso que era.
translations.pt-BR: Não posso mais voltar a ser o mentiroso que eu era.

literal_meaning.en: 'liar was me to-[contrastive] can't-go-back.' 嘘つきだった僕 = 'me, who was a liar' (noun-modifying copula clause).

translations.en: Let's go with sunrise-colored rings.
translations.es: Escojamos anillos del color del amanecer.
translations.pt-BR: Vamos escolher alianças da cor do nascer do sol.

literal_meaning.en: 'morning-sun color of ring [decide] let's-do.' X にする = 'decide on X / choose X'.

translations.en: Let's layer our pounding hearts and dance together.
translations.es: Superpongamos los latidos de nuestros pechos y bailemos.
translations.pt-BR: Vamos sobrepor as batidas do peito e dançar.

literal_meaning.en: 'chest of pounding [obj] layering, let's-dance [emph].' 重ねる = 'place on top / overlay', here metaphorically for two hearts beating in sync.

translations.en: Let's celebrate the fact of living in the now.
translations.es: Celebremos el hecho mismo de vivir el ahora.
translations.pt-BR: Vamos celebrar o simples ato de viver o agora.

literal_meaning.en: 'now [obj] live thing [obj] let's-celebrate [emph].' 〜ことを祝う = 'celebrate the act of (X)'.

translations.en: To these tears I sometimes can't hold back —
translations.es: A estas lágrimas que a veces no puedo contener —
translations.pt-BR: Por essas lágrimas que às vezes não consigo segurar —

literal_meaning.en: 'sometimes can't-hold-back-become tears to.' 堪える = 'endure, hold back' (as in tears); 〜られる negative potential + 〜くなる = 'become unable to'.

translations.en: — there isn't any deep meaning in particular.
translations.es: — no hay ningún significado profundo en particular.
translations.pt-BR: — não tem nenhum sentido profundo em especial.

literal_meaning.en: 'this-and-say deep meaning [topic] not-exist.' これと言って = 'nothing specifically to point to'.

translations.en: Just suddenly remembering the past — (oh, I want to cry) —
translations.es: Solo recordar el pasado de repente — (ah, quiero llorar) —
translations.pt-BR: Só me lembro do passado de repente — (ah, dá vontade de chorar) —

literal_meaning.en: 'just past [obj] suddenly remembering.' 突然 = 'abruptly'; 思い出す = V+V: 思う (think) + 出す (bring out).

translations.en: — light streaming in from an opened door.
translations.es: — luz que entra por la puerta que se ha abierto.
translations.pt-BR: — luz que se derrama pela porta aberta.

literal_meaning.en: 'was-opened door from streams-in light.' 差し込む = 'thrust in / penetrate' (of sunlight).

meaning.en: want to be (〜ている + たい)

translations.en: From now on too, I want to always stay by your side.
translations.es: De aquí en adelante, quiero estar siempre a tu lado.
translations.pt-BR: De agora em diante, quero ficar sempre do seu lado.

literal_meaning.en: 'from-now also always side at want-to-be.' いたい = いる + たい 'want to stay'.

translations.en: There's been no option for anything else, not for a long time now.
translations.es: La opción de otra cosa ya no existe, desde hace mucho.
translations.pt-BR: Opção já não existe há muito tempo.

literal_meaning.en: 'options or-anything already long-ago not-exist.' とっくに = 'well before now, long since'.

translations.en: This day called today is without precedent in history —
translations.es: Este día de hoy no tiene precedente en la historia —
translations.pt-BR: Este dia de hoje não tem precedente na história —

literal_meaning.en: 'today [called] day [topic] past precedent of without.' 過去前例 is a compound noun for 'historical precedent'.

translations.en: — a perfect day for our vow.
translations.es: — un día perfecto para nuestro juramento.
translations.pt-BR: — um dia perfeito para o nosso juramento.

literal_meaning.en: 'we of vow-weather is [emph].' Echoes verse 6; the second appearance personalizes the vow ('our' rather than 'eternal').

translations.en: Once isn't enough.
translations.es: Una vez no basta.
translations.pt-BR: Uma vez não basta.

literal_meaning.en: 'once in not-enough.' Response to the English line 'Kiss me once, kiss me twice'.

translations.en: Give me you.
translations.es: Dame a ti.
translations.pt-BR: Me dê você.

literal_meaning.en: 'you [obj] please-give.' 下さい usually attaches to a noun + を — here the object IS the beloved.

cultural_context.en: あなたを下さい is startlingly direct — normally a request concerns an object or a favor, not a person. The phrase feels both tender and claim-staking.

translations.en: Let's listen, shoulder to shoulder, to the sound of the sun rising.
translations.es: Escuchemos, hombro con hombro, el sonido del sol que amanece.
translations.pt-BR: Vamos ouvir, ombro a ombro, o som do sol nascendo.

literal_meaning.en: 'sun of rising sound [obj] shoulders lining-up, let's-listen.' 肩を並べる = set phrase 'stand shoulder-to-shoulder'.

translations.en: Let's vow to live together.
translations.es: Jurémonos vivir juntos.
translations.pt-BR: Vamos jurar viver juntos.

literal_meaning.en: 'together live thing [obj] let's-vow [emph].' 共に (literary) = 一緒に (colloquial). The song's final note lands on 誓 (vow) — its title.

grammar_points.name: 〜ざるを得ない (zaru wo enai: can't help but; have no choice but to)

explanation.en:
A formal/literary pattern meaning 'must, reluctantly / have no choice but to'. Attach to a verb's negative stem + ざる + を得ない. Irregular: する → せざる; 来る → 来ざる.

From this song: 認めざるを得ない = 'I have no choice but to admit it'.

More examples:
• 行かざるを得ない (no choice but to go)
• 同意せざるを得ない (must agree, reluctantly)
• 諦めざるを得ない (must give up)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 認める → 認め (neg. stem) + ざる + を + 得ない → 認めざるを得ない

grammar_points.name: 〜させないでほしい (sasenaide hoshii: I want you not to make me)

explanation.en:
Causative + negative te-form + ほしい = 'I want you not to cause X / I'd rather you didn't make me do X'.

From this song: あんまり期待させないでほしい = 'I don't want you to make me hope too much'.

More examples:
• 心配させないでほしい (I don't want to make you worry / Don't worry me)
• 泣かせないで (Don't make (me/her) cry)
• 困らせないで (Don't trouble me)

grammar_points.name: Volitional 〜(よ)う (ou / you: let's / I will)

explanation.en:
Attach to a verb to suggest 'let's (do X)'. Godan: drop 〜u, add 〜ou (しよう, 踊ろう). Ichidan: drop 〜る, add 〜よう (生きよう).

From this song:
• 指輪をしよう (let's wear rings)
• 祝おう (let's celebrate)
• 踊ろう (let's dance)
• 誓おう (let's vow)

More examples:
• 食べよう (let's eat)
• 頑張ろう (let's try our best)
• 行こう (let's go)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 祝う → 祝お + う → 祝おう

grammar_points.name: 〜たまま (ta mama: while still / in the state of)

explanation.en:
Attach 〜た (past) + まま to express 'while still X / in the state of having done X'.

From this song: しがみついたまま眠りたい = 'I want to sleep still clinging'.

More examples:
• 電気をつけたまま寝た (slept with the light still on)
• 立ったまま話す (speak while still standing)
• 靴を履いたまま (with shoes still on)

grammar_points.name: 〜くらい / 〜ぐらい (kurai / gurai: to the extent of)

explanation.en:
Attach to a verb/adjective/noun to express 'to the extent of / about / so much that'.

From this song: ダサいくらいしがみついた = 'clung so tight it was uncool'.

More examples:
• 泣くくらい嬉しい (so happy I could cry)
• 痛いくらい抱きしめる (hug so hard it hurts)
• 死ぬくらい疲れた (exhausted to the point of dying)

grammar_points.name: 〜でもない (de mo nai: not even / isn't)

explanation.en:
Attach 〜でもない after a noun to mean 'not even (X) / isn't (X)'. Often paired with 〜ではなく to contrast.

From this song: 約束でもない 誓いだよ = 'it's not even a promise — it's an oath'.

More examples:
• 嘘でもない (it's not a lie either)
• 大した話でもない (not much of a story)
• 誰でもない私 (me who is no one else)

grammar_points.name: 〜という (to iu: called / named / the one where)

explanation.en:
Attach to a noun to mean 'the X called / the X named / the fact of X'. Marks the identity or content of what precedes.

From this song: 今日という日 = 'this day called today / a day that is today'.

More examples:
• 田中という人 (a person called Tanaka)
• 愛という言葉 (the word "love")
• 合格したという知らせ (news that I passed)

translations.en: Start running — start running, hold your flag high in the sky.

literal_meaning.en: 'start-running, start-running, sky high, flag holding-up.' 走り出せ is the imperative of the compound 走り出す (start to run).

translations.en: Let's cross this endless sea and go search.

literal_meaning.en: 'endless this sea [obj] crossing, searching to let's-go [emph].' 〜に行く after a verb stem = 'go in order to (do)'.

translations.en: After the world's miracle that no one has yet been able to find,

literal_meaning.en: 'anyone still can't-find world of miracle [obj].' 見つけられる = potential/passive of 見つける.

translations.en: I'll just push forward as my racing heart tells me.
translations.es: Solo me abro paso, tal como me dicta el corazón que late fuerte.

literal_meaning.en: 'pounding chest, feelings as-they-are push-forward only.' 〜のまま = 'just as / in the state of X'.

translations.en: — following the footprints that dream-chasers leave behind.
translations.es: — siguiendo las huellas que dejan los cazadores de sueños.
translations.pt-BR: — seguindo as pegadas que os caçadores de sonhos deixam.

literal_meaning.en: 'dream-chase person [subj] leaves footprints [obj].' 夢追い人 is a compound: 夢 (dream) + 追う (chase) + 人 (person).

meaning.en: if we make (conditional of する)

translations.en: Any night of storms — if we make our hearts one,

literal_meaning.en: 'whatever storm of night even, heart one into if-make.' 心を一つにする = set idiom 'unite in spirit'.

translations.en: — we can get across, anytime.
translations.es: — podemos cruzarlo, en cualquier momento.

literal_meaning.en: 'crossing can-go-through, anytime.' 〜てゆける = literary 'can continue doing / can make it through'.

translations.en: There are tears I'll never show anyone, though —

translations.en: Chase, chase — the compass that points to the dream

translations.pt-BR: Corre atrás — a bússola que aponta pro sonho

literal_meaning.en: 'chasing, dream [obj] points-to compass [topic].' 指す can mean 'indicate / point at' (as a compass needle does).

translations.en: — is these unwavering eyes; I can't stop now.
translations.es: — son estos ojos decididos; no puedo detenerme.
translations.pt-BR: — são estes olhos firmes; não dá pra parar.

literal_meaning.en: 'straight eyes [assert], can't-stop-walking.' 立ち止まる = 'come to a halt'; potential neg 立ち止まれない = 'can't bring oneself to stop'.

literal_meaning.en: 'well not-going (ず), wall of in-front at come-to-be-unable-to-move.' うまくいく = 'go well'; negative 〜ず = literary form.

translations.en: — unable to do anything, biting my lip, a downcast gaze —

translations.pt-BR: — sem conseguir fazer nada, mordendo o lábio, com o olhar no chão —

literal_meaning.en: 'anything not-able-to-do, lip biting, hanging-head gaze at.' 唇を噛む = idiom 'bite one's lip in frustration'.

translations.en: — a flower blooming on the road paints the seven colors strongly,

literal_meaning.en: 'road on bloomed flower [subj] strongly seven-colors [obj] painting.' 七色 = 'seven hues', the traditional count of rainbow colors in Japanese.

translations.es: — y seguramente coloreará el camino que recorro.

literal_meaning.en: 'going road [obj] color-does-for-me [nom] probably.' 〜てくれる = 'does it for my benefit'.

translations.es: El tiempo sigue fluyendo sin detenerse nunca.

literal_meaning.en: 'time [topic] stop thing without, keep-flowing is-[emph].' 〜ことなく = 'without (ever)'.

translations.en: Move forward — on those feet of yours.
translations.es: Avanza — con esos pies tuyos.

literal_meaning.en: 'forward to let's-advance, those feet with.' 進もう is the volitional of 進む.

literal_meaning.en: 'start-running, than-anyone-more, that ahead toward.' 誰よりも = 'more than anyone'.

literal_meaning.en: 'chasing, eyes in reflected everything now.' 目に映る = 'be reflected in one's eyes = to come into view'.

grammar_points.name: Imperative form (blunt command: 〜え / 〜ろ)

explanation.en:
The blunt imperative — godan verbs drop 〜u and add 〜e (走る → 走れ, 走り出す → 走り出せ); ichidan verbs drop 〜る and add 〜ろ (食べる → 食べろ). Used for punch in songs; in real life it's quite rough.

From this song: 走り出せ = 'Start running!'; 伸ばせ = 'Reach out!'.

More examples:
• 見ろ (look!)
• 待て (wait!)
• 信じろ (believe!)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 走り出す → 走り出せ; 伸ばす → 伸ばせ

explanation.en:
Literary/archaic negative. Attaches to a verb's negative stem, equivalent to 〜ないで. Common in songs and formal writing.

From this song:
• うまくいかず = 'without going well'
• 何も出来ず = 'unable to do anything'

More examples:
• 知らず = 'without knowing'
• 思わず = 'involuntarily'
• 休まず = 'without resting'

grammar_points.name: Potential verbs (〜eる / 〜られる: can do)

explanation.en:
Godan verbs: change 〜u to 〜eru (行く → 行ける). Ichidan verbs: 〜る → 〜られる (食べる → 食べられる). Means 'can / able to (do)'.

From this song:
• 見つけられない (can't find)
• 越えてゆける (can get across)
• 立ち止まれない (can't stop)
• つかめる (can grasp)

More examples:
• 話せる (can speak)
• 泳げる (can swim)
• 食べられる (can eat)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 行く → 行ける; 食べる → 食べられる

grammar_points.name: 〜ば / 〜なければ (ba / nakereba: if / if not)

explanation.en:
Conditional form — godan: change 〜u → 〜eba. Ichidan: 〜る → 〜れば. Negative: 〜ない → 〜なければ = 'if (you) don't'.

From this song:
• 心一つにすれば = 'if (we) make our hearts one'
• 逃げ出さなければ = 'if we don't run away'

More examples:
• 時間があれば (if I have time)
• 頑張れば (if you try hard)
• 行かなければ (if you don't go)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: する → すれば; 逃げ出す → 逃げ出さなければ

grammar_points.name: 〜のまま (no mama: as-is / in the state of)

explanation.en:
Attach to a noun (via の) or a plain form to express 'staying as X / in the state of X / without change'.

From this song: 想いのまま = 'as my feelings are / letting my heart lead'.

More examples:
• そのまま (as it is)
• 昔のまま (the same as before)
• 気持ちのままに動く (move as one's heart dictates)

grammar_points.name: 〜ことなく (koto naku: without ever / without X-ing)

explanation.en:
Attach 〜ことなく after a verb's dictionary form to mean 'without (ever) X-ing'. Slightly literary; emphasizes a continuous state.

From this song: 止まることなく流れ続けてる = 'keeps flowing without ever stopping'.

More examples:
• 疑うことなく信じる (believe without doubting)
• 諦めることなく続ける (continue without giving up)
• 振り返ることなく歩む (walk on without looking back)

grammar_points.name: 〜てくれる (te kureru: does X for me)

explanation.en:
Attach to a verb's te-form to express 'someone does X for my benefit'. Marks directionality of the favor (inward, to the speaker).

From this song: 彩ってくれる = '(something/someone) colors (my path) for me'.

More examples:
• 教えてくれる (teach me)
• 助けてくれる (help me)
• 聞いてくれてありがとう (thank you for listening (for my sake))

grammar_points.name: 〜ならば (naraba: if)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add ならば (naraba) after a noun or clause to express a formal or literary conditional — 'if it is X' or 'if that's the case'. It's the formal version of なら (nara).

Example from this song: 太陽ならば (taiyou naraba) = 'if it were the sun / if I were the sun' — from 太陽 (taiyou, 'sun') + ならば (naraba, 'if')

More examples:
• 君 (kimi, 'you') → 君ならば (kimi naraba, 'if it's you')
• 本当 (hontou, 'true') → 本当ならば (hontou naraba, 'if it's true')
• 愛 (ai, 'love') → 愛ならば (ai naraba, 'if it is love')

Note: Formality: ならば (most formal) > なら (standard) > だったら (most casual). ならば is common in songs, poetry, and dramatic speech. It sets up profound hypothetical scenarios.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 太陽 (taiyou, 'sun') + ならば (naraba, 'if') → 太陽ならば (taiyou naraba, 'if it were the sun')

grammar_points.name: 〜てきた (te kita: have been doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add てきた (te kita) after the te-form of a verb to express an action that has continued from the past up to now — 'have been doing X all along'.

Example from this song: 受け止めてきた (uketomete kita) = 'have been accepting/catching' — from 受け止める (uketomeru, 'to accept/catch') → 受け止めて (uketomete, te-form) + きた (kita, 'came'). Also: 抱えてきた (kakaete kita) = 'have been carrying/holding'

More examples:
• 戦う (tatakau, 'to fight') → 戦ってきた (tatakatte kita, 'have been fighting')
• 耐える (taeru, 'to endure') → 耐えてきた (taete kita, 'have been enduring')
• 愛する (ai suru, 'to love') → 愛してきた (ai shite kita, 'have been loving')

Note: てきた is deeply emotional in songs — it acknowledges accumulated experience and effort. 'All this time, through everything, I have been...' The song uses it twice, showing a pattern of enduring love.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 受け止める (uketomeru, 'to accept') → 受け止めて (uketomete, te-form) + きた (kita, 'came') → 受け止めてきた (uketomete kita, 'have been accepting')

grammar_points.name: 〜たら (tara: if; when)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add たら (tara) to the past form of a verb for a conditional — 'if/when X happens'. This song also uses the related form たなら (ta nara) for a more literary feel.

Example from this song: 感じられたら (kanjiraretara) = 'if I could feel' — from 感じられる (kanjirareru, potential of 感じる, 'to feel') → 感じられたら (kanjiraretara). Also: 癒せたなら (iyaseta nara) = 'if I could heal'

More examples:
• できる (dekiru, 'can do') → できたら (dekitara, 'if I could')
• 会える (aeru, 'can meet') → 会えたら (aetara, 'if we could meet')
• 届く (todoku, 'to reach') → 届いたら (todoitara, 'if/when it reaches')

Note: たら with potential verbs creates deeply wishful expressions: 'if only I could...' たなら is a more literary variant with the same meaning, perfect for song lyrics.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 感じられる (kanjirareru, 'can feel') → 感じられたら (kanjiraretara, 'if I could feel') / 癒せる (iyaseru, 'can heal') → 癒せたなら (iyaseta nara, 'if I could heal')

grammar_points.name: 〜さえ (sae: even)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add さえ (sae) after a noun or verb to mean 'even X' — emphasizing that the stated minimum is extreme or significant.

Example from this song: 泣くことさえ出来なかった (naku koto sae dekinakatta) = 'couldn't even cry' — from 泣く (naku, 'to cry') + こと (koto, nominalizer) + さえ (sae, 'even') + 出来なかった (dekinakatta, 'couldn't')

More examples:
• 名前 (namae, 'name') → 名前さえ知らない (namae sae shiranai, 'don't even know the name')
• 立つ (tatsu, 'to stand') → 立つことさえ (tatsu koto sae, 'even standing')
• 一言 (hitokoto, 'one word') → 一言さえ (hitokoto sae, 'even one word')

Note: さえ...ない expresses 'can't even do the minimum'. さえ...ば means 'as long as': 君さえいれば (kimi sae ireba, 'as long as you're here'). Context determines which meaning.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 泣く (naku, 'to cry') + こと (koto) + さえ (sae, 'even') + 出来なかった (dekinakatta, 'couldn't') → 泣くことさえ出来なかった (naku koto sae dekinakatta, 'couldn't even cry')

grammar_points.name: 〜てくれる (te kureru: to do for me)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add てくれる (te kureru) after the te-form of a verb to express that someone did something for the speaker's benefit — carrying gratitude and warmth.

Example from this song: 笑いかけてくれた (waraikakete kureta) = 'smiled at me (and I'm grateful)' — from 笑いかける (waraikakeru, 'to smile at') → 笑いかけて (waraikakete, te-form) + くれた (kureta, past of kureru, 'did for me')

More examples:
• 助ける (tasukeru, 'to help') → 助けてくれた (tasukete kureta, 'helped me')
• 来る (kuru, 'to come') → 来てくれた (kite kureta, 'came for me')
• 信じる (shinjiru, 'to believe') → 信じてくれた (shinjite kureta, 'believed in me')

Note: てくれる is one of the most emotionally significant patterns in Japanese. It transforms a neutral action into a gift — the person did something that benefited you, and you appreciate it. Essential for expressing gratitude in natural Japanese.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 笑いかける (waraikakeru, 'to smile at') → 笑いかけて (waraikakete, te-form) + くれた (kureta, 'did for me') → 笑いかけてくれた (waraikakete kureta, 'smiled at me')

grammar_points.name: 〜ではなくて (de wa nakute: not X, but)

explanation.en:
How it works: Use noun + ではなくて (de wa nakute) or the casual じゃなくて (ja nakute) to negate one thing and introduce another — 'not X, but rather Y'.

Example from this song: 景色じゃなくて (keshiki ja nakute) = 'not the scenery, but...' — from 景色 (keshiki, 'scenery') + じゃなくて (ja nakute, 'not, but') → followed by 眩しさを (mabushisa wo, 'the brightness')

More examples:
• 嘘 (uso, 'lie') → 嘘じゃなくて本当 (uso ja nakute hontou, 'not a lie, but the truth')
• お金 (okane, 'money') → お金じゃなくて時間 (okane ja nakute jikan, 'not money, but time')
• 悲しい (kanashii, 'sad') → 悲しいんじゃなくて寂しい (kanashii n ja nakute sabishii, 'not sad, but lonely')

Note: じゃなくて is casual; ではなくて is formal. This pattern clarifies what you really mean — correcting a possible misunderstanding. Very useful in daily conversation.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 景色 (keshiki, 'scenery') + じゃなくて (ja nakute, 'not, but') → 景色じゃなくて (keshiki ja nakute, 'not the scenery, but...') + 眩しさを (mabushisa wo, 'the brightness')

explanation.en: Attaches to a verb's -e- stem to mean 'if/when X.' Used for hypotheticals, natural consequences, and reflective statements: 思い出せば 'when I think back'.
explanation.es: Se adjunta a la raíz -e- del verbo para significar 'si/cuando X'. Usada para hipótesis, consecuencias naturales y reflexiones: 思い出せば 'cuando recuerdo'.
explanation.pt-BR: Anexa-se ao radical -e- do verbo para significar 'se/quando X'. Usada para hipóteses, consequências naturais e reflexões: 思い出せば 'quando me lembro'.

explanation.en: 〜ていた describes an ongoing past state or action. In casual speech and lyrics it contracts to 〜てた: 輝いてた = 'was shining', 眠っていた = 'was sleeping'.
explanation.es: 〜ていた describe un estado o acción continuos en el pasado. En el habla casual y las letras se contrae a 〜てた: 輝いてた = 'estaba brillando', 眠っていた = 'estábamos durmiendo'.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜ていた descreve um estado ou ação contínuos no passado. Na fala casual e em letras contrai-se para 〜てた: 輝いてた = 'estava brilhando', 眠っていた = 'estávamos dormindo'.

grammar_points.name: 〜たい / 〜たくなる (desire and emerging desire)

explanation.en: 〜たい (attached to verb stem) means 'want to'. 〜たくなる ('come to want to') describes a desire that arises naturally over time: 疑いたくなる 'I start wanting to doubt'. With 〜ていたい you keep wanting an ongoing state — 見ていたい 'want to keep watching'.
explanation.es: 〜たい (a la raíz verbal) significa 'querer'. 〜たくなる ('llegar a querer') describe un deseo que surge con el tiempo: 疑いたくなる 'empiezo a querer dudar'. Con 〜ていたい uno quiere continuar un estado: 見ていたい 'quiero seguir mirando'.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜たい (anexado ao radical do verbo) significa 'querer'. 〜たくなる ('vir a querer') descreve um desejo que surge naturalmente: 疑いたくなる 'começo a querer duvidar'. Com 〜ていたい você quer continuar um estado: 見ていたい 'quero continuar olhando'.

explanation.en: Plain form + そうだ means 'I hear that...' / 'they say...' — reporting information from someone else. Distinct from the look-like 〜そう that attaches to verb/adjective stems.
explanation.es: Forma simple + そうだ significa 'he oído que...' / 'dicen que...' — informando algo que se ha oído. Distinto del 〜そう de apariencia que se adjunta a la raíz.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma simples + そうだ significa 'ouvi dizer que...' / 'dizem que...' — relatando informação de outra pessoa. Diferente do 〜そう de aparência que se anexa ao radical.

explanation.en: An archaic equivalent of 〜ない still found in poetry, set phrases, and song lyrics for solemn or formal weight: 会えぬ人 'a person I cannot meet', 行かぬ 'does not go'. Attaches like 〜ない (to verb a-stem; する → せぬ; くる → こぬ).
explanation.es: Un equivalente arcaico de 〜ない aún presente en poesía, frases hechas y letras de canciones, con tono solemne: 会えぬ人 'persona a la que no puedo encontrar'. Se adjunta como 〜ない (raíz -a; する → せぬ; くる → こぬ).
explanation.pt-BR: Um equivalente arcaico de 〜ない ainda usado em poesia, expressões fixas e letras de música para dar peso solene: 会えぬ人 'pessoa que não posso encontrar'. Anexa-se como 〜ない (radical -a; する → せぬ; くる → こぬ).

explanation.en: Plain verb/adjective + の at the end of a sentence gives a soft, often feminine, intimate explanation or assertion. Common in introspective lyrics: 忘れられなかったの 'I was never able to forget'. Distinct from explanatory んだ, which is more neutral.
explanation.es: Forma simple + の al final da una afirmación suave e íntima, con frecuencia femenina. Común en letras introspectivas: 忘れられなかったの 'nunca pude olvidar'. Diferente de んだ explicativo, que es más neutro.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma simples + の no final da frase dá uma asserção suave e íntima, frequentemente feminina. Comum em letras introspectivas: 忘れられなかったの 'nunca consegui esquecer'. Diferente de んだ explicativo, que é mais neutro.

grammar_points.name: 〜くらいなら (kurai nara: rather than)

explanation.en:
How it works: くらいなら (kurai nara) means 'rather than (doing X)' — it expresses that the speaker would prefer an extreme alternative over the stated option.

Example from this song: 殺られるくらいなら (yarareru kurai nara) = 'rather than being killed/beaten' — from 殺られる (yarareru, 'to be done in/killed', passive) + くらいなら

More examples:
• 負けるくらいなら死んだ方がいい (makeru kurai nara shinda hou ga ii, 'I'd rather die than lose')
• 嘘をつくくらいなら黙る (uso o tsuku kurai nara damaru, 'rather than lie, I'll stay quiet')
• 待つくらいなら自分でやる (matsu kurai nara jibun de yaru, 'rather than wait, I'll do it myself')

Note: くらいなら literally means 'if it's to the extent of...' — the speaker finds the stated action so unacceptable that they'd prefer an alternative. It's dramatic and emphatic.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 殺られる (yarareru, 'to be beaten') + くらいなら (kurai nara, 'rather than') → 殺られるくらいなら (yarareru kurai nara, 'rather than be beaten')

grammar_points.name: 〜すぎる (sugiru: too much)

explanation.en:
How it works: すぎる (sugiru, 'to exceed') attaches to verb stems or adjective stems to express 'too much.' For verbs: masu-stem + すぎる. For i-adjectives: drop い + すぎる.

Example from this song: 若すぎる (wakasugiru) = 'too young' — from 若い (wakai, 'young') → 若 (waka) + すぎる (sugiru)

More examples:
• 食べすぎる (tabesugiru, 'to eat too much') — from 食べる (taberu, 'to eat')
• 高すぎる (takasugiru, 'too expensive') — from 高い (takai, 'expensive')
• 静かすぎる (shizuka sugiru, 'too quiet') — na-adjective + すぎる

Note: すぎる conjugates as an ichidan verb: すぎた (sugita, past), すぎない (suginai, negative). This is one of the most frequently used grammar patterns — 暑すぎる！(atsusugiru, 'it's too hot!').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 若い (wakai, 'young') → 若 (waka, drop い) + すぎる (sugiru, 'too much') → 若すぎる (wakasugiru, 'too young')

grammar_points.name: 〜なよ (na yo: don't do!)

explanation.en:
How it works: な (na) after a verb's dictionary form is a casual negative command: 'don't do X!' Adding よ (yo) makes it slightly softer or more emphatic depending on tone.

Example from this song: 隠すなよ (kakusu na yo) = 'don't hide it!' — from 隠す (kakusu, 'to hide') + な (na, 'don't') + よ (yo)

More examples:
• 泣くな (naku na, 'don't cry!') — from 泣く (naku, 'to cry')
• 心配するなよ (shinpai suru na yo, 'don't worry!') — from 心配する (shinpai suru, 'to worry')
• 諦めるな (akirameru na, 'don't give up!') — from 諦める (akirameru, 'to give up')

Note: Dictionary form + な is the rough masculine prohibition form. It's very common in anime and songs. Don't confuse with the な that makes na-adjectives (静かな = quiet).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 隠す (kakusu, 'to hide') + な (na, 'don't') + よ (yo, emphasis) → 隠すなよ (kakusu na yo, 'don't hide it!')

grammar_points.name: 〜にだって (ni datte: even by)

explanation.en:
How it works: にだって (ni datte) combines に (ni, 'by') with だって (datte, 'even'). It emphasizes that even the stated agent or means can or can't do something.

Example from this song: テロリストにだって消せない (terorisuto ni datte kesenai) = 'even a terrorist can't erase it' — emphasizing that not even the most extreme agent can destroy it

More examples:
• 誰にだって秘密がある (dare ni datte himitsu ga aru, 'even anyone has secrets / everyone has secrets')
• 子供にだってわかる (kodomo ni datte wakaru, 'even a child can understand')
• 親にだって言えない (oya ni datte ienai, 'can't tell even my parents')

Note: だって adds the nuance of 'even.' It's more emphatic than でも. にだって specifically emphasizes 'even by (this agent).' It's a punk/rebellious way to make a strong point.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: テロリスト (terorisuto, 'terrorist') + に (ni, 'by') + だって (datte, 'even') → テロリストにだって (terorisuto ni datte, 'even by a terrorist') + 消せない (kesenai, 'can't erase')

grammar_points.name: 〜てくれ (te kure: do it for me! / please do)

explanation.en:
How it works: くれ (kure) is the imperative of くれる (kureru, 'to do for me'). Attach it to a verb's te-form for a rough/casual request: 'do this for me!'

Example from this song: 聞いてくれ (kiite kure) = 'listen to me!' — from 聞く (kiku, 'to listen') → 聞いて (kiite) + くれ (kure)

More examples:
• 見てくれ (mite kure, 'look at this!') — from 見る (miru, 'to see')
• 信じてくれ (shinjite kure, 'believe me!') — from 信じる (shinjiru, 'to believe')
• 待ってくれ (matte kure, 'wait for me!') — from 待つ (matsu, 'to wait')

Note: てくれ is more direct/rough than てください. It's masculine and common in punk, rock, and emotional contexts. Adding よ softens it slightly: 聞いてくれよ (kiite kure yo).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 聞く (kiku, 'to listen') → 聞いて (kiite) → 聞いてくれ (kiite kure, 'listen to me!')

grammar_points.name: 〜じまう (jimau: end up doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: じまう (jimau) is the rough casual contraction of でしまう (de shimau). It expresses unintended or regrettable completion. Used after verbs whose te-form ends in で.

Example from this song: 死んじまう (shinjimau) = 'end up dying' — from 死ぬ (shinu, 'to die') → 死んで (shinde) + しまう (shimau) → contracted: 死んじまう (shinjimau)

More examples:
• 飲んじまった (nonjimatta, 'ended up drinking it') — from 飲む (nomu, 'to drink')
• 壊れちまう (kowarechimau, 'gonna end up breaking') — from 壊れる (kowareru, 'to break')
• やっちまった (yacchimatta, 'I messed up / did it') — from やる (yaru, 'to do')

Note: The contraction pattern: てしまう → ちまう/ちゃう, でしまう → じまう/じゃう. じまう is rougher and more masculine than じゃう. Very common in punk/rock lyrics.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 死ぬ (shinu, 'to die') → 死んで (shinde) + しまう (shimau) → 死んじまう (shinjimau, 'end up dying')

cultural_context.en: もがく = 'to struggle, thrash about' — like a fish out of water. Pairs naturally with 苦しむ ('suffer'), 焦る ('be panicked'), 暴れる ('thrash'). Stronger than 頑張る.

grammar_points.name: Verb stem + あう (do mutually / each other)

explanation.en: Adding 合う (あう) to a verb stem creates a reciprocal verb meaning 'do X to each other'. 響きあう ('echo each other'), 叩きあう ('slap each other'), 助けあう ('help each other'), 分かりあう ('understand each other'). Productive — works on most action verbs.
explanation.es: Añadir 合う (あう) a la raíz verbal crea un verbo recíproco 'hacerse X mutuamente'. 響きあう, 叩きあう, 助けあう, 分かりあう. Patrón productivo — funciona con la mayoría de verbos de acción.
explanation.pt-BR: Acrescentar 合う (あう) à raiz verbal cria um verbo recíproco 'fazer X um ao outro'. 響きあう, 叩きあう, 助けあう, 分かりあう. Padrão produtivo — funciona com a maioria dos verbos de ação.

grammar_points.name: Casual emphatic 〜くって / 〜って (= 〜くて / 〜て)

explanation.en: Casual speech doubles the consonant in te-form for emphasis: 立ちたくて → 立ちたくって ('really wanting to stand'); なりたくて → なりたくって. Adds a slightly exaggerated, emotional feel — common in shouted lyrics and rough speech.
explanation.es: El habla casual duplica la consonante de la forma -te para enfatizar: 立ちたくて → 立ちたくって; なりたくて → なりたくって. Aporta un matiz exagerado, frecuente en letras gritadas y habla brusca.
explanation.pt-BR: A fala casual duplica a consoante na forma -te para dar ênfase: 立ちたくて → 立ちたくって; なりたくて → なりたくって. Acrescenta tom levemente exagerado, comum em letras gritadas e fala rude.

explanation.en: ぶっ comes from ぶつ ('to hit') and acts as an emphatic prefix on action verbs: ぶっ飛ぶ ('to be blown away / fly off'), ぶっ壊す ('to smash to bits'), ぶっちぎり ('absolute lead'), ぶっつける ('to smack into'). Adds a 'forcefully / wildly' flavor.
explanation.es: ぶっ procede de ぶつ ('golpear') y actúa como prefijo enfático en verbos de acción: ぶっ飛ぶ ('salir volando'), ぶっ壊す ('destrozar'), ぶっちぎり ('liderazgo arrasador'). Aporta tono 'con fuerza / a lo loco'.
explanation.pt-BR: ぶっ vem de ぶつ ('bater') e funciona como prefixo enfático em verbos de ação: ぶっ飛ぶ ('voar pelos ares'), ぶっ壊す ('destruir'), ぶっちぎり ('liderança esmagadora'). Dá tom 'com força / sem freios'.

grammar_points.name: Causative + くれ ('let me / permit me')

explanation.en: Verb-causative + くれ asks 'please let me do X'. 走らせてくれ ('let me run'); 行かせてくれ ('let me go'); 言わせてくれ ('let me speak'). The combination of causative ('make me / let me') + くれる ('do for me') creates a request to be permitted action.
explanation.es: Verbo-causativo + くれ pide 'déjame hacer X'. 走らせてくれ, 行かせてくれ, 言わせてくれ. La combinación causativo + くれる ('hacer por mí') crea una petición de permiso.
explanation.pt-BR: Verbo-causativo + くれ pede 'deixe-me fazer X'. 走らせてくれ, 行かせてくれ, 言わせてくれ. A combinação causativo + くれる ('fazer por mim') gera um pedido de permissão.

grammar_points.name: Casual contraction 〜てんだ (= 〜ているんだ)

explanation.en: Spoken Japanese drops syllables: 〜ているんだ → 〜てるんだ → 〜てんだ. 始まってんだ = 始まっているんだ ('the thing is, it has started'). Adds explanatory tone (んだ) to a progressive (〜ている). Heavily masculine in flavor.
explanation.es: El japonés hablado omite sílabas: 〜ているんだ → 〜てるんだ → 〜てんだ. 始まってんだ = 始まっているんだ ('lo que pasa es que ya empezó'). Tono explicativo (んだ) sobre un progresivo. Sabor masculino marcado.
explanation.pt-BR: O japonês falado omite sílabas: 〜ているんだ → 〜てるんだ → 〜てんだ. 始まってんだ = 始まっているんだ ('é que já começou'). Tom explicativo (んだ) num progressivo (〜ている). Forte sabor masculino.

grammar_points.name: ら抜き (ra-dropped potential): 信じれる, 食べれる, 見れる

explanation.en: Strict potential of ichidan verbs adds 〜られる: 信じる → 信じられる ('can believe'). In casual speech the ら is often dropped: 信じれる, 食べれる, 見れる. Considered grammatically incorrect by purists but extremely widespread, especially among younger speakers.
explanation.es: El potencial estricto de los verbos ichidan añade 〜られる: 信じる → 信じられる. En el habla informal se suele omitir el ら: 信じれる, 食べれる, 見れる. Técnicamente incorrecto, pero generalizado, sobre todo entre jóvenes.
explanation.pt-BR: O potencial estrito de verbos ichidan adiciona 〜られる: 信じる → 信じられる. Na fala casual, o ら costuma ser omitido: 信じれる, 食べれる, 見れる. Tecnicamente incorreto, mas muito difundido na fala jovem.

grammar_points.name: Emphatic は in negative: 〜たくはない

explanation.en: Inserting は into a negative form adds emphasis/contrast: 終わりたくない ('I don't want it to end') → 終わりたくはない ('I really don't want it — least of all — to end like this'). The は singles out the final element as the un-wanted thing.
explanation.es: Insertar は en una forma negativa añade énfasis/contraste: 終わりたくない → 終わりたくはない ('precisamente no quiero que acabe así'). は singulariza el elemento como lo NO deseado.
explanation.pt-BR: Inserir は numa forma negativa enfatiza/contrasta: 終わりたくない → 終わりたくはない ('especificamente não quero acabar assim'). は destaca o elemento como aquilo que NÃO se quer.

grammar_points.name: 〜ならきっと (nara kitto: if... then surely)

explanation.en:
How it works: Combine the conditional なら (nara, 'if') with the adverb きっと (kitto, 'surely') to express confident prediction: 'if X, then surely Y.'

Example from this song: 世界ならきっと (sekai nara kitto) = 'if it's this world, then surely...' — expressing confidence that this particular world can achieve something

More examples:
• 君ならきっとできる (kimi nara kitto dekiru, 'if it's you, you can surely do it') — encouragement
• 明日ならきっと会える (ashita nara kitto aeru, 'if it's tomorrow, we can surely meet')
• 努力するならきっと報われる (doryoku suru nara kitto mukuwareru, 'if you work hard, you'll surely be rewarded')

Note: きっと adds confidence to any statement. Combined with なら, it creates a powerful expression of faith: 'given this condition, I'm certain of the result.' Very common in encouraging and motivational contexts.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 世界 (sekai, 'world') + なら (nara, 'if') + きっと (kitto, 'surely') → 世界ならきっと (sekai nara kitto, 'if it's this world, then surely')

grammar_points.name: 〜てゆく (te yuku: to go on doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: てゆく (te yuku) is the literary/poetic form of ていく (te iku), expressing an action that continues moving into the future. ゆく (yuku) is the classical form of 行く (iku).

Example from this song: 彩ってゆく (irodotte yuku) = 'continues to color (into the future)' — from 彩る (irodoru, 'to color') → 彩って (irodotte) + ゆく (yuku)

More examples:
• 消えてゆく (kiete yuku, 'fading away') — from 消える (kieru, 'to disappear')
• 変わってゆく (kawatte yuku, 'gradually changing') — from 変わる (kawaru, 'to change')
• 歩いてゆく (aruite yuku, 'walking onward') — from 歩く (aruku, 'to walk')

Note: てゆく and ていく mean the same thing, but てゆく has a more poetic, emotional, or literary feel. Songs and literature strongly prefer ゆく over いく for its elegance.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 彩る (irodoru, 'to color') → 彩って (irodotte) + ゆく (yuku, 'to go on') → 彩ってゆく (irodotte yuku, 'goes on coloring')

grammar_points.name: 〜ば (ba: if; when)

explanation.en:
How it works: The ば (ba) conditional means 'if' or 'when.' For godan verbs, change the final -u to -e and add ば. For ichidan verbs, drop る and add れば.

Example from this song: 合えば (aeba) = 'if we come together' — from 合う (au, 'to match/come together') → 合え (ae) + ば (ba)

More examples:
• 行けば (ikeba, 'if you go') — from 行く (iku, 'to go')
• 見れば (mireba, 'if you see') — from 見る (miru, 'to see')
• 良ければ (yokereba, 'if it's good / if you don't mind') — from 良い (yoi, 'good')

Note: ば implies a natural consequence: 'if A, then B naturally follows.' 合う → 合えば follows the standard godan pattern: u → e + ば.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 合う (au, 'to come together') → 合えば (aeba, 'if we come together')

grammar_points.name: 〜ず (zu: without doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: ず (zu) is the classical negative form meaning 'without doing.' It replaces ない in literary or formal contexts. For most verbs, change the ない-form's ない to ず.

Example from this song: 変わらず (kawarazu) = 'without changing / unchangingly' — from 変わる (kawaru, 'to change') → 変わらない (kawaranai) → 変わらず (kawarazu)

More examples:
• 言わず (iwazu, 'without saying') — from 言う (iu, 'to say')
• 食べず (tabezu, 'without eating') — from 食べる (taberu, 'to eat')
• 諦めず (akiramezu, 'without giving up') — from 諦める (akirameru, 'to give up')

Note: ず is the literary equivalent of ないで or なくて. Exception: する → せず (sezu), not しず. ず can be followed by に to connect: 食べずに寝た (tabezu ni neta, 'slept without eating').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 変わる (kawaru, 'to change') → 変わらない (kawaranai, 'doesn't change') → 変わらず (kawarazu, 'without changing')

grammar_points.name: 〜てくれる (te kureru: to do for me)

explanation.en:
How it works: Attach くれる (kureru) to a verb's te-form to express that someone does something for the speaker's benefit. It conveys gratitude.

Example from this song: 君がくれたもの (kimi ga kureta mono) = 'the things you gave me' — from くれる (kureru, 'to give to me') → くれた (kureta, past) + もの (mono, 'things')

More examples:
• 笑ってくれた (waratte kureta, 'smiled for me') — from 笑う (warau, 'to smile')
• 来てくれてうれしい (kite kurete ureshii, 'happy that you came for me')
• 待っていてくれた (matte ite kureta, 'was waiting for me') — from 待つ (matsu, 'to wait')

Note: くれる is essential in Japanese — it marks that an action benefited the speaker. Without it, the sentence is neutral. With it, there's warmth and gratitude. Very common in love songs.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 君 (kimi, 'you') + が (ga) + くれた (kureta, 'gave me') + もの (mono, 'things') → 君がくれたもの (kimi ga kureta mono, 'the things you gave me')

explanation.en: わ at the end of a sentence is a softening, lightly feminine particle: なかったわ ('it wasn't'), 要らないわ ('I don't need it'). Common in older women's speech, female narrators, and elegant writing. Modern young women rarely use it in actual conversation.
explanation.es: わ al final de frase es una partícula suavizadora, ligeramente femenina: なかったわ, 要らないわ. Habitual en habla de mujeres mayores, narradoras femeninas, prosa elegante. Las jóvenes apenas la usan hoy.
explanation.pt-BR: わ no fim de frase é uma partícula suavizadora, levemente feminina: なかったわ, 要らないわ. Comum na fala de mulheres mais velhas, narradoras femininas, prosa elegante. Mulheres jovens hoje raramente usam.

grammar_points.name: Verb stem + たい / たくない / たくても (want to / don't want to / even if I want)

explanation.en: Verb stem + たい (want), たくない (don't want), たくても (even if I want). Conjugates like an い-adjective: 忘れたい → 忘れたくない → 忘れたくても → 忘れたくなかった. Only for the speaker's own desires.
explanation.es: Raíz verbal + たい (querer), たくない (no querer), たくても (aunque quiera). Se conjuga como adjetivo い: 忘れたい → 忘れたくない → 忘れたくても → 忘れたくなかった. Solo para los deseos propios.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz verbal + たい (querer), たくない (não querer), たくても (mesmo querendo). Conjuga como adjetivo い: 忘れたい → 忘れたくない → 忘れたくても → 忘れたくなかった. Só para desejos do próprio falante.

grammar_points.name: Verb stem + ふり(を)する (pretend to)

explanation.en: ふり means 'a pretense / an act'. Verb-dictionary or adjective + ふりをする ('pretend to'): 知らないふり ('pretend not to know'), 寝たふり ('pretend to be asleep'), 寂しくないふり ('pretend not to be lonely'). The を often drops in casual speech.
explanation.es: ふり significa 'fingimiento'. Verbo en diccionario o adjetivo + ふりをする ('fingir que'): 知らないふり, 寝たふり, 寂しくないふり. El を suele caerse en habla casual.
explanation.pt-BR: ふり significa 'fingimento'. Verbo no dicionário ou adjetivo + ふりをする ('fingir que'): 知らないふり, 寝たふり, 寂しくないふり. O を costuma cair na fala casual.

grammar_points.name: Potential negative 〜られない (can't / unable to)

explanation.en: Adding 〜られる to a verb stem creates the potential ('can do X'). Negate with 〜られない ('can't do X'): 忘れられない ('can't forget'), 止められない ('can't stop'). Common to drop the ら in casual speech ('ら抜き'): 忘れれない. The full form is shown in standard writing.
explanation.es: Añadir 〜られる a la raíz verbal forma el potencial ('poder hacer X'). Negativo: 〜られない ('no poder'): 忘れられない, 止められない. En el habla casual se puede omitir ら ('ら抜き'): 忘れれない.
explanation.pt-BR: Adicionar 〜られる à raiz verbal cria o potencial ('conseguir fazer X'). Negativo: 〜られない ('não conseguir'): 忘れられない, 止められない. Pode-se omitir ら na fala casual ('ら抜き'): 忘れれない.

grammar_points.name: Verb-dictionary + ような (like / a kind of)

explanation.en: Verb-dictionary + ような turns a verb into a descriptor: 燃えるようなキス ('a kiss like burning / an inflammatory kiss'); 泣きそうな顔 ('a face like about to cry'); 飛ぶような速さ ('flying-fast'). Adverbial form is ように.
explanation.es: Verbo en diccionario + ような convierte un verbo en descriptor: 燃えるようなキス, 泣きそうな顔, 飛ぶような速さ. La forma adverbial es ように.
explanation.pt-BR: Verbo no dicionário + ような transforma um verbo em descritor: 燃えるようなキス, 泣きそうな顔, 飛ぶような速さ. A forma adverbial é ように.

grammar_points.name: Layered conditional: 〜たくても 〜られないほど

explanation.en: Stacked: 〜たい (want) + 〜ても (even if) + potential negative + ほど (to the extent). 忘れたくても 忘れられないほど = 'so [intense] that even if I want to forget, I can't'. Three N3 grammar points working together to express devastating intensity.
explanation.es: Apilamiento: 〜たい (querer) + 〜ても (aunque) + potencial negativo + ほど (hasta el punto de). 忘れたくても 忘れられないほど = 'tan intenso que, aunque quiera olvidar, no puedo'. Tres puntos N3 juntos.
explanation.pt-BR: Empilhamento: 〜たい (querer) + 〜ても (mesmo que) + potencial negativo + ほど (a tal ponto). 忘れたくても 忘れられないほど = 'tão intenso que, mesmo querendo esquecer, eu não consigo'. Três pontos N3 juntos.

explanation.en: 取る ('to take') forms many fixed idioms with body/age nouns: 年を取る ('to age', literally 'take on years'), 連絡を取る ('to make contact'), 手を取る ('to take hold of someone's hand'), 距離を取る ('to keep distance'). The verb 取る itself is concrete; the meaning is set by the noun.
explanation.es: 取る ('tomar') forma muchas expresiones fijas con sustantivos: 年を取る ('envejecer'), 連絡を取る ('ponerse en contacto'), 手を取る ('tomar la mano'), 距離を取る ('mantener distancia'). El verbo es concreto; el sustantivo fija el sentido.
explanation.pt-BR: 取る ('pegar') forma muitas expressões fixas com substantivos: 年を取る ('envelhecer'), 連絡を取る ('entrar em contato'), 手を取る ('pegar a mão'), 距離を取る ('manter distância'). O verbo é concreto; o substantivo define o sentido.

grammar_points.name: 〜なき (literary negation, 'without')

explanation.en:
How it works: なき (naki) is the classical/literary form of ない (nai, 'without/not'), used to modify nouns. It gives a poetic, timeless quality.

Example from this song: 終わりなき (owari naki) = 'endless / without end' — from 終わり (owari, 'end') + なき (naki, literary 'without')

More examples:
• 果てなき旅 (hate naki tabi, 'an endless journey') — from 果て (hate, 'end')
• 名もなき花 (na mo naki hana, 'a nameless flower') — from 名 (na, 'name')
• 限りなき愛 (kagiri naki ai, 'limitless love') — from 限り (kagiri, 'limit')

Note: なき is the literary equivalent of ない used as an adjective. Modern Japanese would say 終わりのない (owari no nai). なき appears in song titles, poetry, and formal writing for its elegance.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 終わり (owari, 'end') + なき (naki, literary 'without') → 終わりなき (owari naki, 'endless / without end')

grammar_points.name: 〜かけて (on the verge of)

explanation.en:
How it works: かける (kakeru) attached to a verb's masu-stem means 'about to,' 'on the verge of,' or 'half-done.' It expresses an incomplete or starting action.

Example from this song: 掴みかけて (tsukami kakete) = 'on the verge of grasping' — from 掴む (tsukamu, 'to grasp') → 掴み (tsukami, stem) + かけて (kakete)

More examples:
• 死にかける (shini kakeru, 'nearly die') — from 死ぬ (shinu, 'to die')
• 言いかけて止めた (ii kakete yameta, 'started to say but stopped') — from 言う (iu, 'to say')
• 食べかけのパン (tabe kake no pan, 'half-eaten bread') — from 食べる (taberu, 'to eat')

Note: 〜かけ as a noun modifier means 'half-done': 読みかけの本 (yomikake no hon, 'half-read book'). The て-form かけて connects to the next action: 'was on the verge of X, and then...'

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 掴む (tsukamu, 'to grasp') → 掴み (tsukami, stem) + かけて (kakete, 'on the verge of') → 掴みかけて (tsukami kakete, 'on the verge of grasping')

grammar_points.name: けして〜ない (never)

explanation.en:
How it works: けして (keshite) or 決して (keshite) combined with a negative verb means 'never' or 'by no means.' It creates an emphatic absolute negation.

Example from this song: The song uses けして...ない to express something that will absolutely never happen — an unbreakable resolve.

More examples:
• 決して忘れない (keshite wasurenai, 'I will never forget') — from 忘れる (wasureru, 'to forget')
• 決して諦めない (keshite akiramenai, 'I will never give up') — from 諦める (akirameru, 'to give up')
• 決して許さない (keshite yurusanai, 'I will never forgive') — from 許す (yurusu, 'to forgive')

Note: 決して must always pair with a negative form. Never use it with positive verbs. It's stronger than ぜんぜん〜ない (zenzen ~nai, 'not at all'). 決して expresses firm determination.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 決して (keshite, 'never') + verb negative form → 決して〜ない (keshite ~nai, 'absolutely never')

grammar_points.name: 〜ずに (without doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: ずに (zu ni) is the classical negative te-form meaning 'without doing.' Replace ない with ず and add に to connect to the next action.

Example from this song: 逸らさずに (sorasazu ni) = 'without averting (one's gaze)' — from 逸らす (sorasu, 'to avert') → 逸らさない (sorasanai) → 逸らさず (sorasazu) + に (ni)

More examples:
• 食べずに寝た (tabezu ni neta, 'slept without eating') — from 食べる (taberu, 'to eat')
• 迷わずに進む (mayowazu ni susumu, 'advance without hesitating') — from 迷う (mayou, 'to hesitate')
• 諦めずに頑張る (akiramezu ni ganbaru, 'keep trying without giving up')

Note: ずに = literary ないで. Exception: する → せずに (sezu ni), not しずに. ず can also stand alone without に in literary contexts: 言わず語らず (iwazu katarazu, 'without saying or telling').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 逸らす (sorasu, 'to avert') → 逸らさない (sorasanai) → 逸らさず (sorasazu) + に (ni) → 逸らさずに (sorasazu ni, 'without averting')

grammar_points.name: 〜ために (for the sake of)

explanation.en:
How it works: ために (tame ni) expresses purpose ('in order to') or benefit ('for the sake of'). After a verb dictionary form, it means 'in order to do.' After a noun + の, it means 'for the sake of.'

Example from this song: The song uses ために to express what the speaker is striving for — the purpose behind their actions.

More examples:
• 合格するために勉強する (goukaku suru tame ni benkyou suru, 'study in order to pass')
• 家族のために働く (kazoku no tame ni hataraku, 'work for the family')
• 健康のために走る (kenkou no tame ni hashiru, 'run for health')

Note: Verb + ために = 'in order to (do).' Noun + のために = 'for the sake of (noun).' Compare with ように, which is for non-volitional results.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb dictionary form + ために (tame ni, 'in order to') / noun + の + ために (no tame ni, 'for the sake of')

grammar_points.name: 〜ていく (continuing into the future)

explanation.en:
How it works: ていく (te iku) expresses an action or change continuing from now into the future. It shows forward progression through time.

Example from this song: 生きていく (ikite iku) = 'will go on living' — from 生きる (ikiru, 'to live') → 生きて (ikite) + いく (iku, 'to go')

More examples:
• 強くなっていく (tsuyoku natte iku, 'getting stronger and stronger')
• 変わっていく (kawatte iku, 'keeps changing over time') — from 変わる (kawaru, 'to change')
• 学んでいく (manande iku, 'will continue learning') — from 学ぶ (manabu, 'to learn')

Note: ていく shows future-directed change. てくる shows past-to-present change. 生きていく is a powerful expression meaning 'I will go on living' — often used to express determination in the face of difficulty.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 生きる (ikiru, 'to live') → 生きて (ikite) + いく (iku, 'to go') → 生きていく (ikite iku, 'will go on living')
